Traditional medicine and dietary phytochemicals (curcumin, sulforaphane, resveratrol, EGCG, berberine) can modulate Nrf2 while interacting with NF-κB, Wnt/β-catenin, and Notch pathways. This review synthesises mechanistic and translational evidence on Nrf2 modulation in CRC chemoprevention, stressing conventional medicine-derived agents in modern approaches. It moreover highlights difficulties, limitations, and future viewpoints for precision chemoprevention and personalised interventions.

articles.title: Hazard identification was the aim: reply to Zhao et al. on the exposure context of flavoured-air inhaler toxicity.
Structural context matters when interpreting clozapine AHR docking.
Pharmacological Targeting of Fc Receptor and FcRn Pathways: Therapeutic Antibody Engineering in Immune-Mediated Disorders.
articles.abstract: The Fc domain of therapeutic antibodies is a major pharmacological determinant of efficacy, safety, and disposition because it governs interactions with Fc receptors and the neonatal Fc receptor (FcRn). Advances in Fc engineering have enabled the rational modulation of antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity, antibody-dependent cellular phagocytosis, complement activation, and IgG recycling, thereby improving the pharmacodynamic and pharmacokinetic profiles of antibody-based biologics. In this review, we discuss the structural basis of Fc-mediated signaling and summarize how FcγR- and FcRn-directed engineering strategies are being applied across cancer, autoimmune disease, allergy, and selected chronic inflammatory conditions. Particular emphasis is placed on the pharmacological consequences of Fc glycoengineering, Fc silencing or enhancement, and FcRn antagonism, as well as on clinically advanced agents that illustrate these principles in practice. We also address translational challenges, including receptor polymorphism, tissue-specific response variability, immunogenicity, and developability. Overall, Fc engineering has emerged as a central pharmacological strategy for optimizing next-generation antibody therapeutics.

articles.title: Resolving the Dual Nature of NADPH Oxidase 4 in Cardiac Fibrosis for Selective Therapeutic Targeting: A Narrative Review.
articles.abstract: Cardiac fibrosis is a common route leading to heart failure and arrhythmia. However, there are no cardio-selective antifibrotic drugs currently approved. NADPH oxidase 4 (NOX4), which predominantly produces hydrogen peroxide and requires no cytosolic activator subunits, is regulated by expression, protein stability and post-translational modification. Its intracellular organelle localization makes it a potential redox-medicine target. Setanaxib, the first dual NOX1/NOX4 inhibitor under clinical development, is not NOX4-selective and remains unapproved. This narrative review of MEDLINE literature presents genetic, mechanistic, pharmacological and clinical evidence of associations between NOX4 and cardiac fibrosis in cardiomyocytes, fibroblasts, endothelial and immune cells, including effects of cardiovascular drugs. NOX4 can have pro-fibrotic effects through TGF-β1/Smad activation, regulated cardiomyocyte death, inflammatory signals and atrial/ventricular ion-channel remodelling. Yet, genetic studies report divergent findings reflective of context-dependent influences. NOX4 in the endoplasmic reticulum and mitochondria-associated membranes may promote autophagy and survival, whereas persistent high NOX4-derived ROS in stressed myocardium results in mitochondrial injury and fibrosis. Endothelial NOX4 seems mainly protective. Dual NOX1/NOX4 inhibition and preferential NOX4-targeting have been shown to have antifibrotic effects in pre-clinical cardiac models, although there is no clinical evidence. Divergences may be explained on four axes: ROS level, subcellular compartment, cell type and disease-state. A reasonable approach to translating NOX4-targeted pharmacology into cardiac antifibrotic therapy would be to adopt strategies that are specific to compartment and cell type.

articles.title: Advanced strategies for enhancing mRNA-lipid nanoparticles stability: molecular insights, stabilization techniques, and clinical applications.
articles.abstract: Advancements in mRNA formulation and delivery systems have transformed biomedical research, with the recent success of mRNA vaccines highlighting the technology's immense clinical potential. Despite their clinical success, the global reach of these vaccines is hindered by the necessity for ultracold storage, which restricts accessibility in resource-constrained regions. Improving the stability of mRNA-Lipid Nanoparticles (LNPs) at higher temperatures could be crucial for mass vaccination efforts in future outbreaks. This review evaluates the molecular assembly of mRNA-LNP systems, specifically how electrostatic complexation, hydrophobic interactions, and Van der Waals forces govern internal architectural organization and physicochemical integrity. This dual framework reveals how optimizing molecular coordination enhances the stability necessary for clinical viability. Beyond initial assembly, advanced stabilization technologies (e.g., lyophilization, spray-freeze drying (SFD), and thin-film freeze-drying) are evaluated for their ability to preserve LNP structural integrity during long-term storage. Incorporating these thermostable formulations into microneedle arrays and targeted pulmonary delivery platforms establishes non-invasive routes that enhance mucosal and transdermal bioavailability and clinical efficacy. Bridging nanoscale biophysics and macro-scale stability, this review connects electrostatic complexation, lipid architecture, and hydrophobic interactions to enhanced mRNA-LNP efficacy and extended shelf-life across biopharmaceutical applications.

articles.title: From ecosystem engineering to living computers: integrating dual-paradigm bacterial therapeutics for solid tumor microenvironment reprogramming.
articles.abstract: Recent advances in tumor microbiome biology and synthetic biology have made bacteria attractive therapeutic agents capable of reprogramming tumor-associated microbial ecosystems and serving as programmable living systems in solid tumors. In this review, we construct a dual-paradigm framework combining engineered bacterial therapeutics and ecosystem editing. In the first paradigm, phage-mediated targeting, competitive displacement, and metabolic reprogramming are used to alter tumor-associated microbial communities. In the second paradigm, engineered bacteria are equipped with environmental sensors, genetic logic circuits, and therapeutic payloads. We discuss the mechanistic interplay of these strategies in terms of ecological niche formation, bacterial colonization, immune and metabolic remodeling, and microbiome-host feedback. Clinical experience still varies across platforms due to differences in bacterial strain, attenuation, route of administration, tumor biology, treatment context, and patient characteristics. Major translational challenges include biocontainment, genetic stability, manufacturing and potency control, predictive biomarker validation, and product-specific regulatory requirements. We propose an additional hypothesis-generating framework for patient stratification and adaptive treatment monitoring. These concepts together provide a structured framework for exploring bacterial therapeutics as components of precision oncology, while highlighting the need for prospective clinical validation.

articles.title: Targeting coagulation factor XI/XIa for anticoagulation therapy: from mechanism to drug development.
articles.abstract: Coagulation Factor XI (FXI) and its activated form FXIa have been identified as important regulators of thrombin amplification, contributing substantially to pathological thrombosis while exerting a relatively limited role in physiological hemostasis, making it an attractive target for low-hemorrhagic antithrombotic therapy. In recent years, FXI/FXIa-targeted therapeutics have rapidly advanced in clinical trials and represent a promising strategy for precision anticoagulation. This review systematically summarizes the structural features, biological functions, and mechanistic roles of FXI/FXIa in thrombosis, followed by structure-guided drug design, major therapeutic modalities, and clinical translation. Clinical evidence is critically evaluated to highlight both the opportunities and limitations of FXI/FXIa-targeted therapies across different thrombotic indications. Furthermore, key challenges, including selectivity optimization, disease-dependent efficacy, and the physiological functions of FXI beyond coagulation, are discussed. A more comprehensive understanding of FXI biology will be essential for defining the long-term safety, therapeutic window and clinical positioning of FXI/FXIa-targeted anticoagulants.

articles.title: Thymoquinone exerts anti-inflammatory effects in multiple disease models by regulating immune-inflammatory homeostasis.
articles.abstract: Thymoquinone (TQ), an abundant phytochemical identified from Nigella sativa seeds of the Ranunculaceae family, is recognized for its multifaceted biological effects involving inflammatory regulation, oxidative stress control, and immune modulation. This review summarizes the anti-inflammatory effects of TQ across inflammation-related diseases and integrates bibliometric analysis, network pharmacology, and molecular docking approaches to explore its potential cross-disease immunoregulatory mechanisms. Accumulating evidence suggests that TQ may exert immunoregulatory effects through modulation of key inflammatory and antioxidant pathways, including nuclear factor-κB (NF-κB), mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK), Janus kinase/signal transducer and activator of transcription (JAK/STAT), the NLR family pyrin domain containing 3 (NLRP3) inflammasome, nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2/heme oxygenase-1 (Nrf2/HO-1), and peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma (PPARγ), accompanied by changes in pro-inflammatory mediator production, immune cell functions, and tissue responses in various inflammation-related disease models. Cross-disease mechanistic integrative network pharmacology analysis identified recurrent candidate nodes such as AKT1, TNF, and IL6 across different disease-related networks, suggesting that the broad-spectrum anti-inflammatory effects of TQ may involve coordinated modulation of partially shared immune-inflammatory networks, rather than targeting a single pathogenic pathway. Therefore, this review attempts to break away from the conventional summary model organized by individual diseases or single signaling pathways, and instead adopts the perspective of "immune-inflammatory homeostasis regulation" to comprehensively analyze the anti-inflammatory mechanisms of TQ across various diseases. This approach may facilitate a deeper understanding of its broad-spectrum immunomodulatory effects and potentially provide new theoretical insights for the translation of natural active products into precision immunotherapeutic strategies.

articles.title: HSP27, cell stress, and hormesis: From mammals to humanized yeast models.
articles.abstract: Hormesis is a biphasic dose-response phenomenon characterized by beneficial or stimulatory effects at low exposure levels to a stressor, followed by inhibitory or toxic effects at higher doses. This effect is related to the level of oxidative stress in the cell. Human HSPB1 (HSP27) is a small heat shock protein involved in the oxidative stress response, whose overexpression correlates with increased longevity in mammalian models. HSP27 protects neurons from damage caused by protein aggregation observed in neurodegenerative diseases; however, this same survival capability also favors tumor cells, hindering chemotherapeutic treatment. This review describes HSP27 and demonstrates that the humanized yeast model can aid in understanding the function of this protein, which protects neurons and enhances tumor survival. HSP27 exhibits a dose-dependent hormetic effect when expressed at varying levels in yeast. This expression-dependent response enhances longevity, proteasome activity, and resistance to thermal and oxidative stresses. The humanized yeast model may help elucidate the relationship between the quaternary structure of the protein and its hormetic effect. In addition, the humanization of partial or complete pathways involved in both neurodegenerative diseases and apoptosis may provide a way to identify small molecules that enhance neuronal protection and potentially inhibit HSP27's pro-survival function in cancer treatment.

articles.title: Comment on "Efficacy of traditional Chinese medicine in managing gastric atrophy and intestinal metaplasia in patients with chronic atrophic gastritis: A multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial".
Mechanistic insights into drug loading, host-guest interactions, and release in cyclodextrin-based metal-organic frameworks: a critical review.
articles.abstract: Cyclodextrin-based metal-organic frameworks (CD-MOFs) combine molecular host cavities with framework-generated porosity, but their rational use in drug delivery requires clearer links between guest localization, host-guest interactions, and release. This critical narrative review integrates experimental and computational evidence for native α-, β-, and γ-CD-MOFs, distinguishing them from modified, composite, and MOF-derived carriers. A claim-specific evidence hierarchy separates spatially resolved observations, indirect experimental support, and computational inference. Guest localization depends on molecular dimensions, ionization, polarity, aperture accessibility, loading level, and processing history. Different loadings can favor distinct occupancy patterns, surface association, or guest-rich domains; these comparative states do not establish dynamic redistribution without time-resolved evidence. Stabilization generally involves cooperative hydrogen bonding, hydrophobic and dispersion interactions, and electrostatic or cation-associated contributions. Release may reflect framework transformation or dissolution, diffusion through persistent or added barriers, host-guest dissociation, and subsequent complexation, aggregation, or recrystallization. Similar release profiles can therefore arise from different mechanisms. A diagnostic framework links release interpretation to carrier persistence, guest speciation, medium chemistry, and analytical sampling, while source-specific loading definitions constrain quantitative comparisons. Molecular simulations provide candidate configurations and pathways but require experimental validation; kinetic fits alone do not identify microscopic release mechanisms. This synthesis establishes a structure-occupancy-transport framework and identifies the paired structural, time-resolved, and solution-state measurements needed for more predictable CD-MOF-based drug delivery.

articles.title: Lipid nanoparticles for precision nucleic acid delivery: linking cellular engineering to organ-specific targeting.
articles.abstract: Lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) represent clinically validated non-viral platforms for nucleic acid delivery, yet expanding their application toward precision gene therapy demands more than efficient particle formulation or tissue accumulation. Functional delivery requires navigating a sequential biological cascade: establishing biological access to target tissues, undergoing cell-specific uptake, escaping endosomal entrapment, and releasing intact cargo into the cytosol. Because each stage presents a distinct rate-limiting barrier, success at one step does not guarantee downstream therapeutic activity. This review provides a multiscale evaluation of LNP-mediated delivery, bridging ex vivo cellular engineering and organ-specific in vivo targeting. We first analyze how lipid composition, physicochemical properties, and cargo architecture dictate self-assembly and intracellular fate. For ex vivo applications-highlighting hematopoietic stem/progenitor cells and natural killer cells-we address the balance between high transfection efficiency and the preservation of cell viability, phenotype, and cytotoxic function. For in vivo platforms, we examine how administration routes, physiological barriers, and cellular accessibility govern delivery to the liver, spleen, pancreas, lung, kidney, and brain, emphasizing that bulk organ accumulation often masks poor intracellular bioavailability-particularly given that only 1-4% of internalized cargo reaches the cytosol. Finally, we organize these insights into a route-barrier-cell framework that evaluates biological access, cellular uptake, endosomal escape, and cytosolic activity as interconnected yet distinct performance metrics. Overcoming current translational hurdles-including species-dependent tropism, biological variability, repeated-dose immunogenicity, and manufacturing scalability-will be essential to transition LNPs from broad nucleic acid carriers into precision targeted therapeutics.

articles.title: The ATG4 family: Molecular gatekeepers of autophagic flux and emerging targets for disease intervention.
articles.abstract: Autophagy represents an evolutionarily conserved intracellular degradation pathway. Aberrant activation or impaired autophagic flux contributes substantially to the pathogenesis and progression of numerous human diseases, such as tumors and neurological disorders. As the only cysteine proteases within the core autophagy machinery, autophagy-related protein 4 (ATG4) family proteins directly drive the processing and delipidation cycle of microtubule-associated protein 1 light chain 3 (LC3) and gamma-aminobutyric acid receptor-associated protein (GABARAP). In this review, we systematically summarize research advances concerning the four mammalian ATG4 isoforms and elaborate on their evolutionary conservation, structural basis, and conformational activation mechanisms. Beyond their canonical functions in cleaving autophagy-related protein 8 (ATG8) precursors and mediating delipidation, we also cover emerging non-canonical activities of the ATG4 family. Particular attention is paid to isoform-specific and context-dependent roles exerted by ATG4 members across diverse diseases. Cumulative evidence identifies ATG4B as the most extensively investigated and functionally central isoform, which participates in cytoprotective autophagy, therapeutic resistance, neuronal injury, inflammatory regulation, and tumor progression. In comparison, ATG4A, ATG4C, and ATG4D may exert compensatory or independent functions depending on tissue context, disease stage, and stress stimuli. Furthermore, this review classifies small-molecule inhibitors and activators targeting ATG4 and discusses their potential applications in combination therapies for reversing drug resistance. Finally, we point out deficiencies in current research regarding subtype functional differentiation, structural analysis, and drug development, and propose reference solutions to provide a theoretical basis for basic research and targeted clinical treatment of autophagy-related diseases.

articles.title: Ethanol metabolism and acetaldehyde clearance: A multi-organ symphony.
articles.abstract: Ethanol (EtOH) metabolism and acetaldehyde (AcH) clearance jointly constitute a systemic biological network, coordinated across multiple organs and cellular compartments, and profoundly shaped by physiological, genetic, and environmental contexts. This broader view challenges the conventional notion of the liver as the sole gatekeeper of EtOH oxidation and AcH detoxification. Here, we dissect the enzymatic dynamics of EtOH oxidation and AcH detoxification within the liver, emphasizing cell-type heterogeneity and metabolic zonation, and expand the lens to the gut, liver-gut axis, brain, and other extrahepatic organs. These distributed processes serve functions beyond EtOH oxidation and AcH detoxification: they orchestrate metabolite exchange, modulate drinking behavior, and fuel disease trajectories. Recognizing EtOH metabolism and AcH detoxification as a multi-organ network not only redefines its biological scope and reshapes how we understand alcohol-associated disorders but also offers new options for therapeutic intervention.

articles.title: Isoliquiritigenin in breast cancer therapy: from mechanistic insights to advanced nano-enabled delivery strategies.
articles.abstract: Isoliquiritigenin (ISL), a chalcone from Glycyrrhiza species, exhibits multi-target anti-breast cancer activity but faces pharmacokinetic limitations. This review synthesizes evidence for ISL's molecular targets and mechanisms and evaluates nano-delivery strategies. In preclinical models, ISL inhibits proliferation via miR-374a/PTEN/Akt, reverses EMT through miR-200c/C-JUN/β-catenin, targets cancer stem cells via GRP78 inhibition and WIF1 reactivation, suppresses aromatase and COX-2, modulates osteoclast activity, and reprograms glycolysis and tryptophan metabolism. Independent groups demonstrated brain metastasis inhibition via circNAV3/EGFR, immune enhancement through PD-L1 reduction, and tryptophan reprogramming via IRF5/SLC7A5/IDO1. Systematic reviews consolidated evidence across 33 studies. TNBC is the most promising preclinical indication, with ER + breast cancer a potential target. Four nanoformulation platforms have been developed to overcome low bioavailability, rapid Phase II metabolism, and short half-life. Molecular docking predicts binding to PTEN, GRP78, β-catenin, and COX-2 but requires biophysical validation. Critical gaps remain: key mechanisms need independent validation, nanoformulation data derive mainly from one group, and no nano-ISL has entered clinical trials. This review provides a hypothesis-generating framework prioritizing mechanistic replication, scalable GMP production, GLP-compliant toxicology, and qualified biomarkers.

articles.title: Hydrogen sulfide in bone homeostasis: Mechanisms and therapeutic potential.
articles.abstract: Hydrogen sulfide (H₂S), as an endogenous gaseous signaling molecule, plays a central and complex regulatory role in maintaining bone homeostasis. This review summarizes the current evidence that H₂S participates in skeletal remodeling through coordinated regulation of osteoblast-lineage cells, osteoclasts, macrophage-mediated immune responses, and metabolic stress adaptation. Rather than acting as a simple unidirectional bone-protective factor, H₂S exerts context-dependent effects that are shaped by local concentration, release kinetics, cellular source, disease state, and the surrounding immune-metabolic microenvironment. These properties allow H₂S to serve as a dynamic mediator linking cellular function, microenvironmental remodeling, and skeletal homeostasis. With the development of sustained-release donors, microenvironment-responsive biomaterials, enzyme-modulating approaches, and combination strategies, H₂S-targeted interventions have become a promising direction for bone repair and regeneration. This review integrates cellular mechanisms, disease-associated H₂S synthesis disorders, and translational strategies to clarify the context-dependent role of H₂S in bone homeostasis and to provide perspectives for precision skeletal repair.

articles.title: Population pharmacokinetic models for unbound mycophenolic acid.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Mycophenolic acid (MPA) is a first-line immunosuppressant for organ transplant recipients. MPA therapeutic drug monitoring relies on total drug exposure which poorly reflects the biologically-active unbound MPA in clinical conditions with altered renal function and protein-binding. Population pharmacokinetic-Bayesian forecasting models (i.e. model-informed precision dosing [MIPD]) incorporating unbound MPA are needed to advance personalized MPA dosing. AREAS COVERED: PubMed and Embase were searched up to 22 July 2026 for population pharmacokinetic models of unbound MPA. Eight models were in adult kidney transplantation and three in hematopoietic stem cell transplantation. We evaluated their designs, sampling schedules, structural models, protein-binding, handling of the glucuronide metabolite (MPAG), incorporation of entero-hepatic recirculation (EHC), covariates, pharmacodynamics, and evaluation/validation methods. EXPERT OPINION: The studies exhibit heterogenous sampling schedules, analytical methods, structural models, and covariates. The handling of MPAG and EHC modeling is inconsistent, and protein-binding, a crucial component defining the relationship between total and unbound MPA, is not well characterized. No MIPD strategy is yet available. Over the next five to ten years, unbound MPA therapeutic and toxicity exposure thresholds should be established, which, in conjunction with validated population pharmacokinetic models that capture the complex pharmacokinetics-dynamics of MPA can form a more effective, personalized dosing strategy.

articles.title: siRNA therapeutics: from hepatic delivery to extrahepatic targeting.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Small interfering RNA (siRNA) has progressed from an experimental gene-silencing tool to an established therapeutic modality through advances in chemical modification and delivery. Lipid nanoparticles (LNP) and N-acetylgalactosamine (GalNAc)-siRNA conjugates have driven this clinical translation, particularly for liver-directed applications. Extending comparable delivery efficiency and selectivity to non-hepatocyte cell populations and extrahepatic tissues remains a major challenge. AREAS COVERED: This review examines approved and late-stage siRNA therapeutics and the delivery principles underlying their clinical development. Relevant publications and clinical trial records from 1998 to 2026 were identified through PubMed and ClinicalTrials.gov, supplemented by regulatory agency reports. LNP-based delivery, GalNAc-mediated hepatocyte targeting, and emerging strategies for non-parenchymal liver cells and extrahepatic tissues are discussed, with emphasis on the factors governing cell-selective and productive delivery. Next-generation delivery technologies and the therapeutic distinctions between siRNA and antisense oligonucleotides are also considered. EXPERT OPINION: The next phase of siRNA therapeutics will require a transition from organ-level accumulation toward functional cell-selective delivery. Improved receptor targeting, intracellular trafficking, and endosomal escape, together with rationally designed delivery systems, may extend RNA interference beyond hepatocytes and broaden its therapeutic applications in inflammatory, fibrotic, metabolic, and malignant diseases.

articles.title: A narrative review of stem cell-based therapy for fibrosing interstitial lung diseases: clinical evidence and translational perspectives.
articles.abstract: Fibrosing interstitial lung diseases (F-ILD) are a heterogeneous group of disorders characterized by pulmonary interstitial fibrosis and inflammation. Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is the most common and severe form of F-ILD. Regulator-approved anti-fibrotic drugs, such as pirfenidone and nintedanib, delay rather than reverse disease progression, so the threat of eventual respiratory failure remains. While lung transplantation is an option that can prolong survival for end-stage IPF, its clinical application is greatly restricted by donor shortages, surgical risks, and postoperative complications. Stem cell therapies, and particularly treatments based on mesenchymal stromal/stem cells (MSCs) and their derivatives, have brought new hope for the management of F-ILD due to their immune regulatory, anti-inflammatory, and anti-fibrotic capabilities. A search was conducted to identify relevant articles in the PubMed/MEDLINE, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, China National Knowledge Internet and Wanfang Data from inception to 31st May 2026. This review summarizes the mechanistic overview of stem cell-based therapeutic strategies for F-ILD, safety profiles and therapeutic potentials of various stem cells for the treatment of IPF and other F-ILDs, with an emphasis on stem cell types and delivery routine. This article also discusses the challenges and limitations of stem cell-based therapies, highlighting the need for further clinical studies with standardized efficacy endpoints to validate their effectiveness.

articles.title: Low-molecular-weight heparins in atrial fibrillation: clinical scenarios, limitations, and future perspectives.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is associated with a significantly increased risk of thromboembolic complications, including ischaemic stroke. Despite the dominant role of oral anticoagulants, low-molecular-weight heparins (LMWHs) are still used in selected clinical scenarios. AIM: The aim of this review was to summarise the current clinical role of LMWHs in atrial fibrillation, with particular emphasis on available evidence, practical limitations and selected complex clinical scenarios. METHODS: A review based on the analysis of available clinical trials, guidelines, and pharmacological data. RESULTS: Low-molecular-weight heparins are used primarily for bridging therapy and in situations where oral anticoagulation is temporarily contraindicated or not feasible. However, robust evidence supporting the long-term use of LMWHs for stroke prevention in atrial fibrillation remains limited. CONCLUSION: Low-molecular-weight heparins should not be considered standard chronic therapy for atrial fibrillation. Further studies are needed to better define optimal anticoagulation strategies in patients with atrial fibrillation, particularly in complex clinical settings such as active cancer and thrombocytopenia.

articles.title: Individualized dosing in the precision medicine era: a narrative review.
articles.abstract: Individualized dosing has become a cornerstone of precision medicine by optimizing therapeutic efficacy while minimizing toxicity through patient-specific dose selection. Traditional approaches, including weight- and body surface area-based dosing, remain fundamental for many medications but are increasingly complemented by pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic (PK/PD)-guided strategies and model-informed precision dosing (MIPD). This narrative review summarizes current evidence on individualized dosing across four major therapeutic classes: antimicrobial agents, chemotherapy, monoclonal antibodies and immunotherapies, and anesthetic and critical care agents. It highlights the rationale, advantages, and limitations of conventional dosing approaches while discussing the growing adoption of fixed dosing for selected biologics with predictable pharmacokinetics. The review also examines practical challenges associated with individualized dosing, including dose calculation complexity, medication errors, and operational constraints. Finally, emerging precision-dosing strategies, particularly Bayesian adaptive dosing and biomarker-guided dosing, are discussed as promising approaches to further personalize pharmacotherapy. Collectively, these advances support a shift toward more precise, evidence-based, and patient-centered medication dosing.

articles.title: Biologic and small-molecule therapies for inflammatory bowel disease: mechanisms, comparative evidence and the emerging pipeline.
articles.abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), comprising ulcerative colitis (UC) and Crohn's disease (CD), is a chronic immune-mediated disorder of rising global prevalence, with newly industrialised nations now entering the phase of most rapid growth. Its therapeutic landscape has transformed since 2020. Three selective interleukin (IL)-23p19 antagonists have been approved for both UC and CD; two sphingosine-1-phosphate receptor modulators and a second-generation Janus kinase (JAK) inhibitor have entered routine practice; subcutaneous formulations have altered delivery; and the first formal head-to-head trials, together with placebo-controlled trials incorporating an active reference arm, have begun to replace indirect comparison with direct evidence. In parallel, the ORAL Surveillance trial prompted a class-wide boxed warning that recalibrated, but did not eliminate, the role of JAK inhibitors. Three further strategies have generated late-phase data: anti-TL1A antibodies, which target a pathway not previously addressed pharmacologically in IBD; the miR-124 enhancer obefazimod; and the oral IL-23 receptor antagonist peptide icotrokinra. Several of these results are available only from conference presentations or company announcements and await peer review. Despite this expansion, induction remission rates remain clustered between roughly 15% and 50%, and endoscopic remission rates lower still. This review synthesises the mechanistic basis, pivotal evidence, comparative effectiveness, safety and regulatory status of approved and investigational therapies for IBD, and how treat-to-target principles, early advanced therapy and emerging biomarkers are reshaping positioning. It also covers two areas comparable reviews omit: acute severe ulcerative colitis, where advanced therapy is least well evidenced, and positioning in newly industrialised nations, where tuberculosis and hepatitis B endemicity and reimbursement, not efficacy alone, often determine the choice of mechanism.

articles.title: Pigeonpea leaves in orthopedic diseases: bioactive metabolites, pharmacological actions and therapeutic potential.
articles.abstract: Pigeonpea leaves are derived from Cajanus cajan (L.) Huth [Fabaceae] and have long been used in traditional medicine to relieve blood stasis, swelling, pain, and musculoskeletal disorders. Flavonoids, stilbenes, phenolic acids, and triterpenoids are among the main metabolite classes identified in pigeonpea leaves. Experimental studies have linked pigeonpea leaf-derived materials to changes in inflammatory and oxidative-stress-related outcomes, microcirculation, and bone metabolism. Accordingly, their potential relevance to orthopedic disorders, including osteonecrosis of the femoral head, osteoporosis, osteoarthritis, and bone defects, has attracted increasing interest. Reported preclinical effects include changes in osteogenic differentiation, osteoclast formation, local blood supply, lipid metabolism, and inflammation- or oxidative-stress-related tissue injury. Among the investigated materials, total-flavonoid fractions, stilbene-rich extracts, the purified metabolite cajanin, and Tongluo Shenggu Capsule have shown biological activity in experimental models. This review summarizes the current research on pigeonpea leaves and their extracts, fractions, purified metabolites, and preparations in orthopedic disorders and discusses their possible mechanisms of action, potential relevance to orthopedic disorders, limitations of the available evidence, and remaining research gaps.

articles.title: Analysis of queries in an HIV drug-drug interaction checker to explore changes in prescribing patterns: A 5-year analysis.
articles.abstract: AIMS: Careful consideration of drug-drug interactions (DDIs) is critical as people with HIV age. We analysed queries submitted to the University of Liverpool HIV Drug Interactions Database to assess changes in prescribing patterns over 5 years. METHODS: Queries submitted between January 2020 and December 2024 were extracted and categorized by year, antiretroviral agent, comedication class, interaction severity (green/yellow/amber/red) and country. Descriptive statistics and annual trends were assessed. RESULTS: A total of 7 274 301 queries from 48 countries were recorded, representing a 441% increase over the study period. Dolutegravir (21%) and bictegravir (20%) were the most queried antiretrovirals, and queries involving unboosted integrase inhibitors rose. The most queried comedication classes were antibacterials, lipid-lowering agents and supplements/vitamins. Amber and red DDIs declined by 6% and 3% between January 2020 and December 2024, while green increased by 9%. CONCLUSIONS: Query volume rose markedly while DDI severity declined, likely reflecting broader use of modern antiretrovirals with more favourable interaction profiles. Continued vigilance and interaction-checking tools remain essential in HIV care.

articles.title: Rosmarinic acid combined with cisplatin induces proliferation inhibition of hepatocellular carcinoma.
articles.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is characterized by high proliferation and metastasis potential and is prone to chemotherapy resistance, which seriously restricts the clinical efficacy of cisplatin (DDP)-based treatment. Rosmarinic acid (RA) is a natural bioactive compound that has shown potential anti-tumor and chemosensitizing effects in preclinical studies. The purpose of this study was to systematically explore the synergistic anti-hepatocellular carcinoma mechanism of RA combined with DDP through network pharmacology, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulation, and in vitro experimental verification. Network pharmacology analysis identified HCC-related core targets, which were enriched in cell cycle, apoptosis, and tumor metastasis pathways. Molecular simulation results confirmed that both RA and DDP can stably bind to core oncogenic proteins and exhibit good structural stability. In vitro experiments demonstrated that the combination of RA/DDP had a significant time-and dose-dependent inhibitory effect on the proliferation and colony formation of HCC cells. This combination significantly induced cell cycle arrest and apoptosis in Huh-7 cells and inhibited their migration and invasion, outperforming the single-drug groups. This study provides an integrated and preliminary mechanistic exploration of the potential synergistic effects of RA and DDP against HCC, integrating network pharmacology, molecular simulations, and in vitro functional assays. These in vitro findings suggest that RA may enhance DDP sensitivity in HCC cell models. Further in vivo and clinical studies are needed to determine whether RA can serve as a DDP-sensitizing agent and whether these effects translate into clinical benefit in HCC.

articles.title: Pharmacological interactions of carvedilol and curcumin nanomicelles in spontaneously hypertensive rats: a bliss and HSA analysis.
articles.abstract: Hypertensive target organ damage (TOD), including cardiac fibrosis, vascular remodeling, and low-grade inflammation, is driven by oxidative stress and proinflammatory cytokines. We previously demonstrated that acute carvedilol-curcumin co-administration in a Soluplus® nanomicellar formulation synergistically reduces mean arterial pressure in spontaneously hypertensive rats (SHR). However, the chronic protective effects of this combination on TOD remain unknown. The aim of this study to evaluate whether 8-week co-administration of carvedilol and curcumin in a Soluplus® nanomicellar system exerts synergistic effects on carotid SBP, aortic remodeling, cardiac inflammation, and oxidative stress in SHR and to quantify the drug interaction using the Bliss independence model. SHR received carvedilol (9 mg/kg/day), curcumin (6 mg/kg/day), their combination, or vehicle for 8 weeks. We measured (i) hemodynamics (tail-cuff and carotid SBP, beat-to-beat and short-/medium-term blood pressure variability); (ii) aortic and ventricular fibrosis (histomorphometry); (iii) oxidative stress (protein carbonyls, TBARS); and (iv) cardiac TNF-α, IL-6, and TGF-β (Western blot). We assessed synergy using Bliss independence analysis and the Highest Single Agent (HSA) model. The Bliss analysis revealed antagonistic interactions for cardiac fibrosis and cardiac TBARS, and additive interactions for TGF-β, aortic carbonyls, and aortic TBARS. The HSA analysis revealed that IL-6, TNF-α, and cardiomyocyte size showed additive/independent effects, while aortic fibrosis showed a synergistic interaction (ΔE_HSA =  + 22.22%, p < 0.0001). No synergistic interactions were observed for other parameters. However, the combination still significantly reduced all these parameters compared to vehicle-treated SHR. Chronic co-administration of carvedilol and curcumin in Soluplus® nanomicelles produced a synergistic antifibrotic effect on the aorta, while other parameters showed additive, independent, or antagonistic interactions. The combination preserved the beneficial effects of the monotherapies on oxidative stress and fibrosis, suggesting that the co-administration still provides target organ protection, although not through broad synergistic mechanisms.

articles.title: Exploratory machine-learning analysis of bevacizumab exposure and circulating VEGF dynamics in patients with cancer.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: This study explored pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic factors associated with circulating vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) dynamics during bevacizumab treatment. METHODS: A secondary analysis was conducted using data from 74 patients with breast, ovarian, cervical, non-small cell lung, or colorectal cancer. Paired pre- and post-infusion serum concentrations of bevacizumab and VEGF were measured by ELISA. Exploratory dimensionality-reduction methods and supervised tree-based models were applied. Artificial neural networks were used only as a complementary exploratory analysis on the same dataset. RESULTS: The main outcome of the analysis was VEGF_D, the absolute difference between the paired VEGF concentrations. The supervised models did not perform above the naive three-class benchmark; therefore, their variable-importance outputs were treated as secondary, model-specific, and hypothesis-generating observations. The results show exploratory model patterns of bevacizumab exposure and circulating VEGF dynamics. We did not assess clinical efficacy, safety results, and other dosing strategies in this study. DISCUSSION: The results do not support clinical implementation, personalized dosing, or treatment optimization and need to be confirmed in large independent cohorts.

articles.title: Phytochemical characterization and effects of Dolomiaea costus root extract on ovariectomy-induced metabolic, skeletal, and uterine alterations in rats.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Estrogen deficiency following ovariectomy produces metabolic, skeletal, and uterine alterations. METHODS: In this study, we evaluated an authenticated and chemically characterized dichloromethane-methanol (1:1, v/v) root extract of Dolomiaea costus (Syn. Saussurea costus) in ovariectomized female Wistar rats. Thirty rats were assigned to sham-operated, ovariectomized untreated, and ovariectomized extract-treated groups. Beginning 3 weeks after surgery, the treated group received the extract orally at 300 mg/kg body weight/day for 12 weeks. Metabolic and lipid variables, adipokines, antioxidant status, and bone-related biomarkers were determined. Uterine, femoral, hepatic, and adipose tissues were examined histologically, while estrogen receptor-α (ER-α) and tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF- α) immunoreactivity were evaluated. The extract was characterized using spectrophotometric assays, GC-MS, and HPLC-DAD. RESULTS: Ovariectomy was associated with increased body and adipose-tissue mass, dyslipidemia, impaired glucose homeostasis, altered adipokine concentrations, decreased antioxidant capacity, and structural alterations in the uterus, bone, liver, and adipose tissue. Compared with untreated ovariectomized rats, extract administration was associated with improvements in several biochemical and histological outcomes and with increased uterine ER-α immunoreactivity. Chemical profiling indicated the presence of sesquiterpene lactones, fatty-acid derivatives, and phenolic metabolites. CONCLUSION: Increased ER-α immunoreactivity is consistent with an estrogen-responsive effect but does not establish direct estrogen-receptor agonism. These preclinical findings support further standardized pharmacological and toxicological evaluation of the extract; they do not establish efficacy or safety in menopausal women.

articles.title: Tirzepatide versus other glucose-lowering therapies and risk of COPD exacerbations in patients with comorbid type 2 diabetes: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and type 2 diabetes (T2D) frequently coexist, sharing inflammatory and metabolic pathways. Tirzepatide (TZP), a dual glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide and glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist, has demonstrated metabolic and anti-inflammatory effects. However, its impact on pulmonary outcomes in patients with COPD and T2D remains uncertain. METHODS: Using the TriNetX global research network, we conducted a retrospective cohort study of adults with coexisting COPD and T2D prescribed TZP, sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT2i), dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitors (DPP-4i), or glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RA). Propensity score matching (1:1) was performed separately for each comparison. Primary outcome was COPD exacerbation; secondary outcomes included all-cause mortality, acute respiratory failure, and lower respiratory tract infection. Outcomes were assessed during a prespecified observation period from day one through day 365 after the index date. RESULTS: Matched populations included 6,080 patients per group (TZP-SGLT2i), 4,684 (TZP-DPP-4i), and 6,727 (TZP-GLP-1RA). In the independently matched comparisons, median follow-up was 232 versus 365 days for TZP versus SGLT2i, 235 versus 365 days for TZP versus DPP-4i, and 233 versus 365 days for TZP versus other GLP-1RAs; incidence rates were expressed per 1,000 person-years. Compared with SGLT2i and DPP-4i, TZP significantly reduced COPD exacerbation risk (hazard ratio [HR] 0.73 [95% CI 0.64-0.82] and 0.72 [95% CI 0.63-0.82], respectively) and all-cause mortality (HR 0.30 [95% CI 0.23-0.38] and 0.24 [95% CI 0.18-0.31], respectively). TZP also reduced acute respiratory failure and lower respiratory tract infection risks. Outcomes were similar between TZP and GLP-1RA, except TZP showed lower mortality (HR 0.55 [95% CI 0.42-0.72]). CONCLUSION: Among patients with COPD and T2D, TZP use was associated with lower risks of COPD exacerbations, respiratory complications, and mortality compared with SGLT2i and DPP-4i, findings that warrant confirmation through randomized clinical trials.

articles.title: Adverse reactions of immune checkpoint inhibitors combined with acetaminophen/non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs): a pharmacovigilance analysis of drug-drug interactions.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: The combination of immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) with acetaminophen (APAP) and non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) is commonly employed in cancer treatment. However, potential drug-drug interactions (DDIs) between these agents remain poorly understood. Our study aimed to identify interaction signals associated with the concomitant use of ICIs and APAP/NSAIDs. METHODS: Data were obtained from the US FDA Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS) covering the period from 1 January 2014, to 30 June 2025. Disproportionality analysis was conducted for data mining by calculating the reporting odds ratio and 95% confidence interval (95% CI). Adjusted RORs were analyzed using logistic regression, accounting for age, sex, and reporting year. Further confirmation was performed using both additive and multiplicative models. RESULTS: We identified 4,613 reports related to the combination of immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) with acetaminophen (APAP) and non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs). Significant interaction signals were observed for gastrointestinal disorders (adjusted ROR: 1.57, 95% CI: 1.41-1.70, additive model: 0.0549), investigations (adjusted ROR: 1.27, 95% CI: 1.13-1.43, additive model: 0.3847, multiplicative model: 1.3135), renal and urinary disorders (adjusted ROR: 4.68, 95% CI: 4.19-5.24, additive model: 3.5771, multiplicative model: 3.6312), and skin and subcutaneous tissue disorders (adjusted ROR: 1.64, 95% CI: 1.47-1.83, additive model: 0.6818, multiplicative model: 1.5996). Subset analysis revealed positive interaction signals for the combination of ICIs with APAP in gastrointestinal disorders and investigations, for all APAP/NSAIDs combinations with ICIs in renal and urinary disorders, and for the combination of NSAIDs with ICIs in skin and subcutaneous tissue disorders. CONCLUSION: Based on data from the FAERS, four systemic disorders were identified to be associated with drug-drug interactions (DDIs) resulting from the combined use of ICIs and APAP/NSAIDs. Further preclinical trials and well-designed, large-scale clinical studies are needed to explore the potential pharmacodynamic crosstalk, alterations in inflammatory pathway and changes in the tumor immune microenvironment induced by the co-administration of ICIs with APAP/NSAIDs. This will help deepen the understanding of DDIs associated with this combination therapy.

articles.title: Population cellular kinetics and exposure-CSR analysis of CAR-T cells in Chinese patients with relapsed/refractory B-ALL.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: CD19-targeting chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-T cells have demonstrated great efficacy in treating relapsed and refractory B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (B-ALL). Despite the high objective response rate of CAR-T cell therapy, high-risk adverse event of cytokine-release syndrome occur unexpectedly. OBJECTIVE: As living gene-modified cells, CAR-T cells exhibit unique kinetics. This study aimed to explore the relationship between CAR-T therapy-related CRS and the kinetics of CAR-T cells. METHODS: In this study, data for 2184 CAR-transgene copies from 131 B-ALL patients treated with IL-6 knockdown CD19-targeting CAR-T cells were included to characterize the cellular kinetics using a nonlinear mixed-effects (NLME) model. The extrinsic and intrinsic factors that may impact the kinetics of CAR-T cells were also evaluated. RESULTS: The CD4+/CD8+ ratio of CAR-T cell products was shown to be significantly positively correlated with Tmax, suggesting that a higher CD4+/CD8+ ratio may lead to a delay in reaching the maximum expansion, while other candidate covariates including tumor burden, CAR-T doses and comedication were not significantly associated with the kinetics of CAR-T cells. The estimated values of the cellular kinetic parameters Cmax, Tmax and Foldx were 4.696 × 104 copies/μg, 13.0 days, and 127.5, respectively. The estimated AUC0-28d and AUC0-90d accounted for only 13.0% and 18.5% of AUC0-inf, respectively, indicating that there was long-term persistence of memory CAR-T cells in vivo. In addition, the incidence of CRS was investigated to be correlated with the early kinetics of CAR-T cells, and the optimal cutoff values of Cmax and AUC0-28d for severe CRS were 6.951 × 104 copies/μg and 4.962 × 105 copies/μg × days, respectively.

articles.title: Metformin-associated diarrhea in FAERS: a structured pharmacovigilance study with long-term temporal consistency assessment.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Metformin-associated diarrhea is well recognized, but spontaneous-report analyses remain sensitive to outcome definition, reporting background, and incomplete event-date data. This study evaluated whether the reporting imbalance persisted across prespecified definitions, comparator sets, and calendar periods. METHODS: U.S. Food and Drug Administration Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS) reports from the first quarter of 2020 through the first quarter of 2026 were deduplicated and analyzed with metformin coded as a primary or secondary suspect drug. The primary outcome was the Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities preferred term DIARRHOEA. Sensitivity analyses used a broad loose-stool phenotype, a clean gastrointestinal event composite, alternative exposure roles, active comparators, co-medication exclusions, and stratification. Exact-date report-level event-date intervals among reports containing the strict-diarrhea preferred term were summarized descriptively. A separately processed dataset covering the first quarter of 2004 through the first quarter of 2026 assessed temporal consistency. RESULTS: Among 9,112,609 reports, 60,452 involved metformin as a primary or secondary suspect drug and 4,868 included strict diarrhea. The primary reporting odds ratio (ROR) was 2.72 (95% confidence interval, 2.64-2.80). Restriction to non-metformin antidiabetic reports attenuated the ROR to 1.95 (1.89-2.01), showing sensitivity to the reporting background. Only 595 reports (12.2%) yielded a valid report-level event-date interval; the median interval was 14 days (interquartile range, 1-363). The long-term ROR was 2.76 (2.71-2.81), with marked annual variation. CONCLUSION: Metformin showed a persistent but context-dependent diarrhea reporting imbalance in FAERS. Active-comparator attenuation limits causal and clinical-risk interpretation. The selected interval subset supports descriptive reporting only and cannot define diarrhea-specific onset or a clinical monitoring window.

articles.title: A novel CAF-related gene signature for prognostic and immunotherapy response prediction in PDAC based on single-cell RNA-seq and bulk RNA-seq data.
articles.abstract: Increasing evidence shows that cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) contribute to tumor progression, create an immunosuppressive microenvironment, and promote resistance to immunotherapy. However, the CAF-related gene signature in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) remains largely unexplored. In our study, we constructed a nine-gene CAF-related signature and found that it strongly correlated with the prognosis of PDAC patients in different cohorts. Subsequently, we found that the CAF-related gene signature was associated with the genomic alteration landscape, immune infiltration landscape and responsiveness to immunotherapy. GJB2 had the highest coefficient in our CAF-related gene signature, thus we explored the role of GJB2 in the interactions between CAFs and PDAC cells. The results showed that conditioned medium (CM) derived from the GJB2 knockdown group could suppress the malignant phenotype of PANC1 and MIAPaCa2 cells. In summary, this CAF-related gene signature is useful for prognosis prediction and precision therapy of PDAC patients.

articles.title: In silico evaluation of potential penicillin-binding protein 2 (PBP2) inhibitors from Borassus flabellifer haustorium against cephalosporin-resistant Neisseria gonorrhoeae.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: The emergence of cephalosporin-resistant Neisseria gonorrhoeae strains, encoding altered Penicillin-Binding Protein 2 (PBP2), has become a major global public health concern. The increasing prevalence of antimicrobial resistance necessitates the development of novel antimicrobial agents. In the present study, phytocompounds derived from the haustorium of Borassus flabellifer L. were investigated as potential inhibitors of PBP2 using an integrated in silico approach. METHODOLOGY: Phytochemical profiling of the methanol, ethyl acetate and hexane extracts of white spongy palmyra haustorium was performed using GC-MS and the identified compounds were subsequently evaluated for molecular docking, ADMET analysis and molecular dynamics simulation. RESULTS: A total of 69 compounds were identified and subjected to molecular docking against the transpeptidase domain of PBP2. The docking analysis revealed predicted binding affinities, ranging from -4.5 to -9.7 kcal/mol. The top ten compounds were subsequently evaluated for their ADMET and drug-likeness properties. Among these, 5-(4-nitrophenyl)-1,3,4-oxadiazol-2(5H)-one and 1,2,4-triazol-3-amine, 5-(1,3,5-trimethyl-4-pyrazolyl)amino, demonstrated comparatively favourable pharmacokinetic properties and balanced predicted ADMET profile. Furthermore, the stability of the complexes was assessed for a time period of 100 ns using molecular dynamics simulation. RMSD, RMSF, Rg, SASA, and hydrogen bonds were examined to evaluate protein-ligand interactions throughout the time frame. Principal component analysis and free energy landscape studies further supported ligand-induced stabilization of the PBP2 structure. MM-PBSA revealed favourable interaction energies of -19.11 ± 2.29 kJ/mol and -11.16 ± 2.34 kJ/mol for the two selected compounds, respectively. Among them, 5-(4-nitrophenyl)-1,3,4-oxadiazol-2(5H)-one demonstrated comparatively greater binding stability and thermodynamic favourability. CONCLUSION: These findings suggest that 5-(4-nitrophenyl)-1,3,4-oxadiazol-2(5H)-one could serve as a promising lead molecule for the development of new therapeutics against drug-resistant gonococcal infections and necessitate further experimental validation.

articles.title: Cannabidiol preserves astrocyte viability and attenuates injury-induced glial stress responses across zebra finch song control nuclei.
articles.abstract: Chronic neuroinflammation following traumatic brain injury (TBI) increases the risk of affective disorders and early-onset dementias. Existing anti-inflammatory therapies are limited by systemic side effects with chronic use and by poor brain penetration of newer biologics. Cannabidiol (CBD), a non-euphorigenic phytocannabinoid with a favorable safety profile and multi-target neuroprotective actions, is a promising alternative. Using a songbird microlesion model of learned vocal recovery after targeted damage to the premotor nucleus HVC, we previously showed that systemic CBD (10 mg/kg/day) reduces vocal disruption, inflammatory cytokines, oxidative stress, and synaptic loss. Here we tested the hypothesis that these benefits involve astrocytes. CBD (10 mg/kg/day IM for 7 days) preserved astrocyte viability, attenuated injury-induced lysosomal stress, suppressed reactivity markers (C3, S100A10, aromatase), and upregulated key metabolic and antioxidant transcripts (glutamine synthetase and GCLM) across the interconnected song-control nuclei HVC, RA, and Area X. These changes were accompanied by reduced neuronal apoptosis in lesioned HVC. The results identify astrocyte-associated responses as a candidate cellular substrate of CBD's circuit-wide protective effects and support its translational potential to mitigate secondary injury and communication deficits after TBI.

articles.title: Histopathology-guided spatial transcriptomic analysis identifies an ECM-associated stromal pattern in lacrimal gland adenoid cystic carcinoma with complementary proteomic and functional analyses.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Lacrimal gland adenoid cystic carcinoma (LGACC) is a rare but locally aggressive malignancy characterized by perineural invasion, recurrence, and limited systemic treatment options. Although extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling is increasingly recognized as an important regulator of tumor progression, its spatial organization and functional relevance in LGACC remain incompletely understood. METHODS: A publicly available LGACC spatial transcriptomic tissue section was reanalyzed using histopathology-guided annotation to define a highly cellular Tumor Core and an adjacent stromal region, termed the Stroma Boundary. Regional differential expression and functional enrichment analyses were performed, together with module scoring, a sensitivity analysis within a shared transcriptomic cluster spanning both histopathologically defined regions, and CellChat-based ligand-receptor inference. The spatial findings were further contextualized using a public bulk RNA-sequencing cohort and an in-house quantitative proteomic cohort comparing conventional LGACC with LGACC showing high-grade transformation (LGACC-HGT). The effects of type I collagen were evaluated in SACC-LM cells using morphological assessment, CCK-8, wound-healing, Transwell migration, and Western blotting assays. RESULTS: Within the analyzed spatial section, Stroma Boundary spots showed higher expression of ECM-related genes, including COL1A1, COL1A2, SPARC, and DCN, together with enrichment of collagen fibril organization and extracellular matrix organization. A secondary analysis restricted to a shared transcriptomic cluster spanning both histopathologically defined regions showed that ECM-associated differences remained detectable within a more similar transcriptomic background. CellChat analysis nominated collagen-associated interactions involving CD44 as candidate components of region-to-region communication. Bulk RNA-sequencing provided contextual support for the tumor-associated transcriptional program but incompletely captured the localized stromal pattern. Proteomic profiling demonstrated increased abundance of multiple collagen- and matrix-associated proteins in LGACC-HGT, accompanied by enrichment of ECM-receptor interaction and focal adhesion-related pathways. In vitro, type I collagen induced a more dispersed and spread cellular morphology and enhanced wound closure and Transwell migration without significantly altering short-term cell viability. Collagen exposure was also associated with increased CD44 protein expression. CD44 knockdown attenuated the COL1-induced increase in wound closure, suggesting a functional contribution of CD44 to this response. CONCLUSION: Histopathology-guided spatial analysis identified an ECM-enriched regional transcriptional pattern in the stromal compartment of the analyzed LGACC section. Complementary proteomic and functional findings suggest that collagen-associated remodeling may contribute to the migratory phenotype of ACC cells. CD44 represents a biologically plausible candidate associated with the collagen response, although its mechanistic role requires further validation.

articles.title: 3-[[4-(Benzylamino)quinazolin-2-yl] Amino] Benzenesulfonamide, a Quinazoline-Based PDE5 Inhibitor, Induces Vasorelaxation in Rat Mesenteric Arteries via Multiple Mechanisms.
articles.abstract: We synthesised a series of N2,N4-diaminoquinazoline derivatives, among which 3-[[4-(benzylamino)quinazolin-2-yl]amino]benzenesulfonamide (compound 5) exhibited potent phosphodiesterase type 5 (PDE5) inhibitory activity. Increasing evidence suggests that PDE5 inhibition is a promising therapeutic strategy for peripheral vascular disease. This study aimed to investigate vasorelaxant effects of 5 and its underlying mechanisms in rat mesenteric arteries. Compound 5 was synthesised and purified, and evaluated its vascular activity using organ bath assay. Molecular docking was performed to identify its potential molecular targets. Compound 5 (0.0001-30 μM) induced relaxation of phenylephrine (PE)-precontracted mesenteric arteries (EC50 = 0.76 ± 0.29 μM; Emax = 95.6% ± 1.1%). This effect was attenuated by endothelium removal (EC50 = 5.24 ± 0.98 μM) and by L-NAME (eNOS inhibitor). Compound 5 enhanced sodium nitroprusside-induced relaxation, supporting modulation of the NO-sGC-cGMP axis via PDE5 inhibition. Iberiotoxin (BKCa blocker) reduced relaxation, whereas 4-aminopyridine (KV blocker) and glibenclamide (KATP blocker) had no effect. Compound 5 inhibited vasoconstriction mediated by extracellular Ca2+ influx via receptor-operated Ca2+ channels (ROCCs) and α1-adrenergic receptor activation. Molecular docking provided qualitative support for PDE5A, BKCa channels and α1-adrenergic receptor as potential targets. In conclusion, 5 induces potent vasorelaxation in resistance arteries through eNOS/NO/cGMP signalling, BKCa channel activation and inhibition of ROCCs and α1-adrenergic receptors, supporting its potential as a therapeutic candidate for peripheral vascular disorders.

articles.title: The Predictive Value of Gastrin for the Absorption of Erlotinib in Patients with Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Gastrin regulates gastric acid secretion and increases when gastric acidity is reduced. Erlotinib, a small-molecule inhibitor used to treat patients with advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), has a pH-dependent absorption. We therefore investigated whether elevated gastrin levels, for example, due to proton pump inhibitor (PPI) use or achlorhydria, are associated with reduced erlotinib absorption. METHODS: Data of patients treated with erlotinib for NSCLC that were included in two previously conducted pharmacokinetic studies were used for this pharmacological proof-of-principle analysis. In these studies, patients were randomized to PPI use or not. Gastrin levels were quantified in samples drawn just before intake of erlotinib and used to study correlations with erlotinib concentrations. The pharmacokinetic endpoints area under the curve (AUC), trough concentration, and maximum concentration (Cmax) were correlated to gastrin concentrations and compared in patients with and without hypergastrinemia (gastrin ≥ 150 pg/mL). RESULTS: A total of 52 patients on erlotinib were included. Gastrin showed a significant inverse correlation with erlotinib AUC0-12h (r = -0.277; p = 0.047) and Cmax (r = -0.423; p = 0.002). In 11 patients with hypergastrinemia (gastrin ≥ 150 pg/mL), median erlotinib Cmax was > 30% lower (1890 ng/mL vs 1200 ng/mL; p = 0.024). The median AUC0-12h and AUC0-24h of erlotinib showed a non-significant trend towards lower AUCs of, respectively, 29% (p = 0.087) and 23% (p = 0.074), in patients with hypergastrinemia. CONCLUSIONS: Gastrin concentrations could potentially serve as a marker for erlotinib absorption, helping identify patients at risk for low erlotinib exposure.

articles.title: Stereoselective Determination of Omeprazole and 5-Hydroxy-Omeprazole in Dried Blood Spots for CYP2C19 Activity Assessment.
articles.abstract: We previously proposed stereoselective 5-hydroxy-omeprazole/omeprazole cut-offs for R- and S-omeprazole to differentiate between rapid, normal, and poor CYP2C19 metabolisers. However, the performance of these stereoselective CYP2C19 phenotyping approaches has never been compared with conventional racemic omeprazole phenotyping. Therefore, dried blood spots from healthy, genetically predicted rapid (n = 15), normal (n = 15), and intermediate (n = 14) CYP2C19 metabolisers were stereoselectively reanalysed after administration of omeprazole alone (10 mg) and following CYP2C19 inhibition with voriconazole (400 mg administered prior to omeprazole). Using stereoselective R-, S-, and racemic 5-hydroxy-omeprazole/omeprazole ratios, CYP2C19 phenotyping performance was assessed by genotype-phenotype concordance and phenoconversion patterns relative to prior reports. An adaptive phenotyping strategy using the 3-h metabolic ratio in individuals with delayed absorption and retaining the 2-h ratio otherwise improved agreement with AUC-based CYP2C19 activity measures (Spearman ρ = 0.99 vs. 0.93 and 0.88 for fixed 2- and 3-h ratios, respectively). Across methods, the racemic approach demonstrated the most favourable overall performance, closely followed by the S-enantiomer-based strategy. In conclusion, while racemic omeprazole phenotyping modestly remains the most accurate strategy for assessing CYP2C19 activity, stereoselective assessment of the S-enantiomer provides an alternative that enables CYP2C19 phenotyping in patients treated with esomeprazole without treatment interruption or substitution with omeprazole.

articles.title: In silico and in vitro immunogenicity risk assessment of process- and product-related protein impurities reported in adenoviral-vectored COVID-19 vaccines.
articles.abstract: Process-related protein impurities (PRPIs) such as host cell proteins (HCPs) in biologic products have been associated with unexpected immune responses, adverse events, and the discontinuation of clinical programs. While an HCP threshold of 100 ng/mg (PPM) is considered to be 'acceptable', that threshold may be too high if individual impurities have strong intrinsic immunogenicity or, in contrast, may be overly cautious if many of the HCP impurities have low immunogenicity. In silico methods for predicting the immunogenicity of PRI and HCP may help triage higher risk from lower risk entities. We explored this hypothesis by selecting candidate impurities from a published list of over 1,800 HEK-derived HCPs and adenoviral Product Related Impurities (PRIs) that were detected in high abundance in Chimp Adenovirus (AdV)-vectored COVID vaccine lots, for in silico and in vitro evaluation. The results of human donor peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMC)-based assays were well aligned with in silico estimates. These orthogonal approaches, when combined, have the potential to identify process impurities that should be removed to remove prior to submission of a drug product for approval regulatory authorities. In addition, the in silico and in vitro approach described here provides a framework for improving the overall safety of biologic products.

articles.title: Modulation of Postictal Hypoxia: Sex- and Route-Specific Effects of Acute and Chronic Cannabidiol and Delta9-tetrahydrocannabinol.
articles.abstract: Postictal hypoxia causes several consequences that are detrimental to the quality of life of people with epilepsy. Cannabidiol (CBD) and Δ9-tetrahydrocannabinol (THC), the primary phytocannabinoids from cannabis, have been shown to exhibit vasoactive and antioxidant properties that may mitigate the local oxygen deficiency observed after seizures. Here, we focus on the effects of CBD and THC on seizure-induced hypoxia. Adult Long-Evans rats of both sexes were assigned to drug-specific cohorts and the effects on local hippocampal oxygen were measured before and after seizure elicitation following either vaporized or oral administration of the two phytocannabinoids. Acute effects were assessed following a single administration of each drug, whereas chronic effects were evaluated over 28 days of daily treatment. In naïve rats, acute vaporized CBD significantly attenuated postictal hypoxia in both sexes, whereas acute oral THC attenuated postictal hypoxia in male rats. With chronic daily administration, phytocannabinoids produced time-dependent adaptations. Chronic vaporized CBD in females and chronic oral THC in males maintained attenuating effects on postictal hypoxia but exhibited partial tolerance, characterized by diminished effects on postictal oxygen decline in both sexes, recovery of postictal oxygen in females, and severity of hypoxia in males. These results demonstrate that acutely and chronically administered phytocannabinoids attenuate postictal hypoxia in a route-, sex-, and time-dependent manner. Together, these findings provide evidence that vaporized CBD and oral THC hold potential to treat the postictal hypoxia-induced comorbidities associated with seizures, potentially increasing the overall quality of life of people with epilepsy.

articles.title: Integrative network pharmacology and experimental evaluation reveal TNBC-related biological activity and toxicity of Euphorbia umbellata crude latex.
articles.abstract: Euphorbia umbellata latex is used in Brazilian traditional medicine, including empirically for cancer treatment. However, its chemical composition, molecular targets, pharmacological properties, and biological effects in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) remain insufficiently characterized. This study investigated the TNBC-related biological activity and toxicity of E. umbellata crude latex by integrating computational analyses with experimental evaluation in a 4T1 cell model. Eighteen compounds previously identified in E. umbellata crude latex were curated from phytochemical studies and evaluated for predicted pharmacokinetic and toxicological properties. Compound-associated human targets were integrated with TNBC-related genes, followed by protein-protein interaction network construction, functional enrichment analysis, hub-gene identification, and molecular docking. The effects of crude latex on cell viability, post-treatment recovery, and wound closure were evaluated in 4T1 murine TNBC cells, while acute toxicity was assessed using the Artemia salina lethality assay. The latex-derived compounds exhibited heterogeneous ADMET profiles, with generally low predicted mutagenic, carcinogenic, and hepatotoxic potential. A total of 357 compound-associated targets were identified, of which 204 overlapped with TNBC-related genes. Enrichment analyses highlighted pathways associated with apoptosis, inflammatory responses, oxidative stress, and immune checkpoint regulation. Molecular docking indicated favorable predicted interactions with EGFR, AKT1, and PARP1, whereas PTGS2 showed a more restricted interaction profile. Experimentally, crude latex markedly reduced 4T1 cell viability, with an estimated IC50 interval of 2.15-2.76 mg/mL, and impaired wound closure during acute exposure. However, both effects were partially reversed after treatment removal. The latex also induced concentration-dependent lethality in A. salina, with an estimated LC50 of 3.25 mg/mL. Together, these findings indicate that E. umbellata latex represents a chemically diverse source of bioactive compounds capable of interacting with TNBC-associated molecular networks, while also showing biological activity in a 4T1 murine TNBC model. Nevertheless, the partial recovery of 4T1 cells after treatment removal and the toxicity observed in A. salina indicate that crude latex should not be considered directly suitable for therapeutic use and that further fractionation, chemical standardization, mechanistic validation, and safety studies are required.

articles.title: Targeting Macrophage Glycolytic-Serine Metabolism and NF-κB Activation by Compound Xiancao Granule Confers Renoprotection in Diabetic Nephropathy.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Compound Xiancao Granule (FFXCKL), a traditional Zhuang medicinal formula, has long been used for diabetic complications, yet its molecular mechanism against diabetic nephropathy (DN) remains incompletely understood. AIM OF THE STUDY: To investigate whether FFXCKL alleviates DN by modulating macrophage glucose-serine metabolism and NF-κB-mediated inflammatory responses. MATERIALS AND METHODS: db/db mice and high-glucose-stimulated RAW264.7 macrophages were treated with FFXCKL. Renal function, histopathology, inflammatory cytokines, macrophage polarization, metabolomic profiles, transcriptomic alterations, and the expression of key glycolytic, serine biosynthetic, and NF-κB signaling molecules were evaluated. Glycolytic (2-deoxy-D-glucose) and serine synthesis inhibitors (NCT-503), together with NF-κB activator and inhibitor (JSH-23), were used to investigate the underlying mechanism. RESULTS: FFXCKL improved hyperglycemia, proteinuria, renal dysfunction, and histopathological injury while reducing fibrosis and systemic inflammation in db/db mice. It suppressed high-glucose-induced M1 macrophage polarization and normalized alterations in glucose and serine metabolism, accompanied by downregulation of HK-2, PKM2, PHGDH, PSAT1, and PSPH. Transcriptomic analysis identified NF-κB signaling as a major pathway affected by FFXCKL, and pharmacological modulation of NF-κB supported its involvement in regulating macrophage inflammatory and metabolic responses. Major limitations include the absence of isotope-tracing metabolic flux analysis and macrophage-specific genetic validation of the proposed mechanism. CONCLUSIONS: FFXCKL attenuated diabetic nephropathy by suppressing macrophage-associated inflammatory responses and improving glucose-serine metabolic disturbances, with effects associated with inhibition of NF-κB signaling. These findings support FFXCKL as a promising multi-target immunometabolic therapeutic strategy for diabetic nephropathy while warranting further mechanistic validation.

articles.title: Active components Alignment of Gegen Qinlian Decoction for inflammatory bowel disease: exploring the possible role of the SphK1/S1P/NF-κB pathway.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Gegenqinlian Decoction (GQD) has been used as a folk remedy for gastrointestinal diseases in China over thousands of years, and demonstrates significant efficacy against inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). We previously showed that the active components alignment of GQD inhibits nuclear factor kappa B (NF-κB) p65 signal transduction and plays a key role in preventing and treating IBD. With growing insights into the gut microbiota and its metabolites, the molecular mechanisms underlying therapeutic effects of GQD against IBD require further elucidation. This is particularly relevant given the previously reported relationship between the host NF-κB pathway and the gut microbiota. AIM OF THE STUDY: To explore the therapeutic mechanisms of GQD and its aligned active components against IBD, with a focus on microbiota-involved regulation of the host sphingosine kinase 1 (SphK1) /sphingosine-1-phosphate (S1P) / NF-κB signaling pathway, using both 2,4,6-Trinitrobenzenesulfonic acid (TNBS)-induced rat colitis and dextran sulfate sodium salt (DSS)-induced mouse colitis models and cultured cells. MATERIAL AND METHODS: In this research, the therapeutic effect of GQD on TNBS-induced colitis rats was evaluated through the measurement of body weight, colorectal length, disease activity index (DAI), colon length and hematoxylin-eosin staining. 16S rRNA gene sequencing and untargeted metabolomic analyses were performed to evaluate the restoration of gut microbial and metabolic homeostasis by GQD. Network pharmacology and molecular docking were then utilized to explore the potential relationships between specific targets and the active components alignment (ACA) of GQD on IBD treatment. To further validate the in vivo effects of the ACA, a dextran sulfate sodium salt (DSS)-induced mouse colitis model was established, and body weight, DAI, colorectum length, histopathology, S1P levels, and SphK1/S1PR1 expression were assessed. Experimental validation in LPS-stimulated RAW264.7 macrophages and NCM460 colonic epithelial cells was subsequently conducted to determine whether this active components alignment suppressed the SphK1/S1P/NF-κB pathway via molecular and cellular assays, including cell metabolomics, ELISA, Western blot, and immunofluorescence staining. RESULTS: GQD significantly relieved symptoms, colonic inflammation, and intestinal damage in TNBS-induced colitis rats. It partially reversed gut microbiota dysbiosis, modulated sphingolipid metabolic pathways, and downregulated the expression of sphingolipid-related Sphk1 and S1PR1 proteins, as well as S1P levels, in colon tissues (p < 0.05). In the DSS-induced mouse colitis model, the ACA of GQD significantly alleviated body weight loss, DAI, colorectum shortening, and histopathological damage, and reduced S1P levels and SphK1/S1PR1 expression in colon tissues (p < 0.05 or p < 0.01). In vitro, the ACA of GQD attenuated LPS-induced inflammatory responses in RAW264.7 macrophages and NCM460 colonic epithelial cells, as reflected by significant reductions in the levels of NO, ROS, and pro-inflammatory cytokines such as IL-6, TNF-α, and IL-1β, and S1P production (p < 0.05 or p < 0.01). Mechanistic dissection revealed that this ACA of GQD suppressed SphK1 expression and S1P production, inhibiting IκBα degradation and NF-κB p65 nuclear translocation, as directly evidenced by immunofluorescence staining, thus repressing the transcription of downstream pro-inflammatory genes and alleviating intestinal inflammation. CONCLUSION: GQD restored gut microecological homeostasis and rectified sphingolipid metabolic disturbances. Its active components alignment afforded anti-inflammatory and colitis-protective effects, partially via modulation of the SphK1/S1P/NF-κB signaling pathway.
