The consistent therapeutic and mechanistic effects observed in both TNBS-induced rat colitis and DSS-induced mouse colitis support that the eight-component alignment largely recapitulates the key effects of the complete GQD formulation. These findings provide novel mechanistic insights and a scientific rationale for the clinical application of GQD in the management of IBD.

articles.title: Essential oil from Angelica sinensis Radix attenuates ischemic stroke via the cGMP/PKG/MAPK pathway: insights from network pharmacology and molecular mechanism evaluation.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: As a traditional herbal remedy, the root of Angelica sinensis has long been used to treat headaches, strokes, and dementia. As the primary active ingredient in A. sinensis, A. sinensis essential oil (ASEO) also plays a significant role in the therapy of stroke. Although ASEO has shown clear therapeutic effects, its specific mechanism of preventing ischemic stroke still needs to be further clarified. AIM OF THE STUDY: Through network pharmacological analysis combined with in vitro and in vivo experimental verification, this study investigated the protective effects of ASEO against stroke and elucidated the underlying molecular regulatory mechanisms. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS) was used to analyze the chemical composition of ASEO. Middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion (MCAO/R) rats were administered different doses of ASEO to evaluate its therapeutic effects. The therapeutic effects were evaluated using behavioral, histopathological, and immunofluorescence assays. In addition, using network pharmacology techniques, the potential molecular mechanisms underlying the treatment of ischemic stroke with ASEO have been preliminarily elucidated. HT22 cells treated with oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation (OGD/R) were used as an in vitro model. Subsequently, the key signal transduction pathways involved in the therapeutic effects of ASEO against ischemic stroke were further validated using multiple experimental approaches, including enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA), flow cytometry, Western blotting, pathway-specific pharmacological inhibition and PKG-specific siRNA knockdown. RESULTS: Twenty-seven compounds were identified from ASEO by GC-MS. In vivo experiments demonstrated that ASEO treatment exerted significant protective effects on MCAO/R rats by improving impaired neurological function, reducing cerebral infarct volume, alleviating neuronal apoptosis, and modulating the expression of apoptotic proteins. Mechanistically, network pharmacology studies suggested that the protective mechanism of ASEO may involve the cGMP/PKG and MAPK signaling pathways. Subsequent experiments confirmed that ASEO inhibited neuronal apoptosis via the cGMP/PKG/MAPK axis both in vivo and in vitro. Importantly, both pharmacological inhibition and siRNA-mediated genetic knockdown of PKG significantly attenuated the protective effects of ASEO against OGD/R injury in HT22 cells. CONCLUSION: ASEO exerts its anti-ischemic stroke effect by attenuating apoptosis via the cGMP/PKG/MAPK signaling pathway, providing a scientific foundation for its clinical application in ischemic stroke therapy.

articles.title: Serratol, a cembrane diterpene from Boswellia serrata attenuates α-synuclein and fibrillar amyloid-β aggregation in Caenorhabditis elegans.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Boswellia serrata oleo-gum resin, known as Kundur in Unani medicine, has traditional applications in neurological and cognitive disorders, including Majoon-e-Nisyan and Dawa-ul-Kibreet for Nisyan (amnesia) and Muqawwi-e-Asab (nerve-strengthening) respectively. Serratol is a cembrane diterpene constituent of B. serrata resin, while related frankincense cembranes exhibit neuroactive properties. However, the contribution of serratol to the neurological activities of B. serrata remains poorly explored. AIM OF THE STUDY: To isolate serratol from B. serrata resin, evaluate its effects on protein-aggregation associated phenotypes in transgenic Caenorhabditis elegans models expressing human α-syn and Aβ1-42, and investigate potential molecular associations. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Serratol was isolated from B. serrata resin and evaluated in NL5901 and CL4176 C. elegans models. Network pharmacology, molecular docking and quantitative real-time PCR were used to investigate potential molecular associations. RESULTS: Serratol reduced α-syn associated fluorescence in NL5901 worms, although no significant improvement was observed in behavioral assays. Network pharmacology identified Alzheimer's disease and Notch signaling related pathways and PSEN1 as a computationally predicted candidate target. In CL4176 worms, serratol reduced ThT-positive, fibrillar Aβ associated fluorescence. Because Aβ1-42 is directly expressed in this model, this phenotype does not provide evidence for altered APP processing or γ-secretase-mediated Aβ production. Molecular docking predicted a possible association of serratol with the catalytic region of human PSEN1 and C. elegans SEL-12, while sel-12 mRNA expression remained unchanged. These computational findings do not establish direct target engagement. In silico ADME analysis showed compliance with several conventional physicochemical filters but a low predicted probability of blood-brain barrier penetration. CONCLUSION: Serratol modulates protein-aggregation associated phenotypes involving α-syn and fibrillar Aβ1-42 in C. elegans. The findings provide preliminary evidence supporting further investigation of serratol as a natural product scaffold for proteinopathies, while direct aggregation mechanisms, target engagement, functional rescue and CNS exposure remain to be established.

articles.title: Tetramethylpyrazine enhances angiogenesis in diabetic hindlimb ischemia by modulating the THBS1/PI3K/AKT signaling axis and reversing aberrant expression of MFN1/FIS1-related mitochondrial fusion-fission proteins.
articles.abstract: [BACKGROUND]: Type 1 diabetes with hindlimb ischemia (T1DM-HLI) is a prevalent diabetic microvascular complication characterized by impaired angiogenesis. Tetramethylpyrazine (TMP) demonstrates therapeutic potential in vascular disorders, but its role in T1DM-HLI remains unclear. [PURPOSE]: This study investigates the protective effect of TMP on impaired angiogenesis in T1DM-HLI and underlying mechanisms. [METHODS]: We evaluated TMP's effects on angiogenesis, oxidative stress, and mitochondrial fusion/fission balance in streptozotocin-induced and femoral artery-ligated T1DM-HLI mice and high-glucose-treated human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs). RNA sequencing identified key molecular mechanisms. Molecular docking predicted an interaction between TMP and thrombospondin-1 (THBS1). We show that TMP rescues impaired angiogenesis and disordered mitochondrial dynamics, effects possibly mediated through suppression of THBS1 and activation of the PI3K/AKT axis. [RESULTS]: TMP restored hindlimb perfusion and promoted vascular endothelial growth factor A (VEGFA)-driven angiogenesis in T1DM-HLI mice, while enhancing HUVEC proliferation, migration, and tube formation. It attenuated oxidative stress and reversed aberrant expression of proteins to mitochondrial fusion and fission. RNA sequencing revealed the THBS1/PI3K/AKT axis may play a central role in mediating the therapeutic effects of TMP. Molecular docking predicted a potential interaction between TMP and THBS1, identifying THBS1 as a candidate target of TMP. In vitro and in vivo experiments confirmed TMP treatment reduced THBS1 expression and increased PI3K and AKT phosphorylation. [CONCLUSION]: Our findings demonstrate that TMP may reverse dysregulated expression of mitochondrial fusion-fission proteins and enhance angiogenesis in T1DM-HLI by inhibiting THBS1 and activating the PI3K/AKT pathway, supporting TMP as a therapeutic candidate for diabetic hindlimb ischemia.

articles.title: Pharmacodynamic Evaluation of the Novel Vancomycin Derivative LYSC98.
articles.abstract: LYSC98 is a novel synthetic derivative from chemical modification of vancomycin. In this study, the antibacterial efficacy of LYSC98 was systematically evaluated against multiple clinically significant pathogens using Minimal Inhibitory Concentration (MIC) determination and murine systemic and neutropenic thigh infection models. LYSC98 was active against Gram-positive strains, with MICs generally higher or comparable to vancomycin against vancomycin susceptible isolates; however, it demonstrated elevated activity against vancomycin-resistant Enterococci (VRE), with MICs more than 8 folds lower than vancomycin. In both animal models, LYSC98 was active against methicillin-resistant S. aureus (MRSA), vancomycin-intermediate S. aureus (VISA), penicillin-intermediate S. pneumoniae (PISP), penicillin-resistant S. pneumoniae (PRSP), and VRE. In the systemic infection model, the median effective doses (ED50s) of LYSC98 against MRSA, VISA, PISP, PRSP, and VRE strains were significantly lower than those of vancomycin, and either not significantly different from or significantly lower than those of teicoplanin. In the neutropenic thigh infection model, two intravenous administrations of LYSC98 at 2, 4, and 8 mg/kg achieved 2.30-4.93 log10 CFU/thigh reductions against MRSA strains relative to the 24 h infection control, significantly greater than vancomycin at the corresponding doses; relative to the bacterial burden at the start of therapy (2 h control), net killing was achieved at 4 and 8 mg/kg against both strains, whereas at 2 mg/kg the burden remained at or above baseline. These results indicate that, within the strains, doses and models tested, LYSC98 is active against the Gram-positive species examined and is more effective than vancomycin in selected infection models.

articles.title: Recombinant Spinach Ribosome-Inactivating Protein Induces Cytotoxicity and Alters Gene Expression Associated with PTEN/AKT/mTOR Signaling, Apoptosis, and Stemness in HT29 cells.
articles.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains a major therapeutic challenge, highlighting the need for novel anticancer strategies. These challenges have increased interest in bioactive natural molecules with anticancer potential. In this study, we investigated the antitumor activity of a recombinant spinach (Spinacia oleracea) type I ribosome-inactivating protein (SoRIP) in HT29 colorectal cancer cells and evaluated its effects on cellular survival, apoptosis, and stemness-associated pathways. The SoRIP coding sequence was cloned, heterologously expressed in Escherichia coli BL21 (DE3), and purified by Ni-affinity chromatography, yielding a recombinant protein of approximately 22 kDa. Recombinant SoRIP reduced HT29 cell viability in a concentration-dependent manner after 48 h of treatment, with an IC50 of 48 μg/mL and cell viability of 51.3 ± 2.5% at this concentration. Annexin V-FITC/PI flow cytometry demonstrated a concentration-dependent increase in total apoptotic cells, reaching approximately 15%, 58%, and 79% following exposure to 12, 48, and 180 μg/mL SoRIP, respectively. At the transcriptional level, SoRIP increased CASP3 expression by up to 3.8-fold and PTEN expression by up to 4.3-fold, while reducing AKT and mTOR expression to 0.60- and 0.70-fold, respectively, at 48 μg/mL. BCL2 and CD44 expression were also reduced to approximately 0.65- and 0.70-fold, respectively. These findings indicate that recombinant SoRIP is associated with reduced cell viability, enhanced apoptosis, and coordinated transcriptional modulation of PTEN/AKT/mTOR-related, apoptosis-associated, and stemness-associated genes in HT29 cells. Collectively, these results support SoRIP as a candidate for further investigation in the HT29 colorectal cancer model.

articles.title: Tumor cell-derived SPP1 reprograms fibroblasts into CAFs via CD44/PI3K/AKT/Twist signaling axis to promote immune barrier formation in oral squamous cell carcinoma.
articles.abstract: The persistent progression and therapeutic resistance remain formidable challenges in the clinical management of malignancies. A pivotal mechanism underlying these clinical challenges is the formation of a tumor immune barrier at the tumor margin, which physically and functionally excludes immune cells from the tumor core. This barrier is primarily constructed by cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs), however, the precise mechanisms directing the reprogramming of resident normal fibroblasts (NFs) into these CAFs remain inadequately defined. In this study, we utilized spatial transcriptomics to confirm the presence of a CAF-rich immune barrier at the tumor margin of oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC). By performing integrated single-cell sequencing data analysis and functional assays, we identified osteopontin (SPP1) derived by OSCC cells as the predominant paracrine initiator of fibroblast reprogramming. Mechanistically, SPP1 binds the CD44 receptor on NFs to activate the PI3K/AKT/Twist signaling axis, which drives their transition into CAFs characterized by enhanced collagen production and increased invasive capacity. Notably, we demonstrated a self-reinforcing positive feedback loop wherein Twist activation upregulates CD44 expression, thereby amplifying fibroblast sensitivity to SPP1 and further sustaining the CAF phenotype. Pharmacological or genetic inhibition of any node within the SPP1/CD44/PI3K/Twist axis effectively attenuated the NF-to-CAF transformation and reduced collagen production. Our findings delineate an important molecular circuit underlying stromal remodeling in OSCC, the disruption of which can potentially prevent the CAF-driven immune barrier formation and overcome therapeutic resistance in OSCC.

articles.title: C-terminus of HSC70-Interacting Protein-Mediated Transforming Growth Factor-β 1 Protein Degradation Underlies the Anti-fibrotic Effects of Verbascoside in Pulmonary Fibrosis.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Pulmonary fibrosis (PF) is a progressive and fatal interstitial lung disease with limited therapeutic options. Transforming growth factor-β1 (TGF-β1) is a master driver of fibrogenesis, but strategies to effectively degrade this protein remain underexplored. Verbascoside, a natural phenylethanoid glycoside, exhibits anti-inflammatory and anti-fibrotic activities. However, its molecular mechanism in PF is unclear. METHODS: A BLM-induced mouse model was used to evaluate VBS efficacy in vivo. Human lung fibroblasts (IMR-90) were treated with BLM or TGF-β1 to assess fibroblast activation, migration, and fibrotic marker expression. Mechanistically, we examined the C-terminus of HSC70-interacting protein (CHIP)-mediated ubiquitination and protein kinase A (PKA) signaling, using pharmacological inhibitors (MG132, H89) and CHIP knockdown. RESULTS: VBS significantly reduced BLM-induced pulmonary fibrosis in mice, as shown by decreased hydroxyproline, collagen deposition, and fibrotic markers. In vitro, VBS suppressed BLM- or TGF-β1-induced fibroblast migration and activation. Notably, VBS reduced TGF-β1 protein levels without altering its mRNA expression. Mechanistically, VBS increased intracellular cAMP levels and PKA activity, promoted the interaction between CHIP and TGF-β1, and enhanced TGF-β1 ubiquitination. Furthermore, we demonstrate that PKA directly phosphorylates CHIP. These effects were abolished by PKA inhibition (H89) or CHIP knockdown, confirming that VBS drives CHIP-mediated TGF-β1 degradation via PKA activation. VBS also exhibited a favorable safety profile in mice. CONCLUSION: VBS activates the PKA/CHIP axis to promote TGF-β1 ubiquitination and degradation, thereby alleviating PF. These findings position VBS as a promising PF therapeutic and support targeting TGF-β1 stability.

articles.title: Anti-adipogenic effects of flavonoids and stilbenoids on adipocyte differentiation, lipid accumulation and adipogenic markers in a 3T3-L1 cell line.
articles.abstract: Obesity is a major global health challenge characterized by excessive expansion of adipose tissue mass, driven in part by dysregulated adipogenic differentiation. Targeting adipogenesis has therefore emerged as a promising strategy to limit adipose tissue expansion and associated metabolic disorders. Naturally occurring polyphenols, particularly flavonoids and stilbenoids, exhibit anti-adipogenic properties through multiple mechanisms; however, the molecular determinants underlying their activity remain insufficiently defined. In this study, the anti-adipogenic potential of a panel of 16 structurally related flavonoids and 2 stilbenoids was evaluated using the 3T3-L1 pre-adipocyte differentiation model. Experimental conditions were carefully optimized to ensure biological robustness, including cell passage number, dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO) concentration, and differentiation timing. Following cytotoxicity screening, adipogenic differentiation was assessed by Oil Red O staining and enzymatic quantification of intracellular triacylglycerides. Compounds showing significant inhibitory effects were further characterized by Western blot analysis of key adipogenic and lipid-handling proteins (C/EBPβ, PPARγ, FABP4, and ATGL), with transcriptional regulation evaluated by RT-qPCR for selected compounds. The results indicate that the tested compounds predominantly interfered with late stages of adipogenic differentiation, as C/EBPβ expression was largely preserved. Among the compounds evaluated, C10 (a synthetic 3-decyl-3',4',5,7-tetrahydroxyflavone) and piceatannol (C18) emerged as the most effective inhibitors of lipid accumulation. C10 markedly suppressed PPARγ isoforms, FABP4, and ATGL in a concentration-dependent manner, whereas piceatannol (C18) primarily reduced lipid accumulation through sustained FABP4 suppression with minimal effects on PPARγ. Overall, these findings highlight C10 and piceatannol (C18) as promising modulators of adipogenic differentiation and emphasize the importance of structure-activity relationships in shaping anti-adipogenic efficacy.

articles.title: Mechanism of koumine in treating ulcerative colitis by targeting TSPO to regulate energy metabolism.
articles.abstract: The pathogenesis of ulcerative colitis (UC) remains incompletely understood, and impairment of intestinal barrier function represents its most significant pathological alteration. All cellular functions require an energy supply for maintenance, and UC has been proposed as a potential energy deficiency disease. Translocator protein 18 kDa (TSPO) contributes to energy metabolism and is significantly related to the function of the intestinal barrier. Koumine, a high-affinity TSPO ligand, has well-documented anti-inflammatory activity. However, its effectiveness in treating UC hasn't been examined. The aim of our study was to examine the therapeutic effect of koumine on UC and clarify its mechanisms. First, a UC mouse model was induced with dextran sulfate sodium to investigate the effects of koumine on acute and chronic UC. Next, the effect of koumine on the function of the intestinal barrier was analysed. In addition, TSPO-knockout mice were used to assess whether the therapeutic effect of koumine on UC depends on TSPO. Widely targeted energy metabolomics was ultimately employed to examine the effect of koumine on energy metabolism in UC. The results showed that in both acute and chronic UC models, koumine was therapeutically effective and helped mitigate damage to intestinal barrier function. Moreover, the therapeutic effect of koumine on UC was almost completely eliminated by TSPO knockout. Metabolomics analysis revealed that koumine elevated the levels of DL-glyceric acid while reducing the levels of acetyl-CoA and 3-phenyllactic acid. In conclusion, koumine exerts its therapeutic effect against UC by targeting TSPO to regulate energy metabolism, thereby protecting intestinal barrier function.

articles.title: Trans-cinnamaldehyde targets VASH1 to reverse microtubule detyrosination and cardiac hypertrophy.
articles.abstract: Trans-cinnamaldehyde (TCA) is a bioactive compound derived from cinnamon. Our previous study demonstrated that TCA exerts anti-cardiac hypertrophy effects associated with reduced tubulin detyrosination, but its precise mechanism remains unknown. This study investigated the therapeutic potential of TCA against PE-induced myocardial hypertrophy and its mechanism via the VASH1-dependent α-tubulin detyrosination pathway. PE-induced cardiac hypertrophy models were established in C57BL/6 mice (in vivo) and neonatal/adult cardiomyocytes (in vitro), with TCA administered at 5 μM (in vitro) and 50 mg/kg/d (in vivo), consistent with our previous work. Cardiac structure and function, hypertrophy, tubulin detyrosination, T-tubule integrity, and related protein expression were assessed. Molecular docking and CETSA confirmed the binding of TCA to VASH1, CHX chase assays verified that TCA accelerates VASH1 protein degradation. Further mechanistic validation was performed using VASH1 overexpression rescue experiments. TCA ameliorated PE-induced cardiac remodeling, fibrosis, and diastolic dysfunction in vivo, and reversed cardiomyocyte hypertrophy and excitation-contraction coupling impairment in vitro. Mechanistically, TCA directly binds to VASH1, restrains its overexpression and excessive α-tubulin detyrosination, and further maintains T-tubule structural integrity. It thereby preserves normal JPH2-RyR2 colocalization, rectifies abnormal STIM1-Orai1 distribution, improves defective excitation-contraction coupling and inhibits excessive SOCE, ultimately restoring intracellular calcium homeostasis and sarcomere contractile function. VASH1 overexpression completely abrogates the cardioprotective actions of TCA. Collectively, these results demonstrate that TCA ameliorates PE-triggered myocardial hypertrophy and cardiac dysfunction via targeting VASH1 to normalize microtubule detyrosination, suggesting VASH1 as a promising therapeutic target for adverse cardiac remodeling.

articles.title: 1-Octen-3-ol from Bamboo Leaves Suppresses Lung Squamous Cell Carcinoma Progression by Targeting the PI3K/AKT Pathway and Activating p53/Caspase-3-Dependent Apoptosis.
articles.abstract: Lung squamous cell carcinoma (LUSC), a major subtype of non-small cell lung cancer, presents substantial therapeutic challenges due to limited targeted therapy options and prevalent drug resistance. In this study, we characterised 1-octen-3-ol, an active compound derived from bamboo leaves, as a bioactive natural compound with anti-LUSC activity. In vitro, 1-octen-3-ol significantly suppressed LUSC cell proliferation, migration, invasion, and colony formation, while promoting apoptosis. Network pharmacology predicted the PI3K/AKT pathway as a central mediator of its activity. Mechanistic studies confirmed that 1-octen-3-ol inhibited PI3K and AKT phosphorylation, accompanied by increased expression of p53 and cleaved-caspase3. The PI3K agonist 740Y-P and AKT agonist SC79 partially reversed the effects of 1-octen-3-ol on LUSC cell migration, invasion, colony formation, and protein expression, underscoring the critical role of the PI3K/AKT pathway. In vivo, 1-octen-3-ol markedly suppressed LUSC xenograft growth, and its tumor-suppressive effect was abrogated by co-administration of either the PI3K or AKT agonist. This study is the first to demonstrate that 1-octen-3-ol exerts potent inhibition of LUSC progression via modulation of the PI3K/AKT pathway, thereby activating p53 and initiating caspase-3-dependent apoptosis. These findings provide mechanistic insights into the anti-LUSC activity of 1-octen-3-ol, a natural volatile small-molecule, and support further lead-discovery efforts based on natural-product sources.

articles.title: Sinomenine pretreatment ameliorates septic acute lung injury through α7 nicotinic acetylcholine receptor-dependent inhibition of glycocalyx degradation and endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition.
articles.abstract: Sepsis is an organ dysfunction syndrome driven by microbial invasion, characterized by endothelial barrier damage, microcirculatory failure, and hyper-inflammation. Sinomenine (SIN), an alkaloid from Sinomenium acutum, has been demonstrated to alleviate sepsis by suppressing inflammation and modulating metabolism. However, its effects on the endothelial barrier and its underlying mechanisms remain to be fully elucidated. This study explores the effects of SIN on the endothelial glycocalyx and endothelial-mesenchymal transition (EndMT) in septic acute lung injury (ALI) and elucidates the critical role of the cholinergic anti-inflammatory pathway (CAP). The sepsis model was induced via cecal ligation and puncture, and cellular inflammation was modeled in HUVECs and RAW264.7 cells with LPS. IHC, ELISA, and Evans blue assay were employed to assess pulmonary glycocalyx degradation and vascular permeability. Molecular docking and Cellular Thermal Shift Assay (CETSA) were performed to validate the interaction between SIN and α7 nicotinic acetylcholine receptor. WB and qRT-PCR were used to detect CAP, EndMT, and inflammation markers. These assays showed that SIN can directly bind to α7 nicotinic acetylcholine receptor in a manner analogous to acetylcholine (ACh), while exhibiting a more sustained anti-inflammatory effect. SIN pretreatment activates the CAP by upregulating CAP-related molecules to inhibit the inflammatory response, downregulates the glycocalyx-degrading enzymes HPSE and MMP9 to reduce glycocalyx degradation, and inhibits TGF-β/NOX4-mediated EndMT. However, AAV6-mediated specific knockdown of pulmonary Chrna7 significantly weakened these effects. Collectively, our findings demonstrate that SIN pretreatment alleviates ALI and endothelial barrier damage by inhibiting α7 nicotinic acetylcholine receptor-dependent glycocalyx degradation and EndMT.

articles.title: 4-octyl itaconate alleviates metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis via activation of TFEB.
Pharmacological activation of vitamin D receptor by paricalcitol attenuates ferroptosis-associated myocardial injury after ischemia-reperfusion.
articles.abstract: Ferroptosis is a regulated form of cell death driven by iron-dependent lipid peroxidation and characterized by oxidative damage to membrane phospholipids. Increasing evidence indicates that ferroptosis contributes to myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury (MIRI), a condition that worsens cardiac damage following restoration of blood flow to the ischemic myocardium. This study aimed to investigate the role of ferroptosis in MIRI and to determine whether pharmacological activation of the vitamin D receptor (VDR) by paricalcitol modulates ferroptosis-associated cardiac injury. Myocardial ischemia-reperfusion was induced in mice by transient ligation of the left anterior descending coronary artery followed by reperfusion. Cardiac function was evaluated by cardiac magnetic resonance imaging. Ferroptosis-related pathways were analyzed through transcriptional profiling of antioxidant and iron-regulating genes, lipidomic assessment of oxidized phospholipid species, and ultrastructural mitochondrial evaluation. Complementary in vitro experiments were performed using human AC16 cardiomyocyte-like cells under ferroptotic stress. Ischemia-reperfusion led to a sustained deterioration of cardiac structure and function and induced several alterations consistent with ferroptosis activation, including changes in ferroptosis-related gene expression, accumulation of oxidized phospholipid species, and mitochondrial structural abnormalities. Pharmacological activation of VDR by paricalcitol attenuated ferroptosis-related transcriptional alterations, reduced lipid peroxidation, and mitigated mitochondrial structural damage, collectively limiting ferroptosis-associated cardiomyocyte injury and early ventricular dilation and systolic dysfunction. These findings suggest that VDR activation limits ferroptosis-associated cardiac injury during myocardial ischemia-reperfusion and may represent a pharmacologically relevant strategy to mitigate cardiac damage linked to ferroptosis.

articles.title: Gentiopicroside protects against kainic acid-induced excitotoxicity by preserving glutamate homeostasis in rats.
articles.abstract: This study provides the first evidence that gentiopicroside, a bioactive constituent isolated from Gentiana scabra, protects against kainic acid (KA)-induced excitotoxicity in rats. Intraperitoneal pretreatment with gentiopicroside (50 mg/kg) 30 min prior to KA administration (15 mg/kg) significantly mitigated seizure severity and prevented KA-induced cerebral blood flow (CBF) deficits. Histological analyses revealed that gentiopicroside markedly attenuated KA-induced neuronal loss, ultrastructural damage, and glial activation in the hippocampus. Mechanistically, gentiopicroside preserved the homeostasis of the glutamate-glutamine cycle, thereby reducing pathologically elevated hippocampal glutamate concentrations. This protective effect was mediated by the upregulation of glutamate transporter-1 (GLT-1) and glutamine synthetase (GS), alongside with the downregulation of glutamine transporters (SNAT1/3), glutaminase, and vesicular glutamate transporter 1 (VGLUT1). Furthermore, gentiopicroside normalized KA-induced alterations in AMPA and NMDA receptor subunit compositions, specifically restoring decreased GluA1, GluA2, and GluN2A levels while suppressing GluN2B upregulation. Additionally, gentiopicroside alleviated KA-induced mitochondrial dysfunction by suppressing calpain expression, restoring calpastatin and mitofusin 2 (MFN2) levels, and downregulating apoptotic protease activating factor 1 (Apaf-1). These findings suggest that gentiopicroside exhibits neuroprotective effects against KA-induced acute glutamate excitotoxicity by maintaining glutamate homeostasis, preventing calpain-mediated mitochondrial impairment, and attenuating glial neuroinflammation. These results highlight its therapeutic potential for excitotoxicity-related neurological disorders.

articles.title: Integrated aerosol deposition and epithelial transport in intranasal antiemetic dry powders.
articles.abstract: Intranasal dry powder delivery offers a non-invasive route for rapid systemic drug absorption and may be particularly beneficial for antiemetic therapy when oral administration is compromised. However, conventional in vitro tools typically assess aerosol deposition or epithelial permeability in isolation, limiting their ability to discriminate formulation-dependent transport behaviour. Two spray-dried formulations, differing only in the presence or absence of a non-ionic surfactant, were characterised for physicochemical properties and aerosol performance, followed by biological evaluation using an air liquid interface (ALI) RPMI-2650 nasal epithelial model. Aerosol delivery was performed using a nasal powder device coupled to a modified expansion chamber and cascade impactor, enabling direct deposition onto epithelial cell layers. Cytocompatibility, epithelial barrier integrity, and transepithelial drug transport were assessed alongside quantitative mass balance. Both formulations exhibited comparable solid-state properties, high emitted-dose reproducibility, and similar regional nasal deposition profiles. Neither formulation induced cytotoxicity nor disrupted epithelial barrier integrity, as evidenced by unchanged transepithelial electrical resistance and paracellular permeability. Despite similar deposition behaviour, the surfactant-containing formulation demonstrated faster initial transport and consistently higher transepithelial transport trends, without evidence of barrier compromise. These differences are consistent with formulation-dependent processes following deposition, such as differences in surface wetting and dissolution behaviour at the air-liquid interface. Overall, this study demonstrates that aerosol deposition alone may not fully predict epithelial transport for intranasal dry powders. The integrated deposition-transport platform provides a robust in vitro tool for formulation screening and optimisation, supporting the development of intranasal antiemetic therapies and other nasal drug products requiring rapid and reliable systemic delivery.

articles.title: Engineered hydrogels for boosting chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-cell therapy: strategies and biomedical applications.
articles.abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-cell therapy has emerged as a revolutionary approach to treat various diseases, including cancers and non-cancer diseases. However, as a type of living drug, the therapeutic performance and persistence of CAR cells can be markedly affected by multiple factors, from in vitro manufacturing to in vivo conditions. In recent years, bioactive materials, especially hydrogel-based strategies, have emerged as powerful tools to improve ex vivo and in vivo CAR-cell therapy. In brief, engineered hydrogels might regulate CAR-cell expansion or activation states during manufacturing and as models for cell functional assessments in vitro; in vivo, hydrogels might preserve CAR cells and regulate their retention, release and tissue infiltration while reprogramming adverse disease microenvironments. Despite promising advances, the progress, limitations and future directions of this field have not been comprehensively evaluated. In this mini-review, we evaluate the framework of hydrogel-based strategies in boosting CAR-cell therapy over the past five years, from cell manufacturing to functional improvement. Together, current findings suggest that engineered hydrogels provide spatial and temporal cues to enhance CAR-cell manufacturing and therapeutic capacity. This review might provide insights into design principles for developing tailored hydrogels to improve CAR-cell therapies to treat diverse types of diseases.

articles.title: In vivo skin uptake of piroctone olamine in human subjects assessed by confocal Raman spectroscopy and tape stripping.
articles.abstract: In vivo human studies are considered the gold standard for assessing skin penetration of actives. Tape stripping (TS) is a widely used method for investigating uptake of actives following topical application to the skin of human subjects. The results of TS studies have been shown to be influenced by a number of factors, including the variability in the amount of stratum corneum (SC) removed during the stripping process. This has stimulated much interest in the development of alternative non-invasive techniques for assessing skin penetration of compounds, such as confocal Raman spectroscopy (CRS). In the present work, in vivo skin delivery of piroctone olamine (PO) in human subjects was investigated from multiple solvent systems using CRS and TS. Vehicles were prepared with propylene glycol (PG), diethylene glycol monoethyl ether - Transcutol® (TC), isopropyl myristate (IPM), caprylic/capric triglycerides - Labrafac™ Lipophile WL 1349 (LAB) and propylene glycol monolaurate - Lauroglycol™ 90 (PGML). Analysis of CRS depth profiles, expressed as the area under the signal intensity-depth curve (AUC), showed higher PO uptake for PG:TC:IPM compared with PG:TC and PG:TC:LAB (p < 0.05). TS studies indicated higher total uptake of PO for PG:TC:IPM compared with PG:TC (p < 0.05). Across all formulations, linear correlations were observed between CRS-derived AUC values and TS-measured PO uptake (R2 = 0.79-0.99 for absolute uptake; 0.88-0.99 after protein normalization). To our knowledge, this is the first direct in vivo - in vivo correlation between CRS and TS for topical penetration of an active. It is also the first to investigate the in vivo skin uptake of PO using both CRS and TS, and to demonstrate correlations between these methods for profiling PO distribution within the SC.

articles.title: Application of the LeiCNS-PK model to quantitatively evaluate the roles of BBB active influx and brain metabolism of fluvoxamine and its serotonin transporter (SERT) occupancy in rat and human.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Nonlinear brain distribution of fluvoxamine has been attributed to saturable efflux at the blood-brain barrier (BBB). We hypothesize that active BBB influx and brain metabolism jointly govern fluvoxamine brain pharmacokinetics (PK). METHODS: Rat plasma and brain extracellular fluid (brainECF) PK data were used. The LeiCNS-PK3.5 model was modified by including active BBB influx and brain metabolism (Vmax, Km) of fluvoxamine (LeiCNSPK-3.5-FLV). Plasma PK parameters from observed rat data were used as input for the LeiCNSPK-3.5-FLV. Rat predicted and observed brainECF PK were compared. The model performance was evaluated by graphical diagnostics and quantitative metrics (RAdrug, AFE, AAFE, SMAPE). The rat model was converted to the human version. Using predicted fluvoxamine brainECF PK and a binding kinetic model, rat and human serotonin transporter (SERT) occupancy profiles were predicted. RESULTS: Combined inclusion of active BBB influx and brain metabolism in LeiCNSPK3.5-FLV accurately predicted the observed brainECF PK data in rats. AUC0-6h of predicted unbound fluvoxamine brainECF PK indicated a dose-dependent contribution of brain metabolism, highlighting its role in capturing the observed nonlinearity across the dosing range investigated. The predicted SERT occupancy in both rats and humans within 2-fold errors in quantitative metrics. CONCLUSION: Our findings challenge the previously proposed role of active BBB efflux transport in explaining the nonlinear brainECF PK of fluvoxamine. Instead, our findings demonstrate that the combination of active BBB influx and brain metabolism account for fluvoxamine's nonlinear brain kinetics, thereby enabling more accurate mechanistic understanding and improved translational prediction of brainECF PK and SERT engagement.

articles.title: ZYX knockdown alleviates chemotherapy resistance in epithelial ovarian cancer.
articles.abstract: The high mortality of epithelial ovarian cancer (EOC) is largely attributable to chemotherapy resistance. This study identifies Zyxin (ZYX) as a key driver of this resistance. ZYX was overexpressed in chemoresistant EOC patients and corresponding paclitaxel- (A2780/PTX) and cisplatin-resistant (A2780/DDP) cell lines. Functional experiments demonstrated that ZYX knockdown reversed chemoresistance by suppressing proliferation and migration, inducing apoptosis, and causing cell cycle arrest. Mechanistically, ZYX promotes resistance by interacting with Glycogen synthase kinase 3 beta (GSK3B), while its knockdown enhances paclitaxel sensitivity via β-tubulin upregulation and inhibits migration by reducing microfilament formation. Furthermore, ZYX knockdown potentiated paclitaxel efficacy in chemosensitive SKOV3 cells, both in vitro and in vivo. Our findings establish ZYX as a promising therapeutic target for overcoming chemotherapy resistance in EOC.

articles.title: Mots-c attenuates diabetic nephropathy by downregulating LARS1 to promote lipophagy and suppress tubular senescence.
articles.abstract: Diabetic nephropathy (DN) is a leading cause of end-stage kidney disease, but current therapies do not halt its progression. Mitochondrial-derived peptides have garnered attention for their roles in metabolic regulation, yet whether Mitochondrial Open Reading Frame of the 12S rRNA-c (MOTS-c) participates in DN pathogenesis has not been fully elucidated. In this study, MOTS-c treatment led to dose-dependent preservation of urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio (UACR), accompanied by attenuated tubular injury, diminished lipid deposition, and reduced macrophage accumulation. Transcriptomic analyses revealed significant enrichment of pathways related to senescence and lipid metabolism. Moreover, MOTS-c suppressed p16INK4A, γH2AX, and SA-β-gal activity, while restoring lipid homeostasis through regulation of CPT1A and ADRP. Mechanistically, MOTS-c downregulated LARS1, an established negative modulator of lipophagy, thereby facilitating LC3-mediated clearance of lipid droplets (LDs). LARS1 overexpression in HK-2 cells effectively abrogated these protective phenotypes. Furthermore, co-administration of the autophagy inhibitor 3-MA in db/db mice largely reversed the renoprotective effects of MOTS-c, supporting the functional relevance of lipophagy in this process. Our findings indicate that MOTS-c protects against diabetic kidney injury by downregulating LARS1, thereby promoting lipophagy, reducing lipid deposition, and suppressing tubular senescence. Targeting the LARS1-lipophagy-senescence axis may offer a new strategy for DN treatment.

articles.title: Selection of novel activators of non-genomic estrogen-like signaling (ANGELS) with promising potential for Alzheimer's disease.
articles.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is the most common type of dementia, affecting elderly women two- to threefold more than similar aged man, or the younger generations. Although 17β-estradiol offers neuroprotection, its clinical use is limited by serious side effects. This study explored a molecular group called ANGELS (Activators of Non-Genomic Estrogen-Like Signaling) as safer alternatives. A steroid library was screened via computational docking to estrogen receptor α. The top binders were preselected via in vitro and in vivo tests. The neuroprotective effect was examined in two mouse models of AD (neurotoxic and genetic). Morphological and behavioral changes were investigated. From the 15 top binders six molecules were identified without estrogen-like uterus effects and with rapid kinase activation. The chosen compound (A3270), acutely given, significantly restored cholinergic fiber loss without affecting cell loss or AD-related morphologies (amyloid β and phospho-Tau). Furthermore, it increased locomotor activity but had no effect on short term memory. These molecules lack ERE reporter activity and uterotrophic effects in vitro and in vivo and A3270 was promising in two AD model mice. We believe that these or similar compounds may provide novel approaches for AD therapy.

articles.title: Xinlikang capsule ameliorates cancer-related fatigue in Lewis lung carcinoma tumor-bearing mice: association with inhibition of oxidative stress and attenuation of JNK activation and bone marrow apoptosis.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Cisplatin (DDP)-exacerbated cancer-related fatigue (CRF) and myelosuppression impair patients' quality of life, and effective interventions remain limited. Xinlikang Capsule (XLK), a proprietary Chinese medicine used as adjunctive oncology therapy, has unclear effects on CRF. AIM OF THE STUDY: To investigate the effects of XLK on CRF in Lewis lung carcinoma (LLC) tumor-bearing mice and explore its mechanisms. MATERIALS AND METHODS: LLC tumor-bearing mice received control, model, DDP, or DDP plus XLK low-, medium-, and high-dose treatments. Fatigue behaviors, blood counts, bone marrow histology, and bone marrow cell populations were assessed. Enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) measured hematopoietic factors and cytokines. Network pharmacology predicted core targets, and apoptosis, oxidative stress, mitochondrial function, and JNK/NF-κB signaling were evaluated by histological, flow cytometric, immunofluorescence, and Western blot. RESULTS: XLK ameliorated fatigue-like behaviors, ncreased blood counts, improved marrow histology, elevated bone marrow cell populations, and modulated serum levels of hematopoietic factors and cytokines. Network pharmacology indicated apoptosis as a key pathway. XLK reduced bone marrow cell apoptosis and oxidative stress, restored mitochondrial function, downregulated apoptosis-related proteins (p-MKK4/7, p-JNK, Bax, and cleaved caspase-3), upregulated Bcl-2, inhibited NF-κB p65/IκBα phosphorylation, and reduced the co-localization of p-JNK and cleaved caspase-3. CONCLUSION: XLK alleviates DDP-exacerbated CRF and myelosuppression in LLC tumor-bearing mice. These effects are associated with suppressing of oxidative stress, restoring of mitochondrial function, attenuation of JNK activation, reduction of bone marrow apoptosis, and concomitant inhibition of NF-κB. However, direct causal validation of JNK signaling was not performed.

articles.title: N-(3-Trifluoromethylphenyl)sulfonyl-indole-3-carbaldehyde thiosemicarbazones induce apoptosis and modulate p53-associated signaling in prostate cancer: integrated experimental and computational studies.
articles.abstract: Prostate cancer continues to be an important therapeutic challenge that demands the development of new apoptosis-inducing agents. In the present study, a series of N-(3-trifluoromethylphenyl)sulfonyl-indole-3-carbaldehyde thiosemicarbazone derivatives (5a-s) was synthesized and evaluated for their biological activity against the LNCaP prostate cancer cell line. Among the synthesized compounds, 5a and 5g showed strong antiproliferative activity and favorable selectivity toward non-malignant HEK293 cells, with IC50 values of 7.56 and 5.81 μM, respectively. Compound 5g increased the expression of TP53, CDKN1A, BBC3, and BAX, whereas compound 5a significantly reduced the expression of the anti-apoptotic BCL2 gene. Both compounds also modulated the expression of cancer- and DNA damage response-related genes, including c-MYC, KRAS, PTEN, ATM, and ATR. Molecular docking studies predicted favorable interactions of compound 5g with MDM2 (IFD score = -7.951 kcal/mol; ΔG_bind = -56.75 kcal/mol) and compound 5a with BCL-2 (IFD score = -8.636 kcal/mol; ΔG_bind = -59.55 kcal/mol). 500-nanosecond molecular dynamics simulations further supported the dynamic stability and persistence of the proposed ligand-protein interactions. ADME and DFT analyses further indicated favorable pharmacokinetic and electronic properties of the lead compounds. Overall, the integrated experimental and computational findings identify compounds 5a and 5g as promising lead candidates for further investigation as apoptosis-inducing agents against prostate cancer.

articles.title: High-throughput in vitro lipolysis-permeation screening compared to in vivo drug exposure for a wide range of oral lipid-based formulations.
articles.abstract: During development of lipid-based formulations (LBFs) for poorly soluble drugs, formulations are often ranked according to in vitro API concentrations in the aqueous phase upon pH stat lipolysis. However, in an attempt to improve the in vivo relevance and to give credit to the free drug hypothesis, a recent study combined in vitro lipolysis with permeation, introducing a material-sparing high-throughput lipolysis-permeation approach on 96 well PermeaPad microtiter sandwich plates. The usefulness of the new approach was demonstrated in comparison to earlier published pH stat data for a set of model type I formulations for which in vivo rat pharmacokinetic (PK) data are available in the literature. The present study expands the dataset and is the first study to include formulations across the entire lipid formulation classification system (type I, II, IIIa, IIIb, IV) in a head-to-head comparison of in vitro permeation (flux) and in vivo drug exposure from previously published rat PK data, where the impact of supersaturation, lipase inhibition, lipid chain length, and precipitation inhibition was investigated. A statistical modelling approach was applied to identify the impact of the aforementioned formulation parameters (supersaturation, lipase inhibition, lipid chain length, and precipitation inhibition) on in vitro flux and to correlate in vitro results with in vivo drug absorption data. The analysis revealed that supersaturation increased the flux, in accordance with AUC in vivo for LBFs types I, II, IIIa, and IIIb. Lipase inhibition decreased the flux for type I and IV LBFs in accordance with in vivo results, but not for the other LBF types. The addition of a precipitation inhibitor did not have any significant impact on drug exposure, which was correctly captured in vitro for LBFs types I, II, and IIIa. The impact of lipid chain length was overestimated in vitro, probably due to poor dispersibility of the formulations. Overall, this high-throughput lipolysis-permeation assay was shown to be a promising tool for lipid-based formulation development.

articles.title: Evaluation of novel water soluble compositions of propofol for intravenous anesthesia.
articles.abstract: Solubilizing propofol without lipid-associated risks-hyperlipidemia, microbial growth, and severe injection pain-remains a major formulation challenge spanning over four decades. Traditional lipid emulsions persist largely due to the difficulty of achieving high-capacity aqueous solubilization without compromising safety or stability. This study evaluates a fat-free, preservative-free aqueous 1% propofol formulation enabled by a novel PEG-carbohydrate-lipid conjugate, 3,3-oleoyl-monomethoxy-polyethyleneglycol (n = 12 mean) ether-propanediaminolactobionate ("DOPS-F02"), highlighting its efficiency as an advanced solubilizing excipient for intravenous delivery. Solubilization capacity was profiled alongside a 24-month GLP stability trial of 1% propofol with 2.3% DOPS-F02 in 5% dextrose (Type I glass vials). A fixed-dose combination with 0.11% lidocaine HCl was evaluated without increasing excipient concentration. Pharmacokinetic, pharmacodynamic, and nociceptive profiles (rat paw-flick/paw-lick model) were compared against commercial control (Fresofol). DOPS-F02 demonstrated exceptional solubilization efficiency, driving propofol aqueous solubility up to 80 mg/mL at a low 1:2.2 w/w drug-to-solubilizer ratio in 5% dextrose or saline. Autoclaving induced a reversible cloud-point phase transition, returning to a clear, isotropic state upon cooling. Over 24 months, potency remained within ±3% with total impurities below 0.3%. In vivo, DOPS-F02 achieved therapeutic equivalence to Fresofol (loss of righting reflex; sleep duration 7.73-7.83 min). Unlike typical non-lipid formulations that exacerbate injection pain, DOPS-F02 allowed seamless co-formulation with lidocaine without phase separation, mitigating pain to near-baseline levels. As a novel solubilization platform, DOPS-F02 resolves a multi-decade formulation hurdle, delivering a clear, lipid-free propofol system requiring only a 1:2.2 drug-to-solubilizer ratio that eliminates emulsion liabilities and injection pain.

articles.title: Polymer nanoparticle-mediated delivery of microRNA 145: A potential therapeutic strategy for hepatocellular carcinoma in an experimental model.
articles.abstract: MicroRNA-145 (miR-145) plays a critical regulatory role in the pathogenesis and clinical management of various malignancies, particularly hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). This study aimed to evaluate the therapeutic efficacy of polymer nanoparticle-mediated miR-145 delivery in an experimental model of HCC. Eighty male Balb/C mice were randomized into four distinct groups: a normal control group, an HCC group, a group receiving free miR-145, and a group treated with polymer-conjugated miR-145. Following the intervention, hepatic expression levels of SENP1, P70-S6K1, and FSCN were quantified using real-time PCR. Additionally, serum concentrations of alpha-fetoprotein (α-AFP), vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF), and tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α) were measured via ELISA, complemented by a histopathological evaluation of liver tissue. The results showed that pathological controls exhibited a profound elevation (P< 0.001) in hepatic SENP1, P70S6K1, and FSCN expression, along with significantly higher serum levels of AFP, VEGF, and TNF-α compared with normal controls. While monotherapy with miR-145 successfully down-regulated these tissue biomarkers (P < 0.01) and reduced serum proteins (P < 0.001), the polymer-conjugated miR-145 formulation demonstrated superior therapeutic efficacy. This nanoparticle-mediated delivery yielded the most pronounced reductions compared with the free miR-145 group (P < 0.001 for P70S6K1 and FSCN; P < 0.05 for SENP1). These molecular improvements were further validated by histopathological findings, which showed a marked restoration of liver tissue architecture in the treated groups. In conclusion, utilizing polymer nanoparticles for delivering miR-145 substantially enhances its therapeutic impact, positioning this formulation as a highly promising targeted intervention for the treatment of hepatocellular carcinoma.

articles.title: Targeting PGAM1 overcomes paclitaxel resistance and restores cuproptosis sensitivity in non-small cell lung cancer.
articles.abstract: Paclitaxel (PTX) resistance is a major obstacle in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). The metabolic enzyme phosphoglycerate mutase 1 (PGAM1) is implicated in chemoresistance, but its role in PTX resistance and cuproptosis remains unknown. We analyzed PGAM1 expression in PTX-resistant NSCLC cells and patient cohorts, performed truncation mapping and co-immunoprecipitation, and evaluated the PGAM1/PP2A/AKT/β-catenin/ATP7B axis. Drug sensitivity and cuproptosis were assessed in vitro, in patient-derived organoids (PDOs), and in xenograft models using the PGAM1 inhibitor HKB99. We identified that PGAM1 is overexpressed in PTX-resistant NSCLC and correlates with poor prognosis. PGAM1 overexpression reduces PTX sensitivity and confers cuproptosis resistance. Mechanistically, PGAM1 binds PP2A via its 1-150 region (critical residues V81, R83, N135, D144), inhibiting PP2A and enhancing AKT/GSK3β phosphorylation. This stabilizes β-catenin and promotes its nuclear translocation, where β-catenin/TCF4 drives ATP7B transcription. Elevated ATP7B lowers intracellular copper, impairs DLAT oligomerization, and confers resistance to elesclomol-induced cuproptosis. Pharmacologic or genetic inhibition of PGAM1 restored PP2A activity, re-sensitized PTX-resistant NSCLC cells to paclitaxel, and re-engaged cuproptosis. These effects were rescued by reconstitution with wild-type PGAM1, but not with the PP2A-binding-deficient mutant, indicating that PTX resistance is driven by the scaffolding function of PGAM1. The therapeutic potential of this strategy was validated in PDOs and xenograft models, where HKB99 synergized with PTX to suppress the growth of resistant tumors. In conclusion, PGAM1 drives PTX resistance by enabling cuproptosis evasion through the PP2A/AKT/β-catenin/ATP7B axis; combining PGAM1 inhibition with PTX represents a promising strategy for refractory NSCLC.

articles.title: Ineupatorolide B Alleviates Postpartum Depression-Like Behaviors via the Gut Microbiota-Butyrate-Brain Axis.
articles.abstract: Postpartum depression (PPD) is a common mood disorder after childbirth and is associated with abrupt hormonal withdrawal, systemic inflammation, and neurobiological dysfunction. Increasing evidence implicates dysregulation of the microbiota-gut-brain axis in PPD pathophysiology, but safe and effective treatments remain limited. Here, we investigated the antidepressant-like effects and mechanisms of ineupatorolide B (InB), a bioactive compound isolated from Inula species, using a hormone-simulated withdrawal mouse model of PPD. InB significantly alleviated depressive- and anhedonia-like behaviors, as shown by reduced immobility in the tail suspension and forced swim tests and restored sucrose preference, with efficacy comparable to fluoxetine. InB also reduced serum interleukin-6 and tumor necrosis factor-α levels and restored the expression of postsynaptic density protein 95 and brain-derived neurotrophic factor in the prefrontal cortex. Gut microbiota analysis revealed marked alterations in microbial diversity and composition in hormone-withdrawal mice, accompanied by reduced fecal butyrate levels, which were largely normalized by InB treatment. Correlation analyses suggested associations among specific bacterial phyla, short-chain fatty acid metabolism, and behavioral outcomes. Notably, oral administration of butyric acid also alleviated depressive-like behaviors, suppressed systemic inflammation, and restored PSD-95, BDNF, and occludin expression in the prefrontal cortex of hormone-withdrawal mice. Together, these findings suggest that InB ameliorates PPD-like phenotypes, possibly through modulation of the gut microbiota, butyrate metabolism, systemic inflammation, and synaptic plasticity. However, the causal relationships among these changes remain to be established.

articles.title: The preventive effects of tetrahydroberberine on male obese mice and its uptake by adipocytes are associated with the D2R-PI3K axis and OCT2.
articles.abstract: Obesity arises from a chronic imbalance between energy intake and consumption that culminates in pathological adipose tissue expansion, ectopic lipid deposition, and persistent low-grade inflammation. Tetrahydroberberine, the principal reductive metabolite of berberine, exhibits potent lipid-lowering and fat-targeting activities. However, the causal link between adipocyte uptake of tetrahydroberberine and its preventive treatment effects against obesity remains undefined. This study investigated the uptake of tetrahydroberberine by MDI-induced hypertrophic 3T3-L1 adipocytes and in high-fat diet-induced obese male C57BL/6J mice, as well as its efficacy in the prophylactic treatment of obesity. The results demonstrated that tetrahydroberberine reduced body weight, epididymal fat mass, and perirenal fat mass, while ameliorating pathological changes in the adipose tissue of male obese mice. Moreover, tetrahydroberberine ameliorated lipid accumulation and inflammatory responses in both adipocytes and adipose tissues. Mechanistically, these effects were associated with inhibition of the dopamine receptor D2 (D2R)/phosphoinositide 3-kinase (PI3K)/protein kinase B (AKT) signalling pathway, which in turn suppressed leptin-mediated expressions of sterol regulatory element binding protein type 1c (SREBP-1C) and peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor γ (PPAR-γ). The findings also revealed that tetrahydroberberine primarily enters adipocytes via organic cation transporter 2 (OCT2). Notably, inhibition of the D2R/PI3K axis by tetrahydroberberine elevated OCT2 expression, thereby enhancing its uptake by adipocytes. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that the uptake of THB by hypertrophic adipocytes exerts an inhibitory effect on the development of obesity by regulating the D2R-PI3K axis and OCT2.

articles.title: Pharmacological basis of Suhexiang Wan in ischemic stroke: identification and functional characterization of piperlongumine as a brain-distributed bioactive constituent associated with STAT3-mediated blood-brain barrier protection.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Suhexiang Wan (SHXW) is a classical traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) formula that has been traditionally used for stroke-related disorders, including sudden loss of consciousness, neurological dysfunction, and hemiplegia. Although modern pharmacological studies have suggested its neuroprotective and anti-inflammatory properties, the brain-distributed constituents potentially associated with its therapeutic effects in ischemic stroke (IS) and the underlying molecular mechanisms remain unclear. AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aimed to elucidate the pharmacological basis of SHXW in IS by identifying brain-distributed constituents and investigating a candidate constituent potentially associated with its protective effects against cerebral ischemia/reperfusion injury (CIRI), with particular emphasis on blood-brain barrier (BBB) protection. MATERIALS AND METHODS: SHXW-derived constituents detected in brain tissue under middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion (MCAO/R) conditions were characterized using ultra-high-performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (UHPLC-MS/MS). Integrated network pharmacology analysis was performed to predict potential therapeutic targets and signaling pathways. Piperlongumine (PIP) was further confirmed and quantified in SHXW and brain tissue using an authentic standard-based LC-MS/MS approach. Molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, biophysical binding assays, and cellular target-engagement experiments were used to investigate the interaction between PIP and signal transducer and activator of transcription 3 (STAT3). The protective effects and associated mechanisms were evaluated in a mouse MCAO/R model and an oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation (OGD/R)-induced brain microvascular endothelial cell injury model. RESULTS: Among 1,991 putatively annotated constituents of SHXW, 55 SHXW-derived constituents were detected in brain tissue under MCAO/R conditions. In the MCAO/R mouse model, SHXW significantly improved neurological deficits, reduced infarct volume and brain edema, decreased BBB permeability, and restored tight junction protein expression. Among the brain-detected constituents, PIP, a natural alkaloid derived from Piper longum L., was selected for further investigation based on its detection in brain tissue, network topology characteristics, predicted association with STAT3, and reported pharmacological relevance to ischemic injury. Authentic standard-based LC-MS/MS confirmed PIP in SHXW and brain tissue, with a PIP content of 48.21 ± 1.10 μg/g in SHXW and a brain concentration of 159.67 ± 8.37 ng/g at 2 h after SHXW administration. Biophysical and cellular target-engagement assays supported the interaction between PIP and STAT3. PIP partially recapitulated the protective effects of SHXW by alleviating neurological deficits, preserving BBB integrity, restoring endothelial barrier function, and suppressing STAT3-associated inflammatory responses. STAT3 knockdown partially phenocopied the endothelial protective effects of PIP, whereas restoration of STAT3 expression in STAT3-knockdown cells reversed the protective phenotype. PIP treatment attenuated the injury-associated changes following STAT3 restoration, supporting the functional involvement of STAT3-associated signaling in PIP-mediated BBB protection. CONCLUSIONS: This study provides new insights into the pharmacological basis of SHXW in IS by integrating chemical profiling, brain distribution analysis, and pharmacological validation. SHXW exerted protective effects against CIRI and preserved BBB integrity. Among the SHXW-derived constituents detected in brain tissue, PIP was identified and functionally characterized as a bioactive candidate associated with BBB protection. The findings support the involvement of PIP-STAT3 interaction and STAT3-associated inflammatory signaling in PIP-mediated BBB protection. These results provide pharmacological evidence linking the traditional application of SHXW with its modern molecular mechanisms while highlighting brain-distribution-guided approaches for investigating the therapeutic basis of complex TCM formulas.

articles.title: Schisandrin B attenuates the platelet activation-thrombosis cascade through inhibition of Phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase/AKT and Extracellular signal-regulated kinase-Talin-mediated integrin αIIbβ3 signaling.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Schisandrin B (Sch B), a principal bioactive lignan derived from Schisandra chinensis (Turcz.) Baill. exhibits diverse pharmacological activities. This traditional Chinese medicine possesses therapeutic value for treating symptoms such as palpitations, shortness of breath, and a faint, nearly imperceptible pulse caused by deficiency of both qi and yin. AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aimed to investigate the molecular mechanisms underlying the effects of Sch B on platelet activation and thrombosis, employing a combination of network pharmacology, molecular docking, and comprehensive in vitro and in vivo functional assays. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Platelet aggregation and adenosine triphosphate (ATP) release were assessed using a lumi-aggregometer. Flow cytometry was used to evaluate Sch B's effects on P-selectin expression and integrin αIIbβ3 activation. Platelet adhesion, spreading, and clot retraction assays were performed to analyze outside-in signaling. Potential targets and signaling pathways of Sch B were predicted through network pharmacology, molecular docking, and Cellular thermal shift assay (CETSA), and these predictions were further investigated using western blot analysis. In vivo, the effects of Sch B on thrombus formation were evaluated using murine models. RESULTS: Sch B significantly suppressed platelet aggregation, granule release, adhesion, spreading, P-selectin expression, and PAC-1 binding. Western blot further analysis revealed that Sch B reduced the phosphorylation of key signaling molecules, such as Phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PI3K), AKT, Extracellular signal-regulated kinase (ERK), P38 mitogen-activated protein kinase (P38 MAPK), Talin1, and β3 integrin. In a mesenteric arterial thrombosis model induced by ferric chloride (FeCl3), Sch B significantly prolonged the time to stable thrombus formation. However, it did not significantly effect coagulation parameters or tail-bleeding time in mice. CONCLUSIONS: Sch B inhibits platelet activation by interfering with the PI3K/AKT/ERK-Talin signaling pathway, thereby attenuating thrombus formation. This supports its potential as an antiplatelet agent with a favorable safety profile.

articles.title: Platycodon Decoction alleviates chronic obstructive pulmonary disease associated inflammation with potential dual-layer regulation of PI3K/AKT/NLRP3 signaling and ADGRE5-mediated intercellular interactions.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: The traditional Chinese medicine formula Platycodon Decoction (PD) is known to be effective to alleviate respiratory system-related symptoms, its effect and integrated mechanism for treating COPD requires elucidation. AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aims to systematically address the pharmocology of PD in treating COPD through analyzing how PD inhibiting the intracellular inflammatory pathway and intercellular interactions. MATERIALS AND METHODS: PD composition was ascertained via LC-MS/MS. PD-induced organ damage was assessed through an acute toxicity test. Following the intervention of PD, body weight, lung index, sputum volume, pulmonary function, expression of inflammatory factors, pulmonary tissue injury, mucus secretion, and MUC5AC expression of the COPD-modeled mice were measured. PD's impacts on the levels of inflammatory factors, cellular activity, proliferation, cell cycle, reactive oxygen species (ROS), mitochondrial membrane potential, and inter-cellular communication were assessed through Beas-2b human bronchus epithelial cells and THP-1 human macrophage. The PD-associated, COPD relevant inflammatory pathways were analyzed through network pharmacology, molecular docking and molecular dynamics and then verified through Western blots. The involved cells for cell receptor identified by network pharmacology was analyzed by single-cell sequencing and verified by molecular dynamics and Western blot. RESULTS: The acute toxicity assessment provided preliminary evidence of PD tolerability under the tested conditions. Fifty compounds were identified in PD. Animal experiments demonstrated that PD can decrease the inflammatory levels and alleviate excessive mucus secretion in mice. In vitro cell experiments indicated that PD can efficiently abate inflammation and oxidative stress within the COPD-related airway microenvironment and diminish epithelial-macrophage interactions. Integration of single-cell and network pharmacology analyses identified ADGRE5 as a candidate receptor that may mediate epithelial-macrophage interactions. PD treatment reduced PI3K/AKT/NLRP3 signaling and was accompanied by decreased ADGRE5 expression. Computational analyses suggested a potential interaction between platycodin D and ADGRE5. CONCLUSIONS: PD alleviates inflammation in COPD, potentially involving dual-layer regulation of PI3K/AKT/NLRP3 signaling and ADGRE5-mediated intercellular interactions.

articles.title: Network pharmacology-guided investigation of the anti-angiogenic mechanisms of Spatholobus suberectus Dunn stem in rheumatoid arthritis.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a severe systemic autoimmune disease characterized by progressive joint destruction. Spatholobi Caulis (SC), derived from the vine stem of Spatholobus suberectus Dunn, has a long history of clinical application in traditional Chinese medicine for activating blood circulation and relieving rheumatic arthralgia. However, its pharmacological material basis and anti-angiogenic mechanisms for treating RA remain insufficiently elucidated. AIM OF THE STUDY: To systematically investigate the active constituents of SC and elucidate its anti-angiogenic mechanisms in RA using an integrated approach combining chemical profiling, network pharmacology, and in vivo experimental validation. MATERIALS AND METHODS: The chemical profile of SC was characterized using HPLC-QE-MS. A network pharmacology approach-incorporating target screening, protein-protein interaction (PPI) analysis, and GO/KEGG enrichment-was utilized to predict core targets and pathways. Molecular docking, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations and Surface plasmon resonance (SPR) were performed to evaluate the binding stability between key active compounds and hub targets. Finally, the anti-arthritic and anti-angiogenic effects were validated in a collagen-induced arthritis (CIA) rat model using micro-CT, H&E, immunohistochemistry (CD31), ELISA, and Western blot analysis. Additionally, to directly verify the predicted interactions, the effects of the core compound 7,3',4'-trihydroxyisoflavone (THIF) on TNF-α-induced MH7A cells were assessed. Cell proliferation, VEGF secretion, migration, and protein expression of EGFR and PIK3CB were evaluated after 24 h treatment with THIF. RESULTS: HPLC-QE-MS identified 24 active ingredients in SC. Network analysis identified key hub targets including SRC, PIK3CB, AKT1, EGFR, and ESR1 and revealed that SC predominantly modulates the PI3K/AKT, HIF-1α, and VEGF signaling pathways. Molecular docking, MD simulations and SPR demonstrated strong binding affinities and high structural stability between core compounds (e.g., THIF, Hesperetin, Afzelechin, (-)-Maackiain) and key hub targets (e.g., PIK3CB, EGFR, ESR1). In vivo, SC administration significantly alleviated joint swelling, preserved bone morphology (increased BV/TV and BMD via micro-CT), and reduced the organ indices of the thymus and spleen. Crucially, SC remarkably suppressed synovial neovascularization (decreased CD31-positive vessels), downregulated systemic inflammatory and angiogenic cytokines (IL-1β, TNF-α, IL-6, VEGF, TGF-α), and significantly inhibited the protein expression of SRC, STAT3, EGFR, PI3K, AKT, and HIF-1α in synovial tissues. In vitro experiments demonstrated that SC effectively inhibits the proliferation of MH7A cells. Flow cytometry analysis confirmed that SC significantly induces apoptosis in MH7A cells; However, this pro-apoptotic effect was alleviated upon addition of the PI3K inhibitor LY294002. Further in vitro validation with the pure compound THIF showed that it dose-dependently suppressed TNF-α-induced MH7A cell proliferation, reduced VEGF secretion from 292.18 to 80.32 pg/mL, and inhibited cell migration. Western blot analysis confirmed that THIF significantly downregulated the protein expression of EGFR and PIK3CB in a dose-dependent manner, directly validating the SPR binding results and demonstrating targeted inhibition of the downstream pathological signaling pathways associated with RA. CONCLUSION: SC effectively ameliorates RA progression by mitigating synovial inflammation and preventing structural joint damage. Its therapeutic efficacy is primarily driven by the suppression of pathological angiogenesis via the targeted dual-inhibition of the EGFR/PI3K/AKT/HIF-1α signaling axes.

articles.title: Toxicological Effects of Polyethylene Terephthalate Microplastics on Chronic Kidney Disease: An Integrative Bioinformatics, Network Toxicology, and Machine Learning Study.
articles.abstract: Microplastics and nanoplastics (MNPs) are widely distributed in human organs, including the kidney, brain, and liver, where they induce oxidative stress and inflammatory responses. However, the toxicological effects of MNPs on chronic kidney disease (CKD) remain largely unexplored. In this study, we employed an integrated approach combining bioinformatics, network toxicology, machine learning, and molecular docking to investigate the potential impacts of polyethylene terephthalate microplastics (PET-MPs) on CKD. A total of 191 CKD-related targets were obtained from the GEO database, while 875 potential targets of PET-MPs were identified using PubChem, ChEMBL, SwissTargetPrediction, and the SEA Search platform. Through weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) and machine learning, seven core targets were ultimately identified. KEGG pathway enrichment and Gene Ontology (GO) analyses indicated that PET-MPs may exert effects by modulating immune- and inflammation-related pathways as well as energy metabolism. Molecular docking revealed high-affinity interactions between the PET-MP-derived small molecules and the core targets, suggesting direct interference with cellular activities that could influence CKD progression. This computational framework not only elucidates potential molecular mechanisms of MNP-induced nephrotoxicity but also identifies candidate targets for therapeutic intervention, aligning with the scope of machine-learning-driven drug molecule design.

articles.title: Multimodal Deep Learning for Wound Healing Prediction.
articles.abstract: Chronic wounds, particularly diabetic foot ulcers, heal unpredictably and impose substantial healthcare costs. Deep learning (DL) systems that integrate complementary data streams could support preclinical studies by assessing wound status and therapy efficacy reliably in small-n studies. We developed a three-branch neural network combining convolutional feature extraction for red-green-blue (RGB) images, infrared thermography, and wound-area measurements to classify healing stage and infer treatment response in diabetic mouse wound model. In descriptive ablation analysis, the model integrating RGB and wound-size inputs achieved higher accuracy than the RGB-only configuration (0.75 vs. 0.70), suggesting that explicit size context provided useful complementary information. Thermal images appeared qualitatively informative during early healing but contributed limited additional signal later, likely reflecting subtle inflammatory gradients or angiogenesis in healthy murine skin; this observation motivated a constrained weighted-fusion strategy. In the development-stage comparison, static fusion with tunable fixed weights yielded the highest observed performance (∼0.85 accuracy on the development test subject). Grad-CAM visualizations showed that predictions arose from biologically relevant regions rather than image artifacts. Experiments without subject-level partitioning produced inflated metrics, underscoring the need for grouping by subject to ensure generalizable evaluation. Nested Leave-One-Group-Out cross-validation with KerasTuner-based hyperparameter tuning yielded a mean accuracy of 0.71, estimating performance on unseen subjects. This resulting proof-of-concept model predicts treatment responses for wounds treated with nanofibrillated-cellulose hydrogel. Multimodal DL combining standard and thermal photography with size metrics can stage wound healing and detect divergent treatment trajectories and thus be used in preclinical efficacy evaluation of novel wound treatments. With larger, clinically annotated datasets, this approach could be applied in a clinical setting as well.

articles.title: Crocin alleviates lead acetate-induced liver and kidney damage in rats by regulating oxidative stress, autophagy, apoptosis, and histopathological changes.
articles.abstract: Lead (Pb) is a heavy metal that can trigger oxidative stress, causing toxic effects particularly on the liver and kidneys. Crocin (Cro) has been demonstrated to possess anti-autophagic and anti-apoptotic properties in addition to its antioxidant activity. The objective is to assess Cro's capacity to stop Pb-induced liver and kidney damage. A total of 32 rats were used in the investigation, split into four groups of eight rats each: Control, Cro, PbAc, and PbAc + Cro. In addition to histopathological improvement, treatment with Cro (50 mg/kg, orally, for 7 days) alleviated the damage to liver and kidney tissues caused by PbAc (30 mg/kg, orally, for 7 days) by reducing levels of ALT, AST and ALP, as well as blood urea and creatinine. Cro treatment also increased GSH levels, SOD and CAT enzyme activities and lowered MDA levels in PbAc-induced tissues. By raising 8-OHdG levels in liver and kidney tissues, PbAc damaged DNA. It also stimulated autophagy by elevating Beclin-1, LC3A, and LC3B levels. In addition to all this, it activated apoptosis by increasing Bax and Cyt-c levels whilst reducing Bcl-2 synthesis. However, treatment with Cro decreased DNA damage, autophagy, and apoptosis in both tissues. Our results suggest that Cro could be able to lessen the adverse effects of PbAc-induced liver and kidney damage.

articles.title: Lateral hypothalamic orexin→VTA projection regulates consolation via orexin receptor 1 in male mice.
articles.abstract: Consolation, a prosocial behavior in which individuals comfort distressed conspecifics, is regarded as a fundamental expression of empathy. Orexin (OX) neurons in the lateral hypothalamus (LH) have been implicated in empathic processes, but the specific circuitry and receptor subtypes through which they modulate consolation remain unknown. Here, we investigated the role of LHOX neurons and their projection to the ventral tegmental area (VTA) in regulating consolation-like behavior in male mice. We found that consolation toward a defeat induced stressed partner was accompanied by reduced c-Fos expression in LHOX neurons. Using chemogenetic manipulations, we demonstrated that activation of LHOX neurons, or specifically the LHOX→VTA projections, decreased consolation-like allogrooming. Furthermore, intra-VTA injection of the orexin receptor 1 (OX1R) antagonist SB-334867, but not the OX2R antagonist Seltorexant, rescued the allogrooming deficit induced by pathway activation, identifying VTA OX1R as the critical receptor subtype. These effects occurred without alterations in anxiety-like behavior or general sociability. Collectively, these findings reveal that the LHOX→VTA pathway, acting through OX1R, contributes to the regulation of consolation, establishing a receptor-specific circuit mechanism for orexinergic modulation of empathy-related prosocial behavior.

articles.title: Preconditioning induces ischemic tolerance by attenuating ferroptosis: involvement of the m6A-dependent FTO-IGF2BP1/3-ACSL4 regulatory Axis.
articles.abstract: Cerebral ischemic preconditioning (CIP) confers robust protection against subsequent ischemic stroke by enhancing brain ischemic tolerance. Although ferroptosis is increasingly recognized as a critical pathogenic mechanism in stroke, the role of N6-methyladenosine (m6A) RNA modification in its regulation remains poorly understood. This study investigated the involvement of m6A signaling in the anti-ferroptotic mechanism of CIP using complementary in vivo mouse middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO) and in vitro oxygen-glucose deprivation (OGD) models.
