We found that CIP significantly attenuated ischemia-induced neuronal ferroptosis in vivo, whereas OGD preconditioning (OGDP) recapitulated these anti-ferroptotic effects in HT22 cells. Acyl-CoA synthetase long-chain family member 4 (ACSL4), a key executor of ferroptosis, was markedly upregulated following ischemic injury, whereas CIP effectively suppressed this increase. Similarly, OGDP attenuated OGD-induced ACSL4 upregulation in HT22 cells. Importantly, ACSL4 overexpression significantly attenuated the protective effects of OGDP against OGD-induced ferroptosis. Mechanistic analyses in HT22 cells revealed that OGD downregulated the m6A demethylase fat mass and obesity-associated protein (FTO) and upregulated m6A readers insulin-like growth factor 2 mRNA-binding proteins (IGF2BPs), including IGF2BP1 and IGF2BP3, thereby stabilizing ACSL4 mRNA and promoting ferroptosis. OGDP alleviated these effects by restoring FTO expression, reducing IGF2BP1 and IGF2BP3 levels, and enhancing m6A-dependent ACSL4 mRNA decay. Together, these findings demonstrate that CIP induces ischemic tolerance and attenuates ACSL4-associated ferroptosis. Mechanistic studies in neuronal cells further identify the m6A-dependent FTO-IGF2BP1/3-ACSL4 axis as a potential regulatory mechanism contributing to OGDP-induced ferroptosis resistance.

articles.title: Trojan microparticles of budesonide palmitate nanoparticles: formulation optimization for lung delivery.
articles.abstract: A prodrug of budesonide, budesonide palmitate, was synthesized and formulated into nanoparticles by emulsion-evaporation, using a PEGylated lipid, DSPE-mPEG, as the sole excipient. Spherical nanoparticles of about 200 nm were obtained, with prodrug content between 57-73% by weight. To deliver nanoparticles to the lungs as dry powders, Trojan microparticles containing 5%-20% (w/w) of these prodrug-based nanoparticles were formulated for the first time by spray drying. Results show that the fine particle fraction decreases as the nanoparticle percentage increases. The formulation with 5% nanoparticles is optimal for targeting the alveolar region, with a mean mass aerodynamic diameter of 3.3 μm, a fine particle fraction of 67%, and an alveolar particle fraction of 41%. These Trojan microparticles appear to be promising carriers for the treatment of respiratory diseases via lung delivery.

articles.title: Cytosol-hydrogelled Chlorella enabling intestinal-targeted budesonide delivery for ulcerative colitis treatment.
articles.abstract: Current oral enteric sustained-release formulations largely rely on polymer-based surface coatings and multi-matrix technologies, which increase manufacturing complexity and overall production costs. Here, we report a cytosol-hydrogelled Chlorella pyrenoidosa (CP) delivery system, named BUD-gel@CP, for sustained release of budesonide (BUD) in the intestinal tract. Unlike conventional microalgae-based drug delivery strategies, this system requires neither surface modification nor enteric coating. We find for the first time that the intrinsic proteins of CP, such as chlorophyll protein 47 (CP47), physically entrap BUD in aggregates under acidic gastric conditions, enabling the enteric release of BUD. Importantly, BUD is easily loaded into the cytosol of lyophilized CP in the presence of two FDA-approved excipients, which are Labrasol® as a solubilizer and Soluplus® to form a thermosensitivein situgel. Following oral administration, BUD-gel@CP showed prolonged drug retention in the intestinal tract and elevated BUD concentrations in intestinal tissues. In a DSS-induced colitis mouse model, BUD-gel@CP restored colon length and reduced TNF-α and IL-6 levels, showing improved therapeutic effects compared with non-hydrogelled control groups. Our findings suggest a novel paradigm for preparing an enteric sustained-release oral drug delivery system that utilizes natural food ingredients and commercially approved pharmaceutical excipients without surface coating or modification.

articles.title: CircNFIB attenuates hypoxia/reoxygenation-induced ferroptosis in AC16 cardiomyocytes with involvement of the miR-338-3p/GPX4 pathway.
articles.abstract: Cardiomyocyte ferroptosis contributes to myocardial ischemia/reperfusion injury, but the upstream noncoding RNA mechanisms remain incompletely defined. This study examined whether nuclear factor I B-derived circular RNA (circNFIB) regulates hypoxia/reoxygenation (H/R)-induced ferroptosis in human ventricular cardiomyocyte-derived AC16 cells and whether the miR-338-3p/GPX4 pathway contributes to this effect. The circNFIB back-splice junction was verified by Sanger sequencing. Cell viability, malondialdehyde, intracellular Fe2+, boron-dipyrromethene (BODIPY) 581/591 C11 oxidation, and glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4), acyl-CoA synthetase long-chain family member 4 (ACSL4), and transferrin receptor 1 (TfR1) protein abundance were evaluated. H/R decreased circNFIB expression, cell viability, and GPX4 abundance, while increasing lipid peroxidation, intracellular Fe2+ accumulation, and ACSL4 abundance; the reference ferroptosis inhibitor ferrostatin-1 partially reversed these changes. circNFIB overexpression improved cell viability, reduced intracellular Fe2+ accumulation and lipid peroxidation, partially restored GPX4 protein abundance, and lowered ACSL4 and TfR1 abundance. circNFIB was predominantly cytoplasmic. In reporter assays, miR-338-3p decreased the activity of reporters containing the wild-type circNFIB sequence or GPX4 3' untranslated region (3'UTR), whereas no significant reductions were observed with the corresponding mutant reporters. H/R increased miR-338-3p expression, whereas circNFIB overexpression reduced it. miR-338-3p overexpression aggravated the ferroptosis-associated phenotype and partially counteracted the protection associated with circNFIB overexpression. These findings indicate that circNFIB attenuates H/R-induced ferroptosis in AC16 cells, with the miR-338-3p/GPX4 pathway contributing to this effect.

articles.title: Revealing NMN-induced biomacromolecular complex and conformational regulation of digestive enzymes (Trypsin, Pepsin, α-Amylase): Insights from molecular dynamics simulation and multi-spectroscopy.
articles.abstract: Nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN), a key Nicotinamideadeninedinucleotide (NAD+) precursor, has attracted attention for anti-aging potential. As an oral bioactive molecule, NMN inevitably interacts with digestive enzymes in the gastrointestinal tract, which may affect its bioavailability, stability and physiological function. Nevertheless, the interactions between NMN and digestive enzymes have not been systematically characterized. This study investigated NMN binding with three digestive enzymes (trypsin, pepsin, and α-amylase) using multi-spectroscopic techniques, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. Fluorescence quenching analysis showed NMN induced static quenching of all three enzymes through spontaneous binding. Thermodynamic analysis indicated hydrophobic interactions, supplemented by hydrogen bonding, as primary driving forces. Molecular docking demonstrated NMN was embedded in the hydrophobic cavity and stabilized with the surrounding residues through hydrogen bonds and hydrophobic interaction. Synchronous fluorescence, UV-Vis absorption, circular dichroism (CD), and resonance light scattering (RLS) analyses showed NMN altered aromatic residue microenvironments and induced conformational rearrangements. MD simulations confirmed structural stabilization of NMN-enzyme complexes, particularly the NMN-pepsin system, exhibiting the lowest root mean square deviation (RMSD) and smaller radius of gyration (Rg). Functional assays revealed concentration-dependent inhibition of digestive enzyme activities, with pepsin showing strongest susceptibility. Additionally, antioxidant capacities decreased after complex formation, while anti-inflammatory activity was enhanced. These findings provide mechanistic insights into the interaction between NMN and digestive enzymes under in vitro conditions, which is helpful in clarifying the roles of NMN in digestion, transport, and metabolism processes. They have significant guiding significance for drug design and development.

articles.title: Celastrol induces lipid-associated stress and apoptosis in EBV-positive extranodal NK/T-cell lymphoma with NCOR2-HDAC3 perturbation.
articles.abstract: Epstein-Barr virus (EBV)-positive extranodal natural killer/T-cell lymphoma (ENKTL) remains difficult to treat after relapse or refractory progression. We investigated celastrol-associated chromatin, lipid-metabolic, and stress responses in ENKTL cell-line models. Celastrol reduced SNK6 and SNT8 cell viability, increased apoptotic protein processing, and suppressed short-term SNK6 xenograft growth with increased histological markers of apoptosis. Chemical proteomics identified nuclear receptor corepressor 2 (NCOR2) and nuclear receptor corepressor 1 (NCOR1) among celastrol-associated proteins, and pull-down immunoblotting confirmed NCOR2 recovery. Probe recovery mapped to an NCOR2 region containing the deacetylase activation domain. Celastrol altered NCOR2 thermal stability, reduced its co-immunoprecipitation with histone deacetylase 3 (HDAC3), and inhibited recombinant HDAC3/NCOR2 activity. Histone H3 lysine 27 acetylation (H3K27ac) profiling at 2 h and RNA sequencing at 24 h revealed chromatin redistribution and associated stress-response and lipid-metabolic transcriptional changes. Selected apoptotic, lipid-metabolic, and stress-response protein changes were reproduced in SNT8 cells. In SNK6 cells, the HDAC3 inhibitor RGFP966 partially phenocopied selected celastrol-associated changes. NCOR2 depletion reduced lipid-metabolic enzyme expression and enhanced apoptotic-marker accumulation during celastrol treatment, whereas oleic acid conjugated to bovine serum albumin partially attenuated stress and apoptotic responses. Bulk RNA sequencing showed no coordinated induction of the examined EBV lytic-associated transcripts. These findings identify NCOR2-HDAC3-associated perturbation and lipid-associated stress as components of the celastrol response in EBV-positive ENKTL models.

articles.title: A practical framework to predict human hepatic clearance for Extended Clearance Classification System class 1B acidic and zwitterionic drugs.
articles.abstract: The Extended Clearance Classification System (ECCS) predicts predominant systemic clearance mechanisms of small-molecule drugs based on molecular weight, ionization, and permeability. Highly permeable acids and zwitterions with a molecular weight exceeding 400 Da (ECCS class 1B) are expected to rely on transporter-mediated hepatic uptake. For this class, human hepatic clearance is frequently underpredicted when extrapolated from in vitro metabolic stability, complicating prospective pharmacokinetic predictions. Here, we systematically evaluated the performance of metabolism-based intrinsic hepatic clearance predictions using curated clinical intravenous pharmacokinetic data for 16 ECCS class 1B drugs. Although approximately 70% of compounds were predicted within 3-fold of observed values, clinically meaningful underprediction persisted for a subset (atorvastatin, bosentan, pitavastatin, lovastatin acid, and telmisartan). To prospectively identify compounds at risk of >3-fold underprediction, we compared 4 approaches: (1) rat in vitro-in vivo correlation (IVIVC), (2) nonhuman primate (NHP) IVIVC, (3) IVIVC in chimeric mice with humanized livers (PXB-mice), and (4) measurement of the fraction of active uptake in suspended human hepatocytes. Rat IVIVC reliably identified compounds scaling adequately in humans but showed lower discriminatory power to identify compounds with >3-fold underprediction. In contrast, a human hepatocyte active uptake fraction >50% robustly identified the compounds with human hepatic clearance underprediction. NHP and PXB-mouse IVIVC provided lower discriminatory power. For compounds flagged to be at risk of >3-fold underprediction by the hepatic uptake assay, incorporation of measured hepatic uptake clearance into scaling quantitatively improved human clearance predictions, achieving accuracy comparable to single-species NHP allometric scaling. SIGNIFICANCE STATEMENT: Accurate clearance prediction for Extended Clearance Classification System class 1B drugs is complicated by transporter-mediated hepatic uptake, which can cause substantial underprediction when scaling from metabolic stability. This work introduces a practical decision framework combining rat in vitro-in vivo correlation and human hepatocyte uptake screening to identify compounds at risk of >3-fold clearance underprediction. For the identified compounds, uptake-informed scaling improves human pharmacokinetic predictions, reduces uncertainty during lead optimization, and lowers reliance on nonhuman primates in drug discovery.

articles.title: Population Pharmacokinetic/Pharmacodynamic Analysis of HHT120, a Novel Direct Thrombin Inhibitor, in Healthy Participants from a Phase I Clinical Trial.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: HHT120 is a novel orally administrable direct thrombin inhibitor. In this study, the pharmacokinetic (PK) profiles of HHT120 and its active metabolite Rn-001 were investigated in a first-in-human study and further analyzed with modeling approaches. METHODS: Population pharmacokinetic (PopPK) model and pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) model were developed to describe the dose-exposure-response relationship after HHT120 administration. Furthermore, the activated partial thromboplastin time (APTT) under different dosing regimens was performed to evaluate the anticoagulant effect. RESULTS: In total, 74 healthy participants were involved in the dataset involving single ascending dose (SAD), multiple ascending dose (MAD) as well as food effect (FE) phases, and 918 observations of HHT120 concentration as well as 1697 observations of Rn-001 were collected. A total number of 1314 APTT observations were obtained from 62 subjects excluding FE phase. An Erlang model with 7 transit compartments was utilized in the PopPK model to capture the production of Rn-001, and a three-compartment model was employed to describe the disposition. Covariates were screened on the PK parameters in a stepwise style, and no significant covariate effect was found in the current model. Besides, the relationship of plasma concentration of Rn-001 and APTT was characterized by a direct effect with a mixture of linear and nonlinear models. Simulations showed that HHT120 administered once daily at 100-300 mg or twice daily at 100-200 mg led to an increase of APTT within 2-fold of the upper limit, suggesting good safety profiles of HHT120 in the simulated dose regimens. CONCLUSIONS: The PopPK/PD model offers evidence for the efficacy and safety properties of HHT120 and are expected to provide valuable insights for subsequent clinical research and development of HHT120. TRIAL REGISTRATION: China Drug Trials Registry ( https://www.chinadrugtrials.org.cn ) identifier no. CTR20221837.

articles.title: Systemic mitochondrial injection protects against methanol-induced optic neuropathy through restoration of mitochondrial function and attenuation of oxidative stress.
articles.abstract: Methanol poisoning can cause severe and irreversible optic neuropathy, for which effective neuroprotective strategies remain limited. Mitochondrial dysfunction is important contributors to methanol-induced neuronal injury. Therefore, this study evaluated whether systemic mitochondrial injection could attenuate methanol-induced optic nerve injury. Adult rats were randomly assigned to control, methanol, methanol + single mitochondrial injection, and methanol + double mitochondrial injection groups. Following methanol intoxication, freshly isolated functional mitochondria (250 µg/kg) were administered intravenously. Motor and visual functions were evaluated using the beam walking and visual cliff tests. Mitochondrial dysfunction was assessed by flow cytometric analysis of mitochondrial membrane potential (MMP) and reactive oxygen species (ROS) production. Oxidative stress was assessed by measuring reduced glutathione (GSH) and malondialdehyde (MDA), and optic nerve histopathology was also examined. Methanol exposure impaired motor coordination and visual performance (P < 0.05) and was associated with increased ROS formation (P < 0.001), lipid peroxidation (P < 0.01), MMP collapse (P < 0.001), and GSH depletion (P < 0.05), accompanied by histopathological alterations in the optic nerve. Mitochondrial injection attenuated these changes (P < 0.05) and improved functional and histopathological outcomes. Overall, the double mitochondrial injection was associated with a relatively greater improvement than the single administration in some of the evaluated parameters. Systemic mitochondrial injection attenuated methanol-associated mitochondrial and oxidative disturbances and was accompanied by improved behavioral and histopathological outcomes in this experimental model. Obtained finding in the current study support further investigations of mitochondrial-based approaches as potential strategies for methanol-induced optic neuropathy, while additional works are required to establish their underlying mechanisms, durability, and translational potential.

articles.title: A preliminary pharmacodynamic overview of objective measures of intoxication in regular and fast-acting cannabis edibles.
articles.abstract: RATIONALE: Existing research on biological markers of intoxication while under the influence of cannabis is expansive. We aimed to characterize these parameters across different commercially available products, such as cannabis edibles with both conventional and advanced delivery systems (i.e., fast-acting). Therefore, we sought to examine changes in blood pressure, heart rate, and temperature throughout the administration and intoxication associated with the consumption of a fast-acting cannabis edible, a standard cannabis edible, and a placebo edible. OBJECTIVES: We hypothesized that these biological markers would be significantly different throughout the time course of intoxication for the fast-acting and standard edible compared to the placebo edible. METHODS: 20 participants completed all 3 conditions of the within-subjects design. RESULTS: Post ingestion of the cannabis edibles, changes in blood pressure over time for the standard edible and the fast-acting edible indicated similar effects on blood pressure. Additionally, significant changes in heart rate were observed in both the standard edible condition and the fast-acting edible condition. We observed similar pharmacodynamic effects of cannabis consumption across both standard- and fast-acting edibles, with small but significant differences in blood pressure and heart rate across fast-acting and standard edibles. Heart rate was higher for participants at the onset of and across all conditions, including the placebo, and interestingly decreased over the course of the session. There were no significant differences in temperature across time or condition. CONCLUSIONS: These results provide insight to the biological effects of cannabis edibles, furthering our knowledge of physiological responses to cannabis edible products.

articles.title: Quercetin upregulates TLE4 to block the Wnt/β-catenin signaling pathway and inhibit cell migration and invasion of cervical cancer cells.
articles.abstract: METHODS: Using established TLE4-overexpression and CRISPR-Cas9-knockout cervical cancer cell lines and nude mouse tumorigenesis models, we verified the biological function and regulatory mechanism of TLE4 in cervical cancer. RESULTS: Quercetin treatment upregulated the expression of TLE4 in HeLa cells. Compared with normal cervical tissues from clinical specimens, the expression of TLE4 in the nucleus of cervical cancer tissues was significantly downregulated. Transwell assays showed that the migration and invasion of C-33A TLE4-overexpression cells were significantly suppressed, accompanied by an upregulation of the expression of E-cadherin and a downregulation of the expression of N-cadherin, Vimentin, and Snail. Conversely, the migration and invasion of Ca Ski TLE4-knockout cells were significantly enhanced, and the expressions of these EMT-related markers showed the opposite trend. Meanwhile, the in vivo xenograft experiment revealed that the Ca Ski TLE4-knockout group exhibited faster tumor growth compared with the wild-type group. Furthermore, we examined the role of TLE4 in the Wnt/β-catenin signaling pathway. In C-33A TLE4-overexpression cells, β-catenin, TCF-1, TCF-4, CyclinD1, c-Myc, and MMP-7 were decreased, p-β-catenin expression was increased, whereas in Ca Ski TLE4-knockout cells, the expression trends of these factors were opposite. After treating TLE4-knockout Ca Ski cells with quercetin, the enhanced migration and invasion capabilities induced by TLE4 knockout were effectively reversed. CONCLUSION: Quercetin targets and upregulates the expression of TLE4, which inhibits the migration and invasion of cervical cancer cells by blocking the Wnt/β-catenin signaling pathway, thereby providing theoretical and experimental evidence for quercetin therapy in cervical cancer.

articles.title: Tangeretin protects against nodularin-R-induced hepatotoxicity by modulating oxidative stress, inflammation, and apoptosis.
articles.abstract: Nodularin (NOD) is a cyanobacterial toxin that induces severe biochemical and structural alterations in the liver. This study aimed to investigate the protective effects of tangeretin (TAN) against NOD-R-induced hepatotoxicity by evaluating biochemical, oxidative stress, histopathological, and immunohistochemical alterations in a murine model. Fifty-six male mice were randomly allocated to four experimental groups (n = 14/group): Control, TAN, NOD-R, and TAN + NOD-R. The control, TAN, and NOD-R groups received intraperitoneal (i.p.) injections of 0.9% saline containing 0.1% dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO), TAN (100 mg/kg b.w., 0.9% saline 0.1% DMSO), and NOD-R (15 µg/kg b.w., 0.9% saline), respectively, for 7 consecutive days. The TAN + NOD-R group was administered TAN (100 mg/kg b.w.) for 10 consecutive days and concurrently challenged with NOD-R (15 µg/kg b.w.) from days 4 to 10. At the end of the experimental period, blood samples were collected for the determination of serum aminotransferase activities and oxidative stress parameters, while liver tissues were examined for oxidative stress biomarkers, histopathological alterations, and immunohistochemical expression of tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α), inducible nitric oxide synthase (iNOS), caspase - 3, and proliferating cell nuclear antigen (PCNA). NOD-R exposure significantly increased serum aminotransferase activities and malondialdehyde (MDA) levels and significantly decreased glutathione (GSH) levels and superoxide dismutase (SOD) concentrations, as well as catalase (CAT) and glutathione peroxidase (GSH-Px) activities. Moreover, NOD-R administration induced marked histopathological alterations and significantly increased hepatic expression of TNF-α, iNOS, caspase - 3, and PCNA. On the other hand, TAN pretreatment significantly alleviated NOD-R-induced hepatotoxicity by decreasing aminotransferase activities and MDA levels, restoring antioxidant defenses, attenuating histopathological changes, and downregulating the expression of TNF-α, iNOS, caspase - 3, and PCNA. The findings of this study indicated that TAN can be considered a protective agent against oxidative stress and NOD-R-induced hepatotoxicity.

articles.title: Mechanistic insights into the renoprotective effects of rutin-loaded selenium nanoparticles against 5-fluorouracil toxicity via regulation of Nrf2/Keap1, NF-κB/NLRP3, and PERK pathways.
articles.abstract: 5-Fluorouracil (5-FU) is a mainstay chemotherapeutic compound in the management of solid neoplasia; however, its clinical application is frequently restricted by significant nephrotoxicity. This study was performed to assess the renal protective impact of rutin (RUT), sodium selenite (Na₂SeO₃), and green-synthesized selenium nanoparticles (SeNPs) functionalized with rutin (RUT-SeNPs) in an animal model of 5-FU-provoked renal injury. Thirty-five rats were divided arbitrarily into 5 equal groups: normal control, 5-FU, 5-FU&Na₂SeO₃, 5-FU&RUT, and 5-FU&RUT-SeNPs. Application of 5-FU caused pronounced renal dysfunction, characterized by marked elevations in conventional and early kidney injury biomarkers, profound oxidative stress, activation of inflammatory signaling routes including NF-κB, and stimulation of apoptotic cascades, together with depletion of endogenous antioxidant defenses. Although treatment with RUT or Na₂SeO₃ afforded partial renal protection, RUT-SeNPs demonstrated superior efficacy by markedly attenuating functional, oxidative, inflammatory, and apoptotic derangements and restoring antioxidant homeostasis toward physiological levels. These biological and molecular findings were substantiated by histopathological and immunohistochemical analyses, which revealed preservation of renal architecture and a significant reduction in inflammatory and apoptotic lesions. Collectively, these results highlight RUT-SeNPs as a promising nanotherapeutic approach for alleviating 5-FU-induced nephrotoxicity.

articles.title: Barrier model selection alters apparent diclofenac permeation parameters: a controlled in vitro comparison of Strat-M® and a HaCaT-based epidermal construct.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Synthetic membranes and keratinocyte-based constructs are both used as accessible alternatives to ex vivo skin in in vitro permeation testing (IVPT), but they have not been compared directly for the same marketed products under identical conditions. This pilot study directly compared the synthetic Strat-M® membrane and a HaCaT construct under identical IVPT conditions using Voltaren® and Olfen®, two marketed, nominally dose-equivalent diclofenac gels. The aim was to determine whether the two barrier models yielded consistent apparent permeation parameters and led to the same comparative interpretation of the two formulations. METHODS: Permeation studies were performed using Franz diffusion cells in an internally controlled experimental design. Both formulations were tested in triplicate under identical conditions, including receptor medium, temperature, sampling protocol, and analytical method. Steady-state flux (Jss), permeability coefficient (Kp), lag time (tlag), and cumulative permeation profiles were determined and compared between barrier models. RESULTS: Barrier model selection affected the apparent permeation behavior of diclofenac. Strat-M® detected a statistically significant difference in steady-state flux between Voltaren® and Olfen®, whereas no statistically significant between-formulation difference was detected with the HaCaT construct under the same experimental conditions. Lag time was the parameter most strongly influenced by barrier selection and was consistently shorter with the HaCaT construct than with Strat-M®. DISCUSSION: Under identical IVPT conditions, Strat-M® and the HaCaT-based epidermal construct generated different apparent permeation profiles and yielded different comparative assessments of Voltaren® and Olfen®. This model-dependent divergence underscores the need to justify barrier selection explicitly and to consider its limitations when interpreting comparative IVPT data.

articles.title: Luteolin protects against cholestasis by suppressing hepatocyte apoptosis through direct PI3K binding and AKT activation.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Excessive hepatocyte apoptosis triggered by toxic bile acids is the core pathological event of cholestasis, and the direct target of luteolin (Lut), the major bioactive constituent of Siphonostegia chinensis Benth., for this protective effect remains unclear. This study aims to elucidate how Lut suppresses hepatocyte apoptosis and ameliorates cholestatic liver injury. METHODS: A murine cholestasis model was induced by α-naphthylisothiocyanate (ANIT), and the hepatocyte apoptotic pathways were validated in glycochenodeoxycholic acid (GCDCA)-treated HepG2 cells. Liver tissue pathological changes were assessed via hematoxylin-eosin (HE) histological staining. Network pharmacology paired with supplementary RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) was used to screen candidate pathways contributing to Lut's anti-cholestatic effects. Quantitative real-time PCR, Western blotting and Terminal deoxynucleotidyl transferase dUTP nick-end labeling (TUNEL) immunostaining were jointly utilized to assess apoptotic levels in liver parenchymal cells. Additionally, surface plasmon resonance (SPR) coupled with molecular docking simulations was adopted to clarify the direct binding profile of Lut. RESULTS: Lut treatment markedly ameliorated serum biochemical indices and liver histopathological lesions in ANIT-exposed mice. Meanwhile, oxidative stress was alleviated, bile acid transporters were restored, inflammatory cytokines declined, and hepatocyte apoptosis was suppressed. Network pharmacology combined with RNA-seq predicted that Lut alleviates cholestasis through the Phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase/Protein Kinase B (PI3K/AKT)-mediated anti-apoptotic pathway. This hypothesis was further supported by TUNEL, Western blotting, and qRT-PCR analyses, which indicated that Lut could activate the PI3K/AKT, and then suppress hepatocyte apoptosis in cholestasis. SPR analysis revealed a concentration-dependent direct interaction between Lut and PI3K with a kinetic KD of 9.036 × 10-5 M, and molecular docking revealed a plausible binding mode within the kinase domain. Additionally, the anti-apoptotic effect of Lut was largely abolished when PI3K was inhibited by LY294002 in vitro. CONCLUSION: This study is the first to confirm that Lut directly targets PI3K to initiate the PI3K/AKT signaling cascade, and thereby suppresses bile acid-induced hepatocyte apoptosis. These findings refine the mechanistic understanding of Lut's hepatoprotective action from general antioxidant activity to target-specific anti-apoptotic signaling, and provide a molecular explanation for the traditional use of S. chinensis Benth. for the treatment of damp-heat jaundice.

articles.title: Fe-doped polydopamine pickering emulsion as a nanoplatform for synergistic photothermal-ferroptosis immunotherapy in breast cancer.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Triple-negative breast cancer remains a formidable clinical challenge owing to its immunosuppressive microenvironment and inherently low immunogenicity. METHODS: To address this, we developed a multifunctional Pickering emulsion (Fe-PDA-PE-R837) stabilized by iron-doped polydopamine (Fe-PDA) nanoparticles, which function dually as photothermal agents and localized iron donors, while the soybean oil core encapsulates the immunoadjuvant R837. The Fe-PDA nanoparticles exhibited uniform spherical morphology, excellent colloidal stability, and a broad absorption band extending to the NIR region. Upon 808 nm laser irradiation, the Fe-PDA shell generates local hyperthermia with a photothermal conversion efficiency of 38.5%, disrupts intracellular iron homeostasis to provoke ferroptotic cell death, as evidenced by GSH depletion and MDA accumulation, while the stimuli-responsive release of R837 coupled with immunogenic cell death (ICD) elicits potent local and systemic pro-inflammatory responses. RESULTS: In vitro assays demonstrated that the combination treatment achieved ∼80% cell killing, markedly inhibited cell migration, and significantly upregulated TNF-α and IL-12 secretion. In vivo evaluation using the 4T1 murine breast cancer model confirmed that this nanoplatform significantly suppressed primary tumor growth and pulmonary metastasis, with no appreciable systemic toxicity. DISCUSSION: Collectively, this interfacial engineering strategy underscores the promising translational potential of Pickering emulsion-based nanoplatforms for aggressive solid tumor therapy.

articles.title: Isoalantolactone exhibits activity against Echinococcus multilocularis associated with mitochondrial perturbation and changes in the lesion microenvironment.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Alveolar echinococcosis (AE) is a severe parasitic disease caused by Echinococcus multilocularis. Current therapy relies mainly on benzimidazole drugs and is largely parasitostatic, highlighting the urgent need for new candidate compounds with improved efficacy. We hypothesized that isoalantolactone (ISO) exerts direct anti-Echinococcus multilocularis activity and evaluated whether ISO treatment was associated with changes in the lesion microenvironment and host immune responses during AE progression in vivo. METHODS: In vitro experiments were conducted using isolated Echinococcus multilocularis protoscoleces, metacestode vesicles, and germinal layer cells, with assessments of protoscolex survival, phosphoglucose isomerase release, and germinal cell viability. Scanning and transmission electron microscopy, mitochondrial membrane potential detection, molecular docking, and protein expression analysis were also performed. In vivo efficacy was verified using a murine intraperitoneal infection model treated with ISO or albendazole, combined with evaluations of lesion burden, histopathology, safety indicators, immune cell subsets, and cytokine levels. RESULTS: ISO promoted phosphoglucose isomerase release, with a half-maximal effective concentration of 16.36 ± 3.24 μM, and reduced germinal cell viability, with a half-maximal inhibitory concentration of 17.46 ± 2.25 μM. It exerted dose- and time-dependent parasiticidal effects, achieving complete protoscolex death within 1-5 days at concentrations of 40 μM and 10 μM, respectively. In infected mice, ISO reduced lesion burden and spleen index and was associated with parasite structural damage, mitochondrial abnormalities, and changes in fibrosis-, inflammation-, and immune-related readouts under the present experimental conditions, with no marked abnormalities in most of the evaluated short-term safety parameters. CONCLUSION: ISO shows anti-Echinococcus multilocularis activity in vitro and suppresses AE progression in vivo. Its activity was associated with parasite structural injury, mitochondrial membrane potential depolarization, and changes in the lesion microenvironment and host immune responses. Further preclinical evaluation of ISO as a candidate compound against AE is warranted.

articles.title: P2X7 receptor contributes to hepatic inflammation and collagen deposition in methionine- and choline-deficient diet-fed mice.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Metabolic-Dysfunction-Associated Steatohepatitis (MASH) is characterized by hepatic steatosis, inflammation, and progressive liver injury, with growing evidence implicating purinergic signaling and inflammasome activation in disease progression. Here, we investigated the role of the P2X7 receptor and caspase-1/11 signaling in methionine- and choline-deficient (MCD) diet-induced liver injury in mice. METHODS: Mice were fed an MCD diet to induce liver injury, and hepatic steatosis, inflammation, and tissue injury were assessed by histopathological analysis. Hepatic triacylglycerol and cholesterol accumulation, Il1b mRNA expression, and IL-1β protein levels were evaluated. The hepatic expression profile of purinergic receptors, including P2Y1, P2Y4, P2Y6, P2Y12, and P2Y14, was also investigated in wild-type and P2X7- and/or caspase-1/11-deficient mice. RESULTS: MCD diet feeding induced significant weight loss and marked histopathological alterations, including hepatic steatosis, inflammatory infiltrates, and hepatocellular injury, accompanied by increased hepatic triacylglycerol and cholesterol accumulation. Hepatic injury was partially dependent on caspase-1/11 signaling, whereas hepatic inflammation was partially dependent on the P2X7 receptor. Although Il1b mRNA expression increased following MCD diet feeding, this increase was significant only in wild-type mice, whereas increased IL-1β protein levels were observed only in wild-type animals, suggesting that P2X7 receptor signaling and caspase-1/11 may contribute to IL-1β maturation during MCD diet-induced liver injury. In addition, MCD diet feeding promoted marked remodeling of the hepatic purinergic profile, characterized by downregulation of P2Y1 and P2Y4 receptors and genotype-dependent regulation of P2Y12, whereas P2Y6 and P2Y14 expression remained largely unchanged. DISCUSSION: Together, these findings demonstrate that the P2X7 receptor and caspase-1/11 play a role in amplifying inflammatory responses and reshaping the hepatic purinergic microenvironment during steatohepatitis progression, highlighting the P2X7 receptor as a potential therapeutic target in chronic liver disease.

articles.title: Third-generation EGFR-TKI plus pemetrexed-platinum chemotherapy versus TKI monotherapy as first-line treatment for EGFR-mutant lung adenocarcinoma with brain parenchymal metastases.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of first-line third-generation EGFR-tyrosine kinase inhibitor (EGFR-TKI) combined with pemetrexed-platinum chemotherapy in patients with EGFR-mutant advanced lung adenocarcinoma and brain parenchymal metastases. METHODS: A bicenter retrospective cohort study was conducted. A total of 150 eligible patients were enrolled and balanced by 1:1 propensity score matching. Tumor response, survival outcomes, and treatment-related adverse events were compared between groups. RESULTS: After matching, 60 patients were assigned to each group. The intracranial objective response rate was 78.3% in the combination group versus 61.7% in the monotherapy group (P = 0.046). The median intracranial progression-free survival was 28.3 months in the combination group (hazard ratio = 0.536, 95% confidence interval: 0.350-0.820, P = 0.002). Systemic progression-free survival and overall survival were also significantly prolonged in the combination arm. Adverse events were predominantly chemotherapy-related toxicities and were generally manageable. CONCLUSION: First-line third-generation EGFR-TKI plus pemetrexed-platinum chemotherapy is associated with superior intracranial and systemic survival benefits in EGFR-mutant lung adenocarcinoma patients with brain parenchymal metastases, with a favorable safety profile. This study provides real-world evidence to support clinical treatment decision-making.

articles.title: Phenolic-enriched ethanol-soluble fraction of Codonopsis pilosula attenuates LPS-induced acute lung injury in mice via the gut-lung axis.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Codonopsis pilosula (Dangshen), a traditional Chinese medicine targeting the Lung Meridian, is commonly steeped in 50% (alcohol by volume) distilled spirits (Baijiu) in China as a medicinal liquor for protecting against lung diseases, including acute lung injury (ALI). This alcohol-steeping preparation yields an ethanol-soluble fraction with a distinct phytochemical profile from conventional aqueous extracts. However, its bioactive compounds and the underlying protective mechanisms against ALI remain unclear. OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to characterize the bioactive compounds of the ethanol-soluble fraction of C. pilosula (designated as CPPP) and investigate its protective mechanisms against lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced ALI in mice. METHODS: CPPP was characterized by non-targeted metabolomic profiling and targeted quantitative analysis using UPLC-ESI-MS/MS, performed sequentially to achieve comprehensive metabolite coverage and precise quantification of identified constituents. Male C57BL/6J mice were pretreated with CPPP for 30 days prior to intraperitoneal injection of LPS to induce ALI. Comprehensive assessments included 16S rRNA sequencing of the gut microbiota, untargeted metabolomic profiling of feces and serum, enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) quantification of serum inflammatory factors and LPS, histological evaluation and immunohistochemistry (IHC) analysis of gut and lung tissues. RESULTS: CPPP was enriched in phenolic acids and derivatives (25.3%, w/w). Compared to the normal control, CPPP significantly (P < 0.05) enriched beneficial gut bacteria Clostridium, Bifidobacterium and Akkermansia. CPPP increased fecal levels of butyric acid, serotonin and spermidine, elevated serum level of serotonin, and reduced serum levels of trimethylamine N-oxide, phenylacetylglycine, and phenylacetylglutamine. CPPP significantly (P < 0.001) decreased the levels of LPS-induced pro-inflammatory factors in serum (CRP, TNF-α, IL-6) and lung tissue (MPO, TNF-α, IL-1β, IL-6, IL-18), while increasing the level of anti-inflammatory IL-10 in serum (P < 0.001) and lung tissue (P < 0.01). These anti-inflammatory effects of CPPP, together with the microbiota-derived metabolic alterations, correlated strongly with the CPPP-mediated preservation of intestinal barrier parameters (villus height, goblet cell density, and tight junction protein expression) and attenuation of lung injury parameters (pulmonary inflammation, edema, and histopathological damage). CONCLUSION: CPPP attenuated LPS-induced ALI in mice by remodeling gut microbiota, reprogramming key metabolites and suppressing pro-inflammatory factors along the gut-lung axis. These findings validate the lung-protective potential of phenolic compounds from traditional alcohol-steeping preparation of C. pilosula and provide mechanistic insights for developing microbiota-targeted interventions in inflammatory lung diseases.

articles.title: A mixture of pomegranate peels and propolis extracts reduces inflammation associated with rheumatoid arthritis in vivo.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic condition characterized by the infiltration of immune and inflammatory cells into the synovial membranes, which often leads to severe damage to cartilage and bone. In spite of their efficacy, drug-based therapies produce severe side effects. Therefore, there remains an unmet need for non-pharmacological treatments with a low toxicity profile and limited costs. Propolis has been used since ancient times for the treatment of wounds, ulcers, infections, eczemas, myalgia, and rheumatism. Similarly, the traditional use of all parts of pomegranate (Punica granatum L.) is documented across Egyptian, Persian, and Chinese cultures for the treatment of infections and inflammations. PURPOSE: This study aimed at the development of preparations containing bioactive compounds derived from propolis and pomegranate peels, inspired by traditional recipes used in rural areas of southern Italy, to validate their efficacy in counteracting the inflammation associated with RA. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A preliminary screening led to the selection of the most promising preparation, composed by propolis and pomegranate peel extracts in a ratio 1:2 (Pp1:2). It underwent a complete chemical characterization by both qualitative and quantitative LC-MS analyses and was tested on a collagen-induced arthritis (CIA) mouse model. RESULTS: In vitro tests showed that Pp1:2 treatment of M1 stimulated by LPS/IFNγ reduces cell polarization; furthermore, it reverts the pro-inflammatory effects induced by IL-1β on synoviocytes. In vivo experiments, conducted by administering Pp1:2 orally to a suitable murine model, confirmed the ability of the preparation to reduce sensibly RA-like inflammatory effects, as inferred by the change observed in mice paws volume and other RA-related parameters. Furthermore, histological analyses revealed a reduction in the number of M1 macrophages in mice paws following Pp1:2 treatment, and an attenuation of the pathological remodeling of collagen IV and of ICAM-1 expression, compared to untreated controls.

articles.title: The untapped potential of oral vitamin E in lichen sclerosus: from immunobiology to real-life clinical experience.
articles.abstract: Lichen sclerosus (LS) is a chronic dermatosis characterized by persistent inflammation, progressive fibrosis, and an elevated risk of vulvar squamous cell carcinoma. While ultra-potent topical corticosteroids remain the gold standard of care, the necessity for long-term maintenance therapy raises concerns regarding cumulative toxicity, underscoring the critical need for adjunctive therapies that target underlying pathogenic mechanisms. Vitamin E, traditionally recognized for its antioxidant and membrane-protective properties, has emerged as a promising candidate due to its broad immunomodulatory effects, including its regulatory impact on innate and adaptive immunity and its anti-inflammasome activity. However, the available clinical evidence remains limited to topical formulations, and corresponding efficacy data are scarce. In this Perspective article, we critically analyze the current clinical evidence on oral vitamin E in LS, delineate its immunological mechanisms, and incorporate insights from real-world clinical practice at a tertiary referral center, which should be interpreted as hypothesis-generating given the observational, uncontrolled design. Furthermore, we explore the potential of oral vitamin E formulations, address the pharmacokinetic challenges associated with conventional delivery, and propose future research avenues-such as optimized delivery systems and active metabolite formulations-to fully elucidate the therapeutic role of oral vitamin E in LS management.

articles.title: Astragaloside IV attenuates ferroptosis-related testicular injury in rats with experimental varicocele.
articles.abstract: Varicocele is an important correctable cause of male infertility. Oxidative stress and lipid peroxidation contribute to the associated testicular injury, but the role of ferroptosis remains controversial. Astragaloside IV (AS-IV), a quality-control metabolite of Astragali radix, has antioxidant activity and can modulate ferroptosis-related processes, yet its effect in varicocele is unclear. This study evaluated whether AS-IV attenuates testicular injury in experimental varicocele and examined ferroptosis-related mechanisms. A Sprague-Dawley rat model was established by partial ligation of the left renal vein and treated with oral AS-IV; Ferrostatin-1 served as a pharmacological comparator. Label-free proteomics, histopathology, biochemical assays and targeted molecular analyses were combined with a TM4 Sertoli-cell model of RSL3-induced injury. AS-IV lessened tubular injury and improved Johnsen scores in a dose-related manner, reduced testicular Fe2+, ROS and MDA, and raised the GSH/GSSG ratio. Proteomics showed partial reversal of lipid-metabolism and ferroptosis-related enrichment after AS-IV. These changes were accompanied by recovery of androgen receptor (AR) and MBOAT2. In TM4 cells, AS-IV improved viability and lowered C11-BODIPY oxidation after RSL3; enzalutamide weakened the effects of AS-IV on lipid peroxidation and MBOAT2 and only partly reduced the viability rescue. The findings provide experimental evidence that AS-IV ameliorates varicocele-related testicular injury and that AR/MBOAT2-related signalling may participate.

articles.title: Anti-Nectin4 monoclonal antibodies attenuate airway inflammation and epithelial barrier dysfunction in asthma.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Nectin4 is an epithelial cell-adhesion molecule that may be involved in airway inflammatory responses. However, the effects of Nectin4 targeting in asthma has not yet been investigated. METHODS: Here we engineered anti-Nectin4 monoclonal antibody, N-1T1C8Ab or N-1T3H9Ab, their effects on airway epithelial dysfunction and inflammation. Dermatophagoides pteronyssinus 1 (Der p 1)-stimulated normal human bronchial epithelial (NHBE) cells and ovalbumin-induced asthmatic BALB/c mice were used as experimental models. RESULTS: Anti-Nectin4 antibody treatment restored epithelial barrier dysfunction and was associated with changes in IL-33-related, MyD88/IRAK, and Afadin/Rac1 signaling in NHBE cells. In the murine asthma model, administration of N-1T1C8Ab or N-1T3H9Ab reduced airway inflammation, airway resistance, and immune cell infiltration in bronchoalveolar lavage fluid. Histological analysis demonstrated decreased inflammatory cell infiltration, goblet cell hyperplasia, and fibrosis in lung tissues. Anti-Nectin4 antibody treatment was also associated with modulation of IL-33/MyD88-related signaling components. CONCLUSION: These findings indicate that anti-Nectin4 monoclonal antibodies attenuate airway inflammation and improve epithelial barrier function. Further preclinical studies are warranted to determine the potential of Nectin4 targeting in asthma.

articles.title: Cost-effectiveness of aficamten for obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy: a model-based analysis from the perspective of the Chinese healthcare system.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: To evaluate the cost-effectiveness of aficamten plus standard of care (SoC) versus SoC alone for patients with symptomatic obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (oHCM) from the perspective of the Chinese healthcare system. METHODS: A four-state Markov model based on the phase III SEQUOIA-HCM trial was developed to simulate lifetime outcomes. The first 24 weeks were modeled using trial data, followed by 4-week cycles for long-term extrapolation. Based on FOREST-HCM, the incremental treatment effect of aficamten was assumed to persist through week 96 and then linearly wane to complete loss by year 3. Costs and health outcomes were discounted at 4.5% annually. Model uncertainty was assessed using one-way sensitivity analysis, probabilistic sensitivity analysis, and scenario analyses. RESULTS: Total costs were US$143,281.22 with aficamten plus SoC and US$96,509.03 with SoC alone, with 9.696 and 7.643 QALYs, respectively. Aficamten plus SoC yielded an incremental cost of US$46,772.19 and 2.054 QALYs, corresponding to an ICER of US$22,775.17/QALY, below the WTP threshold of US$29,399.70/QALY. The probability of being cost-effective was 76.6% at the WTP threshold. Scenario analyses showed ICERs of US$19,351.77/QALY when only short-term effects were considered, US$43,752.42/QALY when treatment effects disappeared in year 5, and US$81,220.72/QALY when they disappeared in year 10. Price reductions of 22.0% and 50.5%, respectively, were required in the latter two scenarios. With a permanent discontinuation probability of 0.131% per 4-week cycle, the ICER was US$23,888.94/QALY. CONCLUSION: From the Chinese healthcare system perspective, aficamten plus SoC was cost-effective versus SoC alone for symptomatic oHCM under the base-case assumptions.

articles.title: Comparative real-world pharmacovigilance analysis of adverse event signals associated with six approved CAR-T products using the FAERS database.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Although several CAR-T products have been approved for hematologic malignancies, their post-marketing adverse-event reporting patterns may not be interchangeable. This study compared FAERS-derived positive signals across approved CAR-T products to distinguish recurrent class-related toxicities from product-skewed reporting patterns. METHODS: FAERS reports from Q1 2014 to Q2 2025 were reviewed for CAR-T products. Demographic characteristics were summarized for seven products, whereas PT- and SOC-level signal analyses were restricted to six products with sufficient signal data: Breyanzi, Kymriah, Tecartus, Yescarta, Abecma, and Carvykti. Positive signals were detected using ROR, PRR, and BCPNN algorithms. After predefined exclusion of nonclinical or non-AE terms, indication- or disease-progression-related terms, procedure- or investigation-related terms, efficacy- or persistence-related terms, and product-quality-related terms, eligible signals were compared at the PT and SOC levels. Nonspecific MedDRA-coded PTs were retained if they met the predefined signal criteria, but they were interpreted descriptively and were not used to define product-level profile labels. RESULTS: CRS was consistently among the leading PT-level signals across all six products. Yescarta and Tecartus showed higher reporting of ICANS and neurotoxicity-related PTs. Kymriah was more strongly represented by infection-, immune-, and hematologic-related signals, whereas Carvykti showed several neurologic PTs including Parkinsonism, cranial nerve paralysis, facial paralysis, and Bell's palsy. Abecma showed relatively high-ranking systemic symptom-related PTs, including fatigue, headache, and decreased appetite. At the SOC level, nervous system disorders and infections and infestations were among the most frequently represented categories, but their proportions differed across products. CONCLUSION: FAERS-based signal detection showed a common CAR-T reporting backbone centered on CRS, ICANS/neurotoxicity, hypotension, pyrexia, infection-related events, and hematologic events, together with product-skewed signal patterns. These findings represent disproportionality signals rather than comparative safety rankings, and FAERS data cannot establish causal relationships between CAR-T products and adverse events.

articles.title: 5-HT2A receptor activation induces CB1-dependent presynaptic inhibitory long-term depression in the nucleus accumbens core.
articles.abstract: The serotonin 2A receptor (5-HT2A) is a Gq/11-coupled receptor implicated in reward processing, neuropsychiatric disorders, and the actions of serotonergic psychedelics. Although 5-HT2A activation has been shown to engage endocannabinoid (eCB) signaling in several brain regions, its role in inhibitory synaptic plasticity within the nucleus accumbens (NAc) remains poorly understood. Here, we investigated whether 5-HT2A activation modulates GABAergic synaptic transmission onto medium spiny neurons (MSNs) in the mouse NAc core. Using whole-cell patch-clamp recordings, we found that activation of 5-HT2A receptors with the selective agonist TCB-2 induced a robust inhibitory long-term depression (iLTD) of evoked GABAergic synaptic transmission. This depression was accompanied by reduced spontaneous and miniature IPSC frequency, increased paired-pulse ratio, and changes in coefficient of variation analysis consistent with a presynaptic reduction in GABA release probability. Mechanistically, iLTD was occluded by the CB1 receptor agonist WIN55,212-2 and blocked by the CB1 receptor antagonist AM251, supporting a critical role for endocannabinoid signaling. Furthermore, iLTD induction required postsynaptic G-protein signaling, phospholipase Cβ (PLCβ) activity, and synthesis of the endocannabinoid 2-arachidonoylglycerol (2-AG). Together, these findings demonstrate that 5-HT2A activation induces a CB1-dependent presynaptic iLTD through a postsynaptic PLCβ/2-AG signaling cascade. These results demonstrate that 5-HT2A receptor activation engages endocannabinoid signaling to regulate inhibitory synaptic transmission in the NAc, highlighting a mechanism through which 5-HT2A signaling may modulate mesolimbic circuit function.

articles.title: The pharmacokinetics and pharmacogenomics of voriconazole in pediatric Saudi patients: advancing toward precision medicine.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Voriconazole is a broad-spectrum triazole antifungal. It is used to prevent and treat invasive fungal infections in immunocompromised pediatric patients. Its clinical use is limited due to its nonlinear pharmacokinetics, high variability, and a narrow therapeutic index. Data on pharmacogenomic effects in pediatric patients are limited, particularly in the Saudi population. This study aimed to evaluate voriconazole pharmacokinetics in pediatric patients and to assess the impact of CYP2C19 genotypes on drug concentrations and clearance. METHODS: A prospective observational study was conducted from October 2022 to October 2024 at two tertiary care centers in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. Saudi pediatric patients aged between 1 and 14 years receiving voriconazole were enrolled after informed consent from guardians. Trough blood samples were collected on the fifth day of therapy and CYP2C19 genotyping (*2, *3, *17) was performed. The metabolizer status was assigned according to the Clinical Pharmacogenetics Implementation Consortium guidelines. RESULTS: Forty patients were included. The mean age was 67.7 ± 44.1 months, and the mean weight was 17.8 ± 9.5 kg CYP2C19 phenotypes were distributed as follows: normal metabolizers (65%), rapid metabolizers (17.5%), intermediate metabolizers (10%), and ultrarapid metabolizers (7.5%). No poor metabolizers were observed. The mean voriconazole trough concentration was 2.26 ± 2.68 mg/L and the majority (52.5%) of patients had subtherapeutic levels, 35% were within range, and 12.5% were supratherapeutic. In the multivariable analysis, only weight was significantly associated with clearance (R 2 = 0.14, P-value = 0.02), whereas genotype showed no significant effect (P-value = 0.48). CONCLUSION: Voriconazole trough concentrations showed considerable variability among pediatric patients. Thirty-five percent of patients achieved therapeutic trough concentrations at the first trough assessment and no statistically significant association between CYP2C19 polymorphisms and voriconazole trough concentrations was observed in this cohort. However, the small sample size may have limited the detection of genetic influences. These findings support the conclusion that individualized dosing is needed to optimize therapy.

articles.title: Risk prediction model for pegaspargase-associated severe coagulopathy and blood product costs: a single-center retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Pegaspargase-induced severe coagulopathy (SC) is a common complication in pediatric acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) treatment, yet reliable predictive tools are limited and its economic burden remains unclear. This study developed and internally validated a clinical prediction nomogram for SC, concurrently created a web-based calculator, and quantified the impact of coagulopathy on the cost of blood products. METHODS: Using retrospective data from 356 pediatric patients treated according to the Chinese Children's Leukemia Group Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia 2018 protocol at Hebei Children's Hospital between January 2020 and August 2025, SC was defined as grade 4 fibrinogen reduction or grade ≥3 prolongation of the activated partial thromboplastin time. A nomogram was developed via multivariate logistic regression, and cost drivers were analyzed by multiple linear regression. RESULTS: Hypoalbuminemia, elevated bilirubin, and elevated procalcitonin were independent predictors of SC. The nomogram achieved an area under the curve of 0.819 (95% CI: 0.773-0.864), and decision curve analysis indicated favorable clinical utility. Blood product cost was primarily driven by patient age, product type, and transfusion frequency (adjusted R 2 = 0.677). DISCUSSION: This study developed an accurate predictive model for SC and clarified the associated economic burden, providing evidence to support clinical vigilance and inform healthcare resource planning.

articles.title: Incremental Predictive Value of Dynamic Platelet-to-Lymphocyte Ratio Beyond ESR and CRP for Glucocorticoid Sparing in Rheumatoid Arthritis: A Multi-Center Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To identify independent predictors of sustained glucocorticoid (GC) sparing in patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) initiating biological or targeted synthetic disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (b/tsDMARDs), specifically we evaluated whether the longitudinal platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (ΔPLR) trajectory provides superior prognostic value compared to conventional measurements. METHODS: This multicenter retrospective study analyzed 264 patients from the Taipei Medical University Clinical Research Database. Sparing success was defined as achieving predefined dose reduction targets at month 6 and maintaining stability for ≥ 12 weeks. Candidate predictors were screened using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression, followed by multivariable logistic and Cox proportional hazards modeling. Clinical utility was assessed using "rescue rate" analysis. RESULTS: Sustained GC sparing was achieved by 139 (52.7%) patients. First-line b/tsDMARD initiation was the strongest predictor (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 4.23, p < 0.001) of GC-sparing success. Although static baseline inflammatory markers were non-predictive, every 10% reduction in 6-month ΔPLR independently increased success odds (aOR 1.05 [inverted from 0.95 per 10% increase], p = 0.009) and significantly accelerated the sparing rate (hazard ratio [HR] 1.02, p = 0.021). Conversely, concomitant nonsteroidal antiinflammatory drug use hindered success. Notably, incorporating ΔPLR into the predictive model "rescued" 16.5% of unrecognized candidates for de-escalation-patients capable of successful GC sparing who were misclassified by standard clinical models. CONCLUSION: Although static baseline inflammatory markers are nonpredictive, 6-month ΔPLR offers significant incremental prognostic value beyond conventional erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) and C-reactive protein (CRP). By identifying 16.5% of viable candidates overlooked by standard assessments, dynamic PLR monitoring offers a potential strategy to optimize precision steroid de-escalation in RA.

articles.title: Quality-by-Design-Guided Reactive Oxygen Species-Responsive Antimicrobial Nanotheranostics for Biofilm Eradication: A Translational Perspective.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Biofilm-associated infections remain a major therapeutic challenge due to extracellular polymeric substance (EPS) barriers, metabolic heterogeneity, and hypoxic microenvironments that limit antimicrobial penetration and efficacy. Antimicrobial nanotheranostics have emerged as multifunctional platforms that combine targeted drug delivery, diagnostic imaging, and stimuli-responsive therapeutic activation to overcome these barriers. SIGNIFICANCE OF REVIEW: Reactive oxygen species (ROS)-responsive and oxygen-modulating nanoplatforms represent a promising strategy for biofilm eradication by enhancing oxidative antibacterial activity and improving therapeutic penetration within complex biofilm environments. However, their clinical translation remains constrained by challenges related to reproducibility, scalability, safety, and regulatory compliance. This review addresses these limitations through the integration of Quality-by-Design (QbD) principles into antimicrobial nanotheranostic development. KEY FINDINGS: Recent advances in ROS-responsive and oxygen-regulating nanotheranostic systems are critically examined, with emphasis on the interdependence of hypoxia and ROS generation. The review highlights oxygen-carrying and oxygen-generating nanoplatforms, stimuli-responsive therapeutic strategies, and imaging-guided approaches for biofilm eradication. Furthermore, a QbD-based framework is presented, focusing on Quality Target Product Profiles (QTPPs), Critical Quality Attributes (CQAs), Critical Material Attributes (CMAs), and Critical Process Parameters (CPPs). Functional CQAs, including ROS generation kinetics, oxygen modulation efficiency, and biofilm penetration depth, are identified as key determinants of therapeutic performance and reproducibility. CONCLUSIONS: The integration of ROS-responsive nanotheranostics with QbD principles provides a rational strategy for developing clinically translatable antibiofilm therapies. Defining performance-linked quality attributes and robust design spaces can improve reproducibility, safety, scalability, and regulatory compliance, thereby accelerating the development of next-generation antimicrobial nanotheranostic systems for persistent biofilm-associated infections.

articles.title: Harnessing the Potential of Phospholipids as Pharmaceutical Excipients: A Versatile Platform for Customized Drug Delivery Systems.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: This review critically examines phospholipids as pharmaceutical excipients, focusing on physicochemical properties, self-assembly behavior, drug delivery applications, translational limitations, and future opportunities in customised therapeutics. SIGNIFICANCE OF REVIEW: Phospholipids have evolved from inert excipients into multifunctional materials that modulate drug stability, bioavailability, release kinetics, and targeted delivery. Their amphiphilic architecture enables diverse supramolecular systems-liposomes, lipid nanoparticles (LNPs), liquid crystalline depots, and hybrid polymer-lipid carriers-central to drug delivery. A narrative review evaluated preclinical, clinical, and industrial data on phospholipid chemistry, phase behaviour, nanocarrier architectures, oral bioavailability enhancement, biologics and nucleic acid delivery, oxidative stability, manufacturing scalability, and regulatory compliance, emphasising links between composition, structure, and in-vivo performance. KEY FINDINGS: Packing geometry influences self-assembly into lamellar, cubic, and hexagonal phases, shaping release behaviour across small molecules, biologics, and nucleic acids. PEGylated liposomes can substantially prolong systemic circulation relative to conventional formulations. Doxil and AmBisome demonstrate reductions in cardiotoxicity and nephrotoxicity, respectively. Ionizable lipid nanoparticles containing DSPC enable siRNA delivery in Patisiran and mRNA-vaccine delivery in Comirnaty, although their lipid compositions differ. Phospholipid-containing oral formulations may improve bioavailability of selected BCS Class II compounds through mixed-micelle solubilisation and lymphatic transport. Oxidative instability, anti-PEG immunogenicity, IVIVC limitations, and batch variability remain challenges, mitigated by antioxidants, saturated lipid substitution, and Raman monitoring. CONCLUSIONS: Phospholipids represent a programmable excipient platform used in numerous approved lipid-based drug products. Advances in synthetic lipid engineering, AI-guided design, and personalised medicine are expected to expand their impact across gene therapy, biologics, and long-acting therapeutics.

articles.title: Glycation stress in glioma: a metabolic vulnerability and therapeutic target.
articles.abstract: Gliomas are primary brain tumors characterized by genetic heterogeneity, metabolic reprogramming, and resistance to therapy, which collectively contribute to tumor progression and aggressive clinical behavior. Heightened aerobic glycolysis in these tumors is associated with altered glycolytic flux and dysregulated metabolic landscape. The ubiquitous dicarbonyl metabolite methylglyoxal (MGO) is a highly reactive glycating agent produced from glycolytic intermediates. MGO is a major precursor of advanced glycation end products (AGEs), and excessive AGE accumulation is associated with disruption of cellular homeostasis. Inhibitors of key bioenergetic pathways have shown potential in glioma, indicating that altered glycolysis may create metabolic vulnerabilities that influence tumor cell survival. In this context, increased glycolytic flux in glioma may provide a mechanistic link between glycation stress and tumor progression. This review discusses the influence of glycation stress in glioma biology and emphasize the importance of considering genetic heterogeneity, redox landscape, and metabolic comorbidities to better understand glycation burden and inform therapeutic strategies.

articles.title: DUSP6/MKP3 as an emerging therapeutic target in glioblastoma.
articles.abstract: The role of MKP family dual-specificity phosphatases (DUSPs) in oncogenesis, together with their potential as therapeutic targets in precision oncology, is now well established. These enzymes dephosphorylate both phosphotyrosine and phosphothreonine residues on extracellular signal-regulated kinase ERK1/2, thereby attenuating mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) signalling. DUSP6/MKP3 acts as a context-dependent regulator with tumour-suppressive or tumour-promoting roles across cancers. Glioblastoma (GBM), an aggressive primary brain tumour with dismal clinical outcomes, has shown limited response to both oncogene-targeted and immunotherapeutic approaches. DUSP6/MKP3 is frequently overexpressed in GBM and contributes to tumour growth, invasive behaviour, and treatment resistance. Computational analyses identify DUSP family genes, including DUSP6/MKP3, as recurrently dysregulated within GBM driver networks, supporting a central role in gliomagenesis. Here, we discuss DUSP6/MKP3 in glioblastoma, integrating transcriptional and cell-based evidence to define its molecular mechanisms and clinical relevance.

articles.title: Case Report: Fatal varicella-zoster virus meningoencephalitis with Froin-like cerebrospinal fluid and hydrocephalus following pembrolizumab-containing chemoimmunotherapy.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: In patients receiving immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs), central nervous system (CNS) infections may mimic or coexist with neurological immune-related adverse events (irAEs). ICI-driven immune dysregulation has been proposed to amplify inflammation against latent pathogens ("immunotherapy infections due to dysregulated immunity", ITI-DI), but this remains a hypothesis-generating framework rather than a validated diagnosis. CASE PRESENTATION: A 54-year-old man with stage IIIC lung adenocarcinoma developed a herpes zoster eruption and lumbosacral pain 7 days after the first infusion of pembrolizumab-containing chemoimmunotherapy, followed by rapidly progressive flaccid paraplegia, urinary incontinence, and declining consciousness. Intravenous acyclovir was not initiated until 20 days after rash onset. The first cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) sample was xanthochromic and coagulated spontaneously in the collection tube (Froin-like CSF), precluding protein measurement. A second lumbar puncture showed mild pleocytosis (8 cells/ μ  L; 70% neutrophils) and undetectable glucose; varicella-zoster virus (VZV) DNA was detected in CSF by post-mortem targeted polymerase chain reaction. Spinal Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) showed diffuse meningeal enhancement; follow-up cranial imaging showed acute hydrocephalus. Despite intravenous acyclovir, corticosteroids, and intravenous immunoglobulin, the patient died 43 days after pembrolizumab initiation. CONCLUSION: This case highlights VZV CNS infection as an important diagnostic consideration in ICI-treated patients who develop herpes zoster and neurological symptoms, because infection may mimic or coexist with a neurological irAE. The temporal relationship with pembrolizumab raises, but does not establish, the possibility that PD-1 blockade modified the inflammatory response. Prompt virological testing and adequately dosed antiviral therapy are central to management; the role of adjunctive immunomodulation remains uncertain and should be individualized.

articles.title: Epinephrine-mediated sensitization of thioredoxin 1 enhances chlorpromazine protection against acute hepatotoxicity.
articles.abstract: Acute liver injury (ALI) is characterised by rapid hepatic necrosis and compromised liver functions. Drug-induced ALI, in particular, is associated with glutathione depletion and overproduction of reactive oxygen species (ROS). These alterations highlight the contribution of the thioredoxin system (Trx/TrxR/NADPH) in preserving hepatic redox homeostasis. Previously, we demonstrated that thioredoxin-1 (Trx1) overexpression exerts protective effects against ischemic heart and peripheral vascular disease. Also, the neuroprotective role of thioredoxin reductase (TrxR1) has been reported in Parkinson's Disease. However, it remains unclear whether epinephrine (EP)-mediated boosting of the thioredoxin system, together with chlorpromazine (CPZ), provides sufficient protection against drug-induced ALI. To investigate this hypothesis, C57BL/6 mice were chronically administered a low dose of EP to enhance the expression of Trx1/TrxR1, followed by ALI induction with N-acetyl-para-aminophenol (APAP) and treatment with a subtoxic dose of CPZ. In parallel, hepatoma cell lines were treated with EP and/or CPZ to monitor the associated subcellular and molecular changes. The results showed that EP enhanced the expression of Trx1, thioredoxin-like protein 1 (TrxL1), and TrxR1 in liver and TrxR1 in hepatoma cell lines. Also, EP attenuated liver injury and enhanced the therapeutic effect of CPZ in ALI mice. A significant improvement in liver biomarkers, resolution of inflammation, attenuated oxidative stress, and restoration of hepatic histological architecture accompanied these observations. Moreover, activation of the thioredoxin system in hepatoma cells was associated with overexpression of β-arrestin1, TrxL1, and cAMP-response element-binding protein (CREB1), mirroring their involvement in Trx-mediated protection. Conclusively, these results addressed the protective role of boosting the cytosolic thioredoxin system in drug-induced ALI.

articles.title: The pan-African natural products library compounds oleanolic acid, poinsettifolin B, and rhuschalcone III disrupt SARS-CoV-2 spike-host ACE2 interactions and SARS-CoV-2 replication.
articles.abstract: Natural product (NP)-based chemical libraries are a rich source of antiviral compounds that can serve as the basis for new therapeutic leads to treat viral diseases, particularly for individuals lacking sustained access to existing vaccines and therapeutics. To identify new NP-based candidate inhibitors of SARS-CoV-2 cellular entry and viral replication, we screened the pan-African Natural Products Library (p-ANAPL), a collection of physical pure compounds obtained from African medicinal plants, for NPs that can disrupt the in vitro interaction of the SARS-CoV-2 Spike receptor-binding domain (RBD) with its host ACE2 entry receptor. This screen identified three compounds - oleanolic acid, poinsettifolin B, and rhuschalcone III - which disrupt RBD/ACE2 interactions with half-maximal inhibitory concentrations (IC50s) of 0.5-2.4 µM but do not disrupt an unrelated PD-1/PD-L1 host ligand/receptor binding pair. Oleanolic acid and rhuschalcone III, but not poinsettifolin B, additionally inhibited SARS-CoV-2 replication in Vero cells without cytotoxicity at low micromolar concentrations. Computational modelling indicated that all three compounds interact with numerous RBD and ACE2 residues, including a subset conserved across SARS-CoV-2 variants of concern. Taken together, we identify three NPs that selectively interfere with factors involved in SARS-CoV-2 entry and/or viral replication, representing new antiviral leads for COVID-19 management in resource-limited areas.

articles.title: Decoding Formulation Complexity: Comparative Performance of Statistical, Machine Learning, and Artificial Intelligence Models in Intelligent Nano Depot (iNDEP) Design.
articles.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) are increasingly explored to improve predictive modelling and optimization in pharmaceutical formulation development. This study compared predictive performance of conventional statistical approaches and AI/ML-based models using an experimentally generated dataset from PLGA-mPEG-based Intelligent Nano Depot (iNDEP), smart depot forming long-acting injectable system for sustained co-delivery of Memantine hydrochloride (MH) and Galantamine hydrobromide (GH). Central Composite Design (CCD) dataset of 17 experimental formulations were employed to develop predictive models. The % cumulative drug release (CDR), implant formation time and particle size were measured to determine effects of PLGA-mPEG, Span 80 and Tween 80. Design of Experiments (DoE), SPSS-based Multiple Linear Regression (MLR), Artificial Neural Networks (ANN) and ML workflows in Orange Data Mining and KNIME Analytics Platform were used to produce predictive models. Root mean squared error (RMSE), mean squared error (MSE), and coefficient of determination (R2) were used to evaluate model performance. Models developed using DoE were good fit with R2 values ranging from 0.9882 to 0.9916. The MLR models predicted perfectly (R2 = 0.866-0.951) for the %CDR responses using SPSS. ANN models successfully captured nonlinear relationships between formulation and response. Analysis of ML workflows indicated varying performance of algorithms depending on response; there was no one model that performed good across all responses. Traditional statistical and AI-based predictive methods complement each other. The integration of DoE with AI- and ML-based modelling offers a comprehensive tool for enhancing prediction accuracy and guiding formulation and optimization of pharmaceutical products.

articles.title: Polymorphic Transitions of Erlotinib Hydrochloride in PLGA Binary Mixtures: Influence of Polymer Functionality and Method of Crystallisation.
articles.abstract: Erlotinib hydrochloride (ERL), an oral tyrosine kinase inhibitor used in non-small cell lung cancer, is a classic example of drug polymorphism. However, the influence of crystallisation methods, PLGA, and thermal ageing on its polymorphic behaviour remains unexplored. This study investigated ERL polymorphism in binary mixtures prepared by blending, co-grinding, and solvent evaporation. PXRD revealed that blending and co-grinding retained ERL polymorphic form A, whereas solvent evaporation yielded form B in all binary mixtures. Thermal ageing has a significant effect on ERL crystallinity. DSC melting endotherms for form A are at 213.75 and 233.26°C, whereas form B shows a single melting endotherm at 231.96°C. MDSC efficiently captured the melt-mediated recrystallisation of form A. Further, ATR-FTIR with chemometric analysis differentiated the polymorphs into form A (anti) and form B (syn) conformations based on spectral regions at 3270 cm⁻1 (non-classical H-bonding) and 2540 cm⁻1 (N⁺-H···Cl⁻ interactions). SEM revealed plate-like and needle-like morphologies for forms A and B, respectively. Conversely, saturation solubility results reported higher solubility for the solvent-evaporated drug, due to its crystal morphology. Drug content by RP-HPLC (98-102% w/w) confirmed that the observed changes were solely physical transitions. Overall, this study provides insights into the development of ERL-loaded PLGA microspheres.

articles.title: PLGA-Phospholipid Hybrid Oleogel In Situ Forming Implant for Sustained 30-Day Co-Delivery of Dosnepezil and Memantine.
articles.abstract: The management of Alzheimer's disease requires continuous therapeutic intervention due to its progressive nature. Currently, the FDA has approved acetylcholinesterase inhibitors, NMDA receptor antagonists, and disease-modifying monoclonal antibodies for the treatment of Alzheimer's disease. This study aimed to develop a long-acting injectable formulation for symptomatic therapy. An in-situ gel formulation, DM00PG-M13, comprising Lipoid, PLGA (50:50), and sesame oil, was developed and loaded with memantine and donepezil for combination therapy. The optimized gel formulation demonstrated good uniformity with a pH of 7.80 ± 0.015. Rheological and syringeability studies showed a consistent viscosity in the range of 0.20-0.22 Pa·s and an injection force of 9.97 ± 0.29 N using a 22-G needle. In vitro drug release studies performed in phosphate-buffered saline (pH 7.4) demonstrated sustained drug release over one month, with cumulative releases of 82.58% for donepezil and 87.61% for memantine after 30 days.
