Furthermore, the release kinetics were best described by the Peppas-Sahlin model for donepezil and the Weibull-lag model for memantine. Ex vivo studies evaluating the optimized formulation injected into pig muscle tissue showed release profiles comparable to the in vitro release pattern, with approximately 20% release of donepezil and 26% release of memantine over 7 days, indicating sustained release behavior. Cytotoxicity studies using NIH/3T3 fibroblast cells confirmed the formulation's safety profile. Overall, these results suggest that the drug-loaded DM00PG-M13 formulation can be administered intramuscularly as a depot system for sustained drug release, potentially improving patient compliance.

articles.title: Hot-Stage Microscopy as a Quantitative Preformulation Tool for Assessing API Particle Dissolution in Molten Polymer Matrices.
articles.abstract: High-melting-point active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs) frequently undergo amorphization during hot-melt extrusion (HME) through progressive dissolution and incorporation in a softened polymer rather than by direct melting. The kinetics of this process are strongly influenced by particle size, yet rapid experimental methods for evaluating particle dissolution behaviour in the softened polymer prior to extrusion remain limited. In this work, a quantitative hot-stage microscopy (HSM)-based workflow combined with image analysis was developed to evaluate particle-size-dependent dissolution of a model high-melting-point API into softened Kollidon® VA 64 under predefined thermal conditions. The dissolved fraction of individual particle-size classes was quantified throughout the experiment to determine the particle-size range associated with complete and incomplete dissolution. Complete dissolution was consistently observed for particles smaller than approximately 15-20 μm, whereas particles exceeding approximately 40 μm exhibited a markedly increased probability of retaining residual drug particle under the applied conditions. Between these limits, the dissolved fraction decreased progressively with increasing particle size. Because the methodology evaluates particle dissolution under static thermal conditions, the identified particle-size limits should be regarded as conservative, formulation-specific estimates rather than universal HME processing limits. The proposed workflow transforms HSM from a primarily qualitative visualization technique into a quantitative preformulation screening tool that enables rapid evaluation of particle-size-related processing risks while requiring only minimal quantities of material.

articles.title: Understanding the High Pharmacokinetic Variability of 5-Aminosalicylic Acid Drug Products Using Compartmental, Semi-mechanistic, and Mechanistic Pharmacokinetic Models.
articles.abstract: 5-Aminosalicylic acid (5-ASA) is a cornerstone therapy for ulcerative colitis (UC), but its clinical performance is highly variable due to pH-dependent solubility, formulation design, and intestinal metabolism. Significant intersubject variability (ISV), particularly for modified-release drug products such as Lialda (> 75% variability in Cmax and > 50% in AUC) and Pentasa (> 30 to < 50% for Cmax and > 30% for AUC), limits predictable therapeutic outcomes and necessitates a better understanding using biopredictive tools. An empirical, semi-mechanistic, and mechanistic physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) model was developed using intravenous (IV) and oral data. In vitro dissolution profiles generated under different pH, molarity, and hydrodynamic conditions were fitted and integrated into the PBPK framework to establish biorelevant dissolution methods and predict the in vivo performance of Lialda 1200 mg and Pentasa 4000 mg. Nonlinearity was observed, with 2.7-7.8-fold increases in AUC due to N-acetyltransferase-1 (NAT1) saturation. Optimal predictivity was achieved at pH 7.0 (5 mM) for Lialda (%PE: 4.7% Cmax, 1.2% AUC) and pH 7.5 (25 mM) for Pentasa (%PE: 4.9% Cmax, 4.6% AUC). Variability was driven by NAT1 saturation, pH-dependent solubility/permeability, and formulation effects. PBPK simulations enabled the identification of formulation-specific biorelevant dissolution conditions. The model successfully described pharmacokinetic variability, including intra- and inter-subject differences.

articles.title: Study on the Mechanism of Sasanquasaponin in Inhibiting the Progression of Osteoarthritis via the MAPK and PI3K/AKT Pathways.
articles.abstract: Sasanquasaponin (SQS) exhibits anti-inflammatory and antioxidant effects, with unknown therapeutic effects in osteoarthritis (OA).This study was conducted to verify the effects of SQS and its molecular mechanism in OA.Specifically, flow cytometry was utilized to assess cell apoptosis, and ELISA was used for evaluating the levels of pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-6, IL-8, TNF-α) and matrix-degrading enzymes (MMP-3, MMP-13, ADAMTS-4, ADAMTS-5). The targeting effects of SQS on the MAPK and PI3K/AKT pathways were predicted using the molecular docking method.SQS rescued IL-1β-induced apoptosis in human chondrocytes (C-28/I2) in a concentration-dependent manner while suppressing the production of pro-inflammatory cytokines and matrix-degrading enzymes. Bioinformatics prediction identified reliable binding sites for SQS in key proteins of both the MAPK (p38, JNK) and PI3K/AKT (PI3K, AKT) signaling pathways. In IL 1β stimulated C 28/I2 cells, SQS suppressed the excessive activation of p38, JNK, PI3K, and AKT. Moreover, overexpression of these proteins reversed the protective effect of SQS against C-28/I2 apoptosis, as well as its inhibitory effect on the production of pro-inflammatory cytokines and matrix-degrading enzymes.Collectively, SQS alleviates OA inflammation and matrix degradation via inactivation of the MAPK and PI3K/AKT pathways.

articles.title: Rethinking Inhalation Risk Assessment: Integrating Respiratory Cell Models with Air-Liquid Interface Exposure?
articles.abstract: Air-liquid-interface (ALI) exposure systems, combined with respiratory cell models, have been increasingly used for the past decades to assess the hazard of substances and for drug safety and efficacy testing. Further, these are being used for exploring disease mechanisms. Currently, on a global scale, there is a critical mass of scientific researchers conducting such experiments and using the technologies for ALI exposure. The methodology is already paramount within the training of the next generation of researchers, due to the concomitant necessity to develop alternative, human relevant models for regulatory risk assessment and accelerating drug development. There are many different ALI respiratory cell models and exposure systems available, but there is a lack of widely accepted standard operating procedures and pre-validation efforts for increasing confidence and acceptance by different stakeholders. However, how do we get there? The herein commentary intends to discuss the current situation of ALI-based experimentation, as well as consider the future challenges that must be overcome to establish these next-level testing strategies to be accepted in the regulatory arena.

articles.title: Pesticide Residues in Common Vegetables: A Probabilistic Risk Assessment Using Monte Carlo Simulation for Adult and Child Consumers.
articles.abstract: This study investigates the presence of noxious pesticide residues in commonly consumed vegetables from Kerman Province, Iran, and evaluated the probabilistic dietary health risks for adult and child consumers using Monte Carlo simulation. Targeted samples were analyzed using a modified QuEChERS method coupled with LC-MS-MS and GC-MS-MS. The method demonstrates the linearity range of 0.015-0.50 mg kg-1 (R2 > 0.9975), recoveries of 81.2%-111.5%, limits of detection of 0.004-0.006 mg kg-1, limits of quantification of 0.015-0.020 mg kg-1 (RSD≤13%). The non-carcinogenic risks were assessed by calculating Hazard Quotients for adults and children. The results demonstrated that all mean and 95th percentile HQ values were substantially below the safety threshold of 1.0, indicating negligible non-carcinogenic health risks. Chlorpyrifos produced the highest HQ values among the investigated pesticides, whereas profenofos contributed the lowest dietary risk. Although children consistently exhibited higher HQ values than adults because of lower body weight and greater food intake relative to body mass, all estimated risks remained within acceptable safety limits. The acquired result represented current pesticide residue levels are unlikely to pose significant health risks. Nevertheless, continuous monitoring, implementation of integrated pest management strategies and periodic probabilistic risk assessments are recommended to ensure long-term consumer safety.

articles.title: Editorial: Special Issue Apoptosis Insights.
Development of a lateral flow assay as a point-of-care diagnostic device for the detection of poisoning with cholinesterase-inhibiting compounds.
articles.abstract: Organophosphorus (OP) nerve agent and pesticide exposure pose a threat to both the armed forces and civilians. To support clinical decision-making, erythrocyte acetylcholinesterase and plasma butyrylcholinesterase activity in whole blood can be evaluated. Currently, laboratory diagnosis is time-consuming and not broadly available. Thus, we developed in a proof-of-concept study a lateral flow assay for the rapid, on-site diagnosis of an OP poisoning. The lateral flow assay is based on the colorimetric Ellman reaction and detects total cholinesterase activity in whole blood through a clear color change at the test strip, allowing for visual evaluation. OP poisoning is indicated when no color change occurs on the absorbance pad of the test strip, while normal cholinesterase activity is indicated by a pronounced yellow color change. A parallel visual control strip serves as a reference; its yellow color intensity is calibrated to represent uninhibited cholinesterase activity, helping users interpret the results. Furthermore, the reproducibility and sensitivity of the lateral flow assay were assessed using the persistent organophosphate nerve agent VX and the organophosphate pesticide paraoxon-ethyl. The findings indicated high reproducibility and adequate sensitivity.

articles.title: Acute and sub-acute toxicity evaluation of rhamnolipid derived from Stutzerimonas stutzeri PS1 in Wistar rats.
articles.abstract: Rhamnolipid biosurfactants have gained attention due to their surface-active properties and applications in the pharmaceutical and food industries. However, toxicological profiling remains for their safe integration. This study assessed the purity of rhamnolipid by HPLC and evaluated its acute and sub-acute toxicity in Wistar rats. In the acute toxicity, a dose of 2000 mg/kg was administered, and animals were monitored for 14 days. In sub-acute toxicity study, rats received oral doses of 250, 500, and 1000 mg/kg for 28 days. Toxicity was assessed through clinical observation, hematological analysis, serum biochemistry, and histopathological examination of the liver and kidney. No mortality or abnormal signs were observed in any treated groups. The hematological parameters and serum biochemical markers (SGPT, SGOT, urea, and creatinine) showed no significant differences (p > 0.05) compared to the control group, indicating maintained hepatic and renal functions. Furthermore, histopathological analysis of liver and kidney sections revealed preserved cellular architecture with no evidence of inflammation, necrosis, or structural alterations across all doses. The No-Observed-Adverse-Effect Level (NOAEL) for hepatic and renal endpoints exceeded 1000 mg/kg/day. These findings suggest no hepatic or renal toxicity observed under tested conditions and support the suitability of this biosurfactant for pharmaceutical and biotechnological applications.

articles.title: Ocular irritation potential and selected regulatory labeling requirements of hair-styling pomades marketed in Brazil: A comparative assessment using Short Time Exposure test (OECD TG 491) and HET-CAM.
articles.abstract: In February 2023, during Brazilian Carnival, more than 700 cases of temporary blindness were reported after rain exposure, with affected individuals describing blurred vision, burning pain, and a film-like sensation over the eyes. Hairstyling pomades were implicated in these events, leading to a temporary ban on the commercialization of such cosmetics. Shortly after the mark re-entry of some brands in April 2023, 10 commercially available products were investigated by assessing their pH and evaluating their in vitro ocular irritation potential by Hen's Egg Test-Chorioallantoic Membrane (HET-CAM) and Short Time Exposure (STE) assays. One product lacked a warning regarding accidental eye exposure, and pH ranged from 2.6 to 7.6. Two formulations could not be evaluated by STE because suitable test preparations could not be obtained. Of the eight tested products, four were Category 1, three were No Prediction, and one was No Category. HET-CAM classified three products as severe irritants. HP-5 showed the strongest response, with 0.2 ± 5.0% cell viability at 5% in STE and a mean HET-CAM irritation score of 15.5 ± 2.1. These findings support complementary non-animal methods for post-market ocular hazard screening while emphasizing method-specific limitations.

articles.title: Retrospective (Q)SAR analysis of genotoxicity data from European pharmaceutical scientific advice and authorization procedures and performance improvements using structural alert and chemical subspace analyses, reliability filtering, and expert review.
articles.abstract: Drug development warrants a high number of animal studies, fostering the development of New Approach Methodologies (NAMs) to reduce, replace and refine animal studies (3Rs). As part of this effort, various (Q)SAR models have been developed, and many of these models were designed to predict genotoxicity. To retrospectively investigate the performance and regulatory applicability of available computational genotoxicity prediction models and to evaluate methods for improving prediction performances, a dataset was manually curated from proprietary and publicly available Austrian, French, and European regulatory pharmaceutical procedures. The collected experimental endpoints (Ames bacterial mutagenicity, in vitro mammalian cell genotoxicity, and in vivo genotoxicity) were then retrospectively analyzed with different available (Q)SAR prediction models. Model performance proved to be endpoint and model specific, with Ames test models routinely used in regulatory ICH M7 analyses showing better performances than in vitro mammalian cell and in vivo genotoxicity models. In many cases improvements of prediction performance were possible by applying structural alert analyses, chemical subspace analyses, prediction reliability filtering, and expert review. Still, in vitro mammalian cell genotoxicity and in vivo genotoxicity models need further refinement before they can be applied in regulatory decision making.

articles.title: Nano-Emulsification and Soft Gel Encapsulation to Improve the Delivery of Anti-Diabetic Drug Ertugliflozin-L-Pyroglutamic Acid via SNEDDS: An In Vitro Assessment using RP-HPLC.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: This study aim to develop and evaluate a novel soft gelatin capsule formulation of Ertugliflozin-L-Pyroglutamic Acid (ERT) using a self-nanoemulsifying drug delivery system (SNEDDS) to enhance its solubility, physicochemical stability, and in vitro drug dissolution relative to the commercial Steglatro® tablets. SIGNIFICANCE: Poor aqueous solubility and limited dissolution behavior are two major challenges that hinder the therapeutic performance of many antidiabetic drugs. Herein, for the first time we formulated ERT as a SNEDDS-based soft gelatin capsule, providing a promising strategy for enhancing oral drug delivery system that manages Type 2 diabetes more efficiently. METHODS: ERT was encapsulated in a SNEDDS formulation matrix of Labrasol® (surfactant), PEG-200 (co-surfactant) and cardamom oil in an optimized ratio. Stability studies were conducted across varied pH ranges, mimicking the gastrointestinal tract environment. Advanced characterization techniques, including AFM, DLS, Zetasizer and FT-IR spectroscopy confirmed consistent particle size and desirable morphological attributes. RP-HPLC as per ICH guidelines evaluated dissolution profile and assay recovery against the commercial Steglatro® tablets. RESULTS: The optimized ERT-SNEDDS soft gel formulation demonstrated high stability across various pH conditions, with an assay recovery of 98.78 ± 0.04%. The complete dissolution profile (CDP) at three different pH values (0.1 N HCl, pH 4.5 and pH 6.8 buffers) showed significantly superior in vitro drug release compared to established Steglatro® tablet. CONCLUSION: The developed SNEDDS based soft gelatin capsule demonstrated favorable physicochemical characteristics and rapid in vitro dissolution of ERT, supporting its potential as an alternative lipid-based oral dosage form to the marketed tablet.

articles.title: AQbD-Driven Green RP-HPLC Method Development and Validation for Simultaneous Quantification of Apremilast and Quercetin in Nanostructured Lipid Carriers.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To develop and validate a green RP-HPLC method, guided by Analytical Quality by Design (AQbD), for the simultaneous quantification of apremilast and quercetin in nanostructured lipid carriers. SIGNIFICANCE: Accurate simultaneous estimation of apremilast and quercetin in lipid-based nanoformulations remains limited. An AQbD-guided method with a focus on environmental sustainability offers improved robustness, reproducibility and suitability for formulation development and quality control. METHODS: Chromatographic conditions were optimized using an AQbD framework based on a Box-Behnken Design. The RP-HPLC method was validated according to ICH guidelines for specificity, linearity, accuracy, precision, robustness, limit of detection, and limit of quantification. The validated method was applied to determine entrapment efficiency, drug loading, and in vitro drug release from nanostructured lipid carriers. Method greenness was evaluated using AGREE, BAGI and ComplexGAPI assessment tools. RESULTS: Quercetin and apremilast were detected at retention times of approximately 8.32 and 10.95 min, respectively, with satisfactory chromatographic resolution. The method demonstrated excellent linearity within the concentration range of 10-50 µg/mL, with R2 values of 0.9992 for quercetin and 0.9999 for apremilast. Precision was high with %RSD values below 1%. The optimized nanostructured lipid carriers showed entrapment efficiencies of 69.87 ± 2.41% for quercetin and 60.12 ± 2.85% for apremilast, along with sustained drug release over 24 h. Greenness assessment indicated good adherence to green analytical chemistry principles. CONCLUSIONS: The AQbD-driven green RP-HPLC method proved sensitive, robust and validated. It is suitable for the simultaneous quantification of apremilast and quercetin in nanostructured lipid carriers and related pharmaceutical applications.

articles.title: Drug-drug interaction between vonoprazan and imatinib: in vivo pharmacokinetics and in vitro metabolic inhibition characterization.
articles.abstract: 1. Vonoprazan and imatinib may be co-prescribed in patients with acid-related disorders, but the pharmacokinetic consequences of this combination remain unclear.2. We evaluated the effects of vonoprazan on imatinib pharmacokinetics in rats and compared metabolic inhibition in human and rat liver microsomes.3. Rats (n = 6/group) received vehicle or vonoprazan (5.0 or 20.0 mg/kg) orally for 7 days, followed by imatinib (30.0 mg/kg). Imatinib and N-desmethyl imatinib were quantified by UPLC-MS/MS. Inhibition kinetics were examined in human (HLM) and rat liver microsomes (RLM).4. Imatinib AUC(0-t) increased by 37.2% and 63.7% at 5.0 and 20.0 mg/kg vonoprazan, respectively; the increase was significant at 20.0 mg/kg (p < 0.05). N-desmethyl imatinib AUC(0-t) decreased by 37.4% and 69.4% (both p < 0.05). IC50 values were 17.52 μM in HLM and 9.35 μM in RLM. Inhibition patterns were consistent with competitive inhibition in HLM and mixed-type inhibition in RLM, with apparent Ki values of 38.97 and 37.17 μM, respectively.5. Vonoprazan increased imatinib exposure in rats and inhibited microsomal metabolism. Species differences and uncertainty in the kinetic estimates limit quantitative extrapolation; clinical interaction studies are needed.

articles.title: Adverse events during cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator modulator therapy in children with cystic fibrosis: an observational study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Cystic fibrosis (CF) is a life-limiting genetic disease caused by pathogenic variants in the CFTR gene. CFTR modulators (CFTRms) have substantially improved clinical outcomes, but real-world data on symptoms reported during therapy in pediatric populations remain limited. This study evaluated the frequency and distribution of adverse events (AEs) reported during 12 months of CFTR modulator (CFTRm) therapy in pediatric and adolescent patients with CF. METHODS: This prospective, dual-center observational study conducted in Poland included 74 patients aged 2-18 years receiving lumacaftor/ivacaftor (LI), tezacaftor/ivacaftor (TI), or elexacaftor/tezacaftor/ivacaftor (ETI). Reported symptoms were monitored prospectively and categorized as respiratory, nervous system, gastrointestinal, or other AEs. AE profiles according to patient characteristics and CFTRm regimen were explored. RESULTS: At least one adverse event (AE) was reported by 90.5% of patients during follow-up. AE involving the respiratory and nervous systems were the most frequently reported, occurring in 79.7% and 75.7% of patients, respectively. Most AEs were intermittent and rarely required treatment interruption (n = 3). Lung function and nutritional status improved significantly during therapy. The overall frequency of reported AEs did not differ depending on the FEV1 or BMI outcomes. Nervous system AEs were more frequently reported among patients aged > 10 years and among patients receiving ETI compared with LI. CONCLUSIONS: CFTRm therapy was generally well tolerated in this pediatric CF cohort. Reported AEs were common but predominantly intermittent and rarely led to treatment interruption. Systematic monitoring remains important, particularly for neurological symptoms, to better characterize tolerability of CFTRm therapy.
